data.title: My Family and the Flood
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者一家在德州瓜达卢佩河边度假时遭遇洪水袭击的经历。四岁的Rosemary最先醒来，告诉父亲Lance屋顶有异响。不久后，大家被雷雨惊醒，发现河水迅速上涨，已逼近他们建在桩上的房子甲板。洪水迅速逼近，最终冲破玻璃门涌入屋内。在混乱中，一家人忙着保护孩子并试图寻找逃生方法，但水位持续上升，房屋开始变形，情况十分危急。最终，他们在洪水中挣扎，等待可能的救援。

44576352.article_content:
Rosemary, the four-year-old, woke up first. She told my brother-in-law, Lance, that there was something on the roof.
Seven of us were at my family’s river house on the Guadalupe, between Ingram and Hunt, for the Fourth. Our little stretch of river is wide, green, cool, deep, and slow. It is some of the best swimming anywhere and one of the most beautiful spots in Texas, as far as I’m concerned. I’ve spent many peaceful afternoons there, floating and staring up at the cypress trees that tower over the water. The house, a one-story cabin on stilts about fifty yards from the river up our steeply sloped yard, was built right after the
1987 flood
that devastated this region, killing ten teenagers. Concrete pillars put our family’s place a few feet above what officials consider a one-hundred-year floodplain. More than once I’d tried to imagine the waters rising that high, but it seemed impossible.
We’d had pizza for dinner and spent that Thursday evening playing hide-and-seek with Rosemary, a rambunctious, expressive, willful little girl with blond hair and blue eyes who can speak Spanish and calls me Tío, and her baby brother, my twenty-month-old nephew, Clay, a towhead who’d just learned to say the words “boo” and “yellow.” After the kids went to sleep, a few of us played charades until about 9:30 p.m., when we all said goodnight and went to bed.
I woke around 3 a.m. to the sound of thunder and rain. My only thought was, I hope it stops so I can go on an early-morning run. Shortly before 4:30, I would later learn, Rosemary climbed down from the top bunk of the kids’ bedroom and went to get her father. Lance stepped out of bed to see what was causing all the pounding and creaking. I stirred at about that time, too, and heard what I figured were the kids running around the house, excited by the storm. Or maybe the winds were causing tree branches to slam against the metal roof. I heard Lance call out for his wife, my sister Alissa, and I got out of bed and walked into the main living area. I saw my dad, Clint, who is 73, and Lance peering out through the sliding-glass doors that led to the back deck. The house was dark, but Dad held a flashlight, aiming it into the night.
“What’s going on?” I asked.
“We’re in trouble,” he said. “Big trouble.”
I looked past them. The river was as high as the deck, twenty feet above the ground.
We had spent so many hours on that porch looking out over the yard and to the river below. Now the water splashed against the bottom of its railing. The gravity of our situation didn’t sink in right away, but the facts were clear: We were surrounded by fast-moving floodwater, and we had no way of escaping to higher ground.
Rosemary and Clay Parisher in Austin this summer.
Courtesy of Darhys Rodriguez
I ran back to my bedroom and woke up my husband, Patrick. Soon all of us—Dad, Lance, Alissa, Rosemary, Clay, Patrick, and me—came together in the living area. Clay flashed his adorable smirk at Patrick, eager to play. We talked through our options. Getting onto the roof was impossible. We had no ladder, and the eaves were about eight feet above the deck. Patrick weighed whether we could all climb through a window into the live oak whose branches were near the back of the house, then realized it wasn’t reachable. Lance called 911, but the dispatcher said he didn’t know when anyone could get to us.
I tried to imagine a scenario that would turn out okay. I imagined rescuers in a yellow raft emerging from the darkness. I imagined being stuck in the house for hours or days, grateful for all the groceries we’d brought for the weekend. I imagined my husband pointing out that the floodwaters were starting to recede. I imagined the relief I would feel when I realized he was right.
The river rose. Within a minute or two it was about a foot high against the glass door. We got dressed, put on shoes, and packed bags so we could be ready to leave in case someone, anyone, miraculously arrived.
The family river house, near Ingram, in 2021.
Courtesy of Aaron Parsley
As we reassembled in the kitchen, the vinyl flooring under our feet started to bubble, and then water began to pool. My dad walked into his bedroom and saw the carpet floating off the floor. The river’s musty scent permeated the house, mixed with what smelled like freshly chopped wood. My sister sat Rosemary and Clay on the kitchen island countertop. We discussed whether we could get them higher, maybe even on top of the cabinets in the small space below the ceiling. Then the roof over the porch crashed down and we heard glass shatter in my father’s room, just off the kitchen.
Rosemary asked, “Why did the window break?”
Clay started to cry.
When the sliding-glass door opened and water poured in, Lance ran to it, shoved it closed, and held it shut. The pendant lamps began to swing wildly over the kitchen counter. The house was shifting. It lurched sharply, and we all struggled to stay on our feet. It felt like walking down the aisle of a plane during

data.title: Running a million-board chess MMO in a single process
data.author: isaiahwp
data.article_summary:
《Running a million-board chess MMO in a single process》一文介绍了名为"One Million Chessboards"的在线国际象棋游戏。该游戏由1000x1000的棋盘组成，棋子可以在不同棋盘间移动，所有玩家的动作是实时同步的，没有回合限制。游戏在一个单一进程中运行，作者通过使用Golang和Protobufs等技术，优化了性能，确保了客户端能快速响应。游戏初期吸引了超过15万玩家，产生了数百万次移动和查询。

游戏设计强调最小化带宽使用，并通过简单架构实现高效性能。服务器使用Golang编写，主要组件包括棋盘、客户端管理器、小地图聚合器和磁盘状态处理器。棋盘状态以8000x8000的数组存储，每个连接用户有一个goroutine负责处理数据传输和压缩。游戏还具有小地图、缩放等功能，并通过Nginx反向代理和Cloudflare进行部署。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"One Million Chessboards"项目的技术实现、优化方案及相关问题的讨论

不同观点：
• 关于"Rooklyn"和"Queens"是否为不可摧毁结构的讨论：
  - butlike指出根据规则，棋子无法跨棋盘捕获其他棋子，因此这些结构在特定规则下是不可摧毁的。
  
• 关于带宽和缓存优化的讨论：
  - mannyv建议通过Cloudflare缓存静态数据，以节省带宽，类似于视频帧差异技术，仅在关键帧保存整个棋盘状态。
  
• 关于单线程优化和高效内存使用的讨论：
  - dangoodmanUT分享了类似项目UltimateArcade的经验，强调单线程优化和无锁编程的高效性。
  
• 关于计算资源效率和优化的讨论：
  - commandlinefan认为在当前"云"环境下，重新关注效率和实际成本的关系非常重要，期待优化编程的复兴。
  
• 关于自动化和机器人参与的讨论：
  - omoikane提到是否有人为自动化（机器人）参与项目，并指出机器人可能解决冷启动问题，但也可能影响用户体验。
  
• 关于技术实现细节和Golang使用的讨论：
  - dvoros表示对项目技术栈和实现方式的赞赏，并计划借鉴一些想法用于自己的Golang项目。
  
• 关于冲突处理和回滚机制的讨论：
  - CJefferson质疑是否可以通过简单地重置用户状态来解决冲突，而非复杂的回滚操作，并提到可能存在的竞争条件。

补充讨论：
• 关于项目视觉设计和灵感来源的评论：
  - sehansen赞赏项目的状态框设计，认为其受StarCraft启发。
  
• 关于游戏规则修改的建议：
  - heroku建议修改规则，允许玩家在棋盘之间移动并仅能捕获进入棋盘的棋子。
  
• 关于项目背后动机的讨论：
  - topato对项目创作者的动机和时间安排表示好奇，质疑其是否为大公司工程师的个人项目。

争议焦点：
• 项目中规则的设定和优化方案的选择，如是否引入机器人、冲突处理方式及回滚机制的复杂性。

44541088.article_content:
Running a million-board chess MMO in a single process
How One Million Chessboards works
Jun 24, 2025
One Million Chessboards
is a 1000x1000 grid of chess boards. Moving a piece moves it for everyone, instantly. There are no turns, and pieces can move between boards.
Loading...
making some moves
In the 10 days after launch, over 150,000 players made over 15,000,000 moves and hundreds of millions of queries. The game runs out of a single process that I didn’t touch over those 10 days
1
.
1
Once activity died down I bounced the server, reset the game, and started
experimenting with rule tweaks.
Making this project taught me a lot. It’s the first time I’ve used protobufs or
golang
, the first time I’ve measured nanoseconds, and my first time writing
rollback netcode
.
Let me tell you about it.
read the code here
play the game here
this essay is also a video on my youtube channel, if that’s more your style
Basics
Here’s a quick overview of the site before we jump into the details.
Rules
Pieces can move between boards
- I wanted one global game, not a million simultaneous ones
2
.
2
This seemed to really disappoint actual chess players. I’m a little surprised
by that - I don’t think that a million simultaneous games would lead to
particularly interesting gameplay! - but maybe I’m wrong.
Loading...
moving between boards
This meant that sharding the boards over many processes wasn’t free because those processes would need to communicate.
There are
no turns
. I didn’t think asking the whole internet to take turns would work well. And I thought real-time chess would be fun.
Loading...
taking a king
This meant that speed mattered; I needed to make sure that clients could make moves fast.
I prevented pieces from
capturing
pieces on other boards
. This was originally to prevent a queen from immediately capturing the king on the board above or below her, but ended up producing fun emergent gameplay as people (ab)used it to make indestructible structures like Rooklyn and Queens.
Rooklyn, Queens, and a digital monument
This rule was interesting, but it locked up the game. After activity died down I tried relaxing the restriction to only apply to unmoved pieces. I think this was a mistake - the original version was likely better.
The site has some other fun features. You can click on pieces to see how many times they’ve moved or captured a piece, there’s a minimap that lets you quickly jump to anywhere on the grid, and you can zoom out to see an overview of a larger chunk of the board at once.
Loading...
15 moves and 14 captures for this queen - not bad!
System Design Goals
Last year I built a surprisingly popular site called
One Million Checkboxes
. I learned a lot while
scaling it to handle load
; those learnings directly lead to my design goals.
I wanted to
minimize bandwidth
since it was my one unbounded cost. It’s very stressful going to bed not knowing what you’ll owe when you wake up.
I chose to run in a
single process
- partially because it was easier than sharding, partially because it was a fun challenge, but primarily because I was still smarting from a Hacker News
comment
(correctly!) pointing out that could have run One Million Checkboxes in a single process (instead of the 8 vms and a database).
This irked me because they were *right*
I aimed to be
bottlenecked by syscalls or message serialization
overhead. Both of those operations parallelize well, which means I could scale vertically to address them if I needed to.
And finally, I wanted to be
surprisingly fast
. My biggest gripe with most One Million Checkboxes clones is that they have too many loading spinners (One Million Checkboxes sent all its data to all clients which - when it wasn’t crashing - kept things snappy). I couldn’t ship
all
my data to clients this time so they’d have to load data occasionally - but I wanted to be faster than anyone would reasonably expect.
Basic Architecture
The server runs in a single golang process. It sits behind an nginx reverse proxy that sits behind cloudflare. An auxiliary VM handles metrics collection and stores backups of the game state. The frontend is written in React.
metrics are handled via vector and loki
The server has 4 core components - the board, client manager, minimap aggregator, and board to disk handler.
yes, they're all arrays, what of it
The board
is a dense 8000x8000 array of uint64s representing pieces.
The client manager
tracks the location of each client
The minimap aggregator
summarizes where pieces are
The board to disk handler
duplicates our board state and regularly serializes that state to disk
The server also has a set of goroutines (go’s lightweight threads) for every connected user. These goroutines track per-client data, accept moves, and are responsible for compressing and sending data to each client:
I regret calling this 'client' since it sounds like I'm referring to the website
The client has a few more responsibilities like assigning you a starting location next to another active pla

data.title: Unlike ChatGPT, Anthropic has doubled down on Artifacts
data.author: bewal416
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Dropbox在2010年代通过云计算功能实现强大网络效应的成功，并将其与AI市场中的类似现象进行比较。文章首先回顾了Dropbox通过免费层和简便的文件共享吸引用户，然后分析了OpenAI和Anthropic在AI领域的不同策略。OpenAI推出了定制GPT功能，但之后似乎放弃了这一方向。而Anthropic则通过其“Artifacts”功能让用户无需编码即可创建AI驱动的应用程序，并解决了API认证和费用问题，实现了用户增长和经济效益的双赢。文章认为Anthropic的策略不仅技术上令人印象深刻，而且商业上也非常聪明，使Claude成为AI时代的Dropbox，为市场提供了实际价值。最后，文章还展望了未来通过与支付系统合作，进一步简化应用货币化的可能性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕不同AI工具（如Claude、OpenAI的Custom GPTs、Artifacts等）的实用性、成本和用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对Claude订阅和成本的看法**：
  - [graphememes] 认为Claude的API超时增加和使用成本过高，转而使用更便宜且性能相当的其他模型，因此取消了订阅。
  - [zebix86] 认为Claude在聊天界面上表现优异，可能更多针对普通用户而非开发工具整体产品线。

• **对OpenAI放弃Custom GPTs的看法**：
  - [esafak] 对OpenAI在Spring ‘24更新后基本放弃Custom GPTs表示不解，认为这应是OpenAI解决的问题，而不是用户的。
  - [PeterStuer] 猜测Custom GPTs只是营销策略，用来免费推广并获取商业发展线索，但效果不如预期。
  - [MagicMoonlight] 认为Custom GPTs只是不可见的提示词包装，没有实质区别，不值得关注。

• **对Artifacts功能的看法**：
  - [oidar] 对Artifacts的功能持怀疑态度，认为其在小规模代码时有用，但代码量大时变得笨重，无法单独编辑一行。
  - [danieltanfh95] 认为Artifacts能有效减少Token使用，提升对话轮次，并减少AI心理问题，如HALO式暴走或上下文中毒。
  - [jasonjmcghee] 曾经因为Artifacts的多种问题（如错误更新代码、无效编辑等）而关闭该功能，认为不值得。
  - [oc1] 对Anthropic的Artifacts产品策略表示怀疑，认为其重复OpenAI在GPT Marketplace上的错误，导致用户决策疲劳和失望。

补充讨论：
• **对Claude Code和Artifacts市场前景的看法**：
  - [bl4kers] 对将Claude比作Dropbox表示疑问，暗示可能并非褒奖。
  - [Shindi] 认为Claude在构建和分享上的易用性优于Custom GPTs，并提到人们在GPT商店 hackathon上对定制GPT感到失望。
  - [yshunnar] 赞同Claude的新战略，认为认证和支付是用户锁定的关键功能。
  - [mxwsn] 对是否有出色的Artifacts表示好奇，希望看到实例。

争议焦点：
• **Custom GPTs和Artifacts的实用性和市场价值**：一方认为这些功能简化了用户体验并提供更多选择，另一方则认为这些功能笨重、不实用，且导致用户决策疲劳和失望。

44577171.article_content:
Back in high school, I remember receiving an email for a study guide from a friend. Instead of the PDF coming attached to the email, it was a link to a site called Dropbox.
Upon opening the file, you create an account. From there you’re introduced to a feature stack that went well beyond any typical PDF: shared collaboration, comments, version history… the benefits of cloud computing- all within the familiarity of a PDF!
Dropbox achieved strong
network effects
in the 2010s due to generous free tiers, easy file sharing, and one-click account creation. Last year, I wrote
a blog post
on network effects, guessing if (and how) they would be brought into the AI market. In the post, I argued two points:
OpenAI began flirting with network-driven growth by introducing Custom GPTs in November 2023, and even more so when making them accessible to free users in May 2024.
AI companies might not
need
network effects to succeed, as user-generated content might not be what incrementally improves these tools (rather, artificial content, better memory, & great UX)
The rest of this post will be a follow-up of #1. In short, OpenAI appears to have
basically abandoned Custom GPTs
since their Spring ‘24 update, and I’m a bit stumped as to why. Sure, engagement might have been low, or a desire to shift the product team to other features like Canvas, improved memory, Deep Research, and Apple Intelligence integration. But, one would think that the allure of network effects would drive any consumer tech startup to continue toying with the idea!
Meanwhile, Anthropic’s Claude has been quietly pursuing a more powerful way for users to build for other users. Two months after the Custom GPT release,
Claude announced Artifacts
, allowing users to create single-page HTML apps, among other things. Artifacts became a hit within the tech community, potentially mainstreaming “vibe coding” for the first time. Writer Simon Willison (or dare I say,
fellow
writer)
became quite obsessed with Artifacts
over the past year.
Unlike ChatGPT, Anthropic has doubled down on Artifacts, making it more reliable and accessible to users. And in June 2025, they went
big
. Anthropic announced that Artifacts can now become AI-powered:
Today, we’re introducing […] the ability to embed AI capabilities directly into your creations—transforming artifacts into interactive, AI-powered apps.
Artifacts turn anyone into an app creator—no coding needed. Just tell Claude your idea to instantly create shareable apps, tools, and games.
Here’s their announcement video of a drum-making kit. You’ll see that the drum kit users can “Describe [a] beat” in the Claude-powered search bar.
It’s pretty cool! But, wouldn’t the creator need to worry about API authentication? Then, users abusing their credits? Or entering abusive prompts that would flag their account? It appears not.
Here’s
what makes this announcement newsworthy:
Claude [turns] artifacts into AI-powered apps, where the economics actually work for sharing.
When someone uses your Claude-powered app:
They authenticate with their existing Claude account
Their API usage counts against
their
subscription, not yours
You pay nothing for their usage
No one needs to manage API keys
While technically impressive, I find this to be an oddly brilliant business strategy for the prosperity of the Claude Chatbot- especially when Ben Thompson himself
categorized it as non-focus for Anthropic
. As an Artifact creator, I can infinitely extend the power of my Artifact at zero risk; all my users need is a Claude account.
Claude is the Dropbox of the Gen AI era.
It’s providing real value to the market for the return of user acquisition and CLV- something that its competitors are incapable or avoidant of doing.
Coding is the easiest part
One week before this Artifacts update, the father of vibe coding himself, Andrej Karpathy, went on stage to deliver a talk about the continued shifts in software development.
At the end
, Andrej shared that while the “coding” step of app development is easier than ever, getting to that last mile of production deployment still exists:
While Claude Artifacts are still in this “toyish” phase of single-page web apps, you can’t help but be in awe at all the things it solved on this slide: LLM API keys, Deployments, and Authentication. And no one needs to pay an Enterprise license to make it happen.
After Karpathy’s talk, I spent most of my time thinking about “Payments”. How hard would it be for a PayPal or Link to partner with a v0 or Lovable? I could see a future where vibe coded apps can be locked behind a paywall with one click- making apps as easy to monetize as a Gumroad product. I suppose pricing tiers would complicate things, but hey, there’s nothing code can’t solve!
Perhaps I’m romanticizing the tech ecosystem- Google can do everything on Andrej’s slide. Maybe that’s what
Sundar will task Varun and Douglas
to do.

data.title: Thunderbird: Fluent Windows 11 Design
data.author: skipnup
data.article_summary: FluentBird是一款为Mozilla Thunderbird设计的userChrome.css主题，实现了Windows 11的Fluent Design和Mica透明材质效果。该主题支持亮色和暗色模式，增强了Thunderbird在Windows 11系统上的视觉体验。最新版本0.1.5修复了暗模式下的信封图形问题，并解决了卡片视图中主题冲突等问题。安装需启用userChrome.css，并将相关文件复制到Thunderbird的配置目录中。由于是测试版，仍存在一些未完成的样式和已知问题，如无法完全主题化所有元素。该项目基于MIT许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Thunderbird的界面设计及其自定义主题功能

不同观点：
• paintbox认为搜索栏占用太多空间，影响界面美观和空间利用，并希望借鉴浏览器设计演变的经验来改进。
• ttoinou则认为应用的默认设计往往是最适合长时间使用和减少眼部疲劳的，尽管不美观但有效，并以自己多年使用Thunderbird的经验为例。
• ape4澄清了对"fluent"设计名称的误解，指出它实际上是指微软的一种设计风格，而非编程中的流畅接口。
• huhtenberg批评设计中有太多空白空间，信息密度低，但认为这种设计可能会在设计社区中受欢迎。
• accrual欣赏"Fluent"设计的透明效果，并希望通过这种设计带回早期玻璃效果的美学，同时对搜索栏的位置有所保留。
• bluedino对现代屏幕只能显示少量邮件列表表示不满，怀念早期邮件客户端的设计。
• MortyWaves担心使用CSS而非操作系统原生实现可能导致问题，强调了原生实现的重要性。
• tummler对Thunderbird的整体性能提出批评，尤其是邮件数据下载问题，尽管喜欢主题设计。
• Calzifer提供了有关如何在Thunderbird中绕过Shadow DOM限制的技术细节，分享了个人经验和解决方案。
• AdmiralAsshat提到仍在使用一个多年未更新的Monterail主题，并对该主题的开发停滞表示遗憾。
• thesuitonym和guluarte都不理解为什么有人想把Thunderbird设计得像Outlook，表现出对这种设计趋势的困惑。
• hk1337惊讶Thunderbird仍在更新，并对跨平台使用Windows 11设计表示好奇。
• kookamamie担心Thunderbird是否仍然存在可能损坏邮件的bug，对软件稳定性提出质疑。
• neogodless希望看到更多有关多文件夹管理的界面截图，关注设计的实际应用效果。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到Thunderbird的界面空间利用、信息密度、主题美观与实用性的平衡、Shadow DOM的技术问题以及对软件稳定性和性能的关注。
• 争议的焦点包括搜索栏的位置和空间使用、默认设计与自定义主题的优劣、以及设计是否应借鉴其他应用（如Outlook）等问题。
• 部分用户关注设计的实际效果和长期使用体验，而其他用户则更在意技术实现和软件功能。

FluentBird
FluentBird is a userChrome.css theme for Mozilla Thunderbird, that implemenets Windows 11 Fluent Design and Mica transparency materials.
Created by Danny King -
www.dannyking.co.uk
Released under the MIT License
Features
Implements Fluent Design styling in Thunderbird
Supports both dark and light modes (system theme)
Enhances and highlights Mica transparency on Windows 11 systems
This will likely be the last beta release, unless more issues are raised, with 1.0 release to occur alongside Thunderbird 141.
0.1.5 Release Notes
Improves the "no messages" envolope graphic in dark mode.
Fixes the subject line clashing with the star / tags icons in card view.
0.1.4 Release Notes
Adds Fluent icons and correct button styling for the "Reply List" button
Fixes button hover colour in Dark Mode
Fixes subject line colour on card view in Dark Mode
Credits
FluentBird uses Fluent Design icons provided by Microsoft, licensed under the MIT License.
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.
Setup Instructions
Enable userChrome.css
Open Thunderbird
Go to
Settings
>
General
Click
Config Editor…
under
Advanced
Search for
toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets
Set it to
true
Restart Thunderbird
Enable the Mica flags in Thunderbird’s (Firefox-based) advanced configuration:
Open Thunderbird
Go to
Settings
>
General
Scroll down and click
Config Editor…
under
Advanced
In the search bar, type
widget.windows.mica
and set it to
true
Search for
widget.windows.mica.popups
and set it to
2
Make sure no other theme is selected in Thunderbird settings.
Do not
select Light, Dark, or any theme from the Thunderbird extension store.
The theme must be set to "System Theme" or simply unselected.
Copy the included files to the
chrome
folder in your Thunderbird profile directory:
Click on Help > Troubleshooting information
Scroll down to "Profile Folder" under "Application Basics" and click "Open Folder"
Create a new folder named
chrome
inside your profile folder, if it does not already exist
Place the userChrome.css file and all folders into the 'chrome' directory
Restart Thunderbird.
Known Issues
This is a beta release. Expect bugs and incomplete styling.
Untested on Mac and Linux (should work, but without Mica).
Report issues via the GitHub repository.
Also, note that some areas of ThunderBird are rendered outside of the influence of userChrome.css in a "Shadow DOM" - as such, it is not possible to fully theme all elements of Thunderbird.
The mail section is fully themed, as is the general window chrome. The Contacts, Calendar, Tasks and Chat functions have limited themeing in some areas.
It isn't possible to style the new message / reply message window, or any other pop-up windows.
As they are entirely contained within a Shadow DOM, it is also not possible to theme the settings areas.
Questions?
Check the GitHub repo or open an issue there. Enjoy!

data.title: MARS.EXE → COM (2021)
data.author: reconnecting
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了1993年由Tim J. Clarke编写的火星景观渲染器代码，对其进行了详细分析和研究。原始的MARS.EXE文件大小为5649字节，作者对其进行反汇编、重写和优化，将其压缩至1517字节。文章提供了原始代码和优化后的MARS.COM代码，并详细说明了转换过程和算法。此外，文章还介绍了如何使用DEBUG工具提取和解析二进制数据，同时提醒操作时需谨慎。作者尝试联系原作者Tim未果，希望他能看到此文并取得联系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于经典DOS时代3D演示程序MARS.EXE及其技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• **对MARS.EXE的赞美与怀旧**：
  - [skrebbel] 和 [reconnecting] 提到MARS.EXE作为经典DOS演示程序，在1993年时带来了极大的震撼，尤其是其实时渲染的分形地形效果在当时的硬件条件下显得不可思议。
  - [Andrew_nenakhov] 表示对MARS.EXE这一名字久违的怀念。

• **技术细节与实现方式**：
  - [reconnecting] 引用了pouet.net上的描述，指出MARS.EXE是由Elixir的Tim Clarke在1993年编写，并且由于其出色的表现，Tim被邀请到Lunacorp工作。同时建议在DOS模式下运行该程序以避免崩溃。
  - [phkahler] 提到自己曾在学校用Turbo Pascal在486电脑上实现过类似的程序。

• **对微优化与现代技术结合的讨论**：
  - [londons_explore] 认为这种微优化虽然能带来巨大的性能提升，但非常耗费人力，并提出如果AI能够实现这种优化，可能会带来软件性能的革命。
  - [flockonus] 希望看到通过WASM等技术在网页上运行类似演示。

• **硬件性能与现代环境的比较**：
  - [amiga386] 质疑在现代多GHz机器上通过DOSBox模拟运行MARS.EXE与原生386硬件上的表现差异。
  - [baal80spam] 对比了MARS.EXE和现代Windows 11上的记事本程序，指出后者占用的磁盘空间显著增加。

• **技术探索与实践**：
  - [nickdothutton] 回忆自己在1988年购买了一本关于分形的Springer Verlag书籍，并尝试在z80家用电脑上复现分形图形，但速度非常慢。
  - [tetris11] 提到寻找可以在网页上使用的DOSBox来加载ASM，但未找到合适的工具。

• **算法与技术影响的争议**：
  - [kragen] 提出MARS.EXE是否预见了Comanche游戏中的Voxel Space 3D渲染算法的问题，暗示可能存在技术上的关联或启发。

• **其他技术发现**：
  - [shmerl] 提到在二进制编辑器中修改颜色调色板的经历，发现改变一个字节就能从红色切换到绿色或蓝色。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提及MARS.EXE的技术实现及其在DOS时代的突破性，但也有人关注如何在现代技术环境下复现或改进这种经典演示程序，并探讨了微优化和AI技术的结合潜力。
• 争议焦点可能在于MARS.EXE是否对后来的3D渲染算法（如Voxel Space）产生了影响，这一问题引发了对技术传承和创新的讨论。

44541662.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了1993年由Tim J. Clarke编写的火星景观渲染器代码，对其进行了详细分析和研究。原始的MARS.EXE文件大小为5649字节，作者对其进行反汇编、重写和优化，将其压缩至1517字节。文章提供了原始代码和优化后的MARS.COM代码，并详细说明了转换过程和算法。此外，文章还介绍了如何使用DEBUG工具提取和解析二进制数据，同时提醒操作时需谨慎。作者尝试联系原作者Tim未果，希望他能看到此文并取得联系。

不同观点：
• Alex3917质疑为何使用传统的ELO评分系统，而不是使用不假设结果分布的ELO变体，如"whole history rating"。
• slybot指出Bradley-Terry和ELO是两种完全不同的排名系统，前者使用比率基础，而后者使用逻辑评分函数。他还提到ELO变体如MLE、贝叶斯ELO和随机化ELO等，试图改进ELO在不同应用场景中的问题。
• fulmicoton认为在处理"文档在位置i优于位置j"的信息时，应考虑排名位置的影响，并提到LambdaMART在这方面表现更好。
• ashwindharne分享了他们内部使用现成模型进行重新排序和过滤的经验，强调该方法有效但成本高且速度慢。
• pbhjpbhj提出文档级别的比较可能过于粗略，建议考虑在段落级别进行比较，以提高检索效果，特别是在涉及复杂文档分析的领域。
• Neywiny介绍了一种使用2AFC排序替代ELO的方法，认为这种方法有明确的终点，并提供了代码和会议演示链接。
• patrickhogan1关注在网络搜索中使用ELO风格的截止机制，以避免混合高质量和低质量的来源，从而提高答案的可信度。
• rjmunro认为ELO风格的排名适用于Uber rides和餐厅评价，通过相对比较而不是绝对评分来提高评分的准确性。
• seanhunter分享了一个关于ELO名称由来的有趣事实，指出ELO是以发明者的名字命名的，而不是缩写。
• mkaszkowiak关注模型的多语言支持和多语言基准测试。
• etk934讨论了使用MSE训练的reranker是否比使用InfoNCE的更好，以及在RAG应用中使用reranker分数的阈值是否更有用。
• rahulnair23提到他们在ACL 2024上发表的关于LLM排名的论文，提供了HuggingFace空间的示例链接。

补充讨论：
• 不同评论中提到了多种ELO变体和替代系统，如whole history rating、Bradley-Terry、MLE、贝叶斯ELO、随机化ELO和LambdaMART，讨论了它们在不同应用场景中的优缺点。
• 评论中还涉及了文档级别和段落级别比较的优劣，特别是在信息检索和复杂文档分析中的应用。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于如何在网络搜索中混合高质量和低质量来源的问题，以及使用ELO风格的截止机制来提高答案的可信度。
• 评论中还分享了一些相关的代码和论文链接，提供了进一步阅读和研究的资源。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否应使用传统的ELO系统还是其变体，以及在不同应用场景中哪种排名系统更为合适。例如，slybot和Alex3917对ELO和Bradley-Terry的适用性提出了不同看法。

data.title: Pgactive: Postgres active-active replication extension
data.author: ForHackernews
data.article_summary: **pgactive** 是一个 PostgreSQL 扩展，用于实现 **active-active（双活）数据库复制。这种复制方式允许多个数据库实例同时接受写入操作，并相互复制数据，适用于多区域高可用性、减少写入延迟、蓝绿部署等场景。与传统的 active-standby 模式不同，active-active 没有单一的数据来源，因此需要处理数据冲突和复制延迟等问题。该项目利用 PostgreSQL 的逻辑复制功能，并通过扩展增强其对双活复制的支持。项目基于 Apache-2.0 许可证，目前有 426 个星标和 19 个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres的分布式扩展、多主复制（active-active replication）以及相关工具的分析和争议

不同观点：
• [eatonphil] 提供了BDR和pglogical的发展历史，指出多个版本的演变过程，包括开源和闭源版本的更替，最终被EnterpriseDB（EDB）收购并发布了PGD v6。他强调了不同版本之间的技术演进。
• [zknill] 分析了pgactive的实现，指出它基于Postgres的逻辑复制，采用最后写入为准（last-write-wins）的冲突解决机制，并将冲突记录在特殊表格中供后续处理。
• [nico] 提出了一个关于“本地可写读副本”的需求，即副本可以从主数据库接收数据，但不将本地更改反馈给主数据库。他分享了一种基于快照的解决方案，但指出该方案在索引构建时存在问题。
• [ahachete] 对“冲突解决”提出批评，认为它实际上是在丢失已提交的数据，并建议要么避免跨节点的写冲突，要么使用如Yugabyte这样的分布式数据库。
• [everfrustrated] 质疑AWS参与pgactive项目的动机，指出AWS的RDS和Aurora使用的是不同的复制技术，因此他认为pgactive不太可能被AWS产品采用。
• [iotapi322] 基于实际操作经验，表达了对pgactive插件的不信任，认为它可能会导致生产环境的不稳定。
• [mosselman] 寻求一种简化的方式来设置高可用的Postgres集群，包括自动故障转移和节点恢复，但对现有的如patroni和etcd的方案感到复杂。
• [ltbarcly3] 警告除非非常了解技术细节，否则不应使用这类active-active复制方案，认为它不能提升性能或扩展性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于pgactive的冲突解决机制和整体可靠性。一些用户认为它可能导致数据丢失或不一致，而另一些用户则关注其在实际生产环境中的适用性。
• 关于高可用Postgres集群的设置，存在多种工具和方案（如patroni、repmgr、pgool），但它们的复杂性让部分用户感到困扰，寻求更简化的解决方案。
• 对AWS参与pgactive项目的动机存在质疑，认为其现有技术栈与pgactive的应用场景不符。

Active-active Replication Extension for PostgreSQL (pgactive)
pgactive is a PostgreSQL replication extension for creating an active-active database.
Documentation
Overview
Security
License
Overview
Database replication is a method that copies changes between databases instances, and is a key component for use cases like high availability, reducing latency between an application and its source data, moving data between systems such as production and test, infrastructure migration, and others. Relational databases such as PostgreSQL typically support an active-standby model of replication, where one database instance accepts changes and makes them available to one or more read-only databases. Because changes in an active-standby cluster can only occur on a single instance, it’s more straightforward to build applications that work with this deployment topology because there is a single source of truth that contains all of the latest changes.
Sometimes it’s preferable to have a database cluster that uses an active-active replication topology, where it’s possible to write data on multiple instances in the same cluster. In an asynchronous active-active replication deployment, multiple databases in a cluster can accept changes and replicate them to other databases, but this means the database cluster doesn’t have a single source of truth. Use cases for this include running a Multi-Region high availability database cluster, reducing write latency between applications and databases, performing blue/green updates of applications, and migrating data between systems that must both be writable. Applications that work with active-active database clusters must be designed to handle situations that occur in this deployment topology, including conflicting changes, replication lag, and the lack of certain convenient database features such as incremental integer sequences.
A fundamental component of active-active replication is logical replication. Logical replication uses a data format that allows external systems to interpret changes before applying them to a target database. This lets the target system perform additional actions, such as detecting and resolving write conflicts or converting the statement into something that is supported in the target database software. PostgreSQL added native support for logical replication in PostgreSQL 10 in 2017, but still requires additional features to fully support an active-active replication topology. PostgreSQL’s design makes it possible to build the necessary components for supporting active-active replication in an extension while the development community continues to add it into the upstream project.

• [eatonphil] 提供了BDR和pglogical的发展历史，指出多个版本的演变过程，包括开源和闭源版本的更替，最终被EnterpriseDB（EDB）收购并发布了PGD v6。他强调了不同版本之间的技术演进。
• [zknill] 分析了pgactive的实现，指出它基于Postgres的逻辑复制，采用最后写入为准（last-write-wins）的冲突解决机制，并将冲突记录在特殊表格中供后续处理。
• [nico] 提出了一个关于“本地可写读副本”的需求，即副本可以从主数据库接收数据，但不将本地更改反馈给主数据库。他分享了一种基于快照的解决方案，但指出该方案在索引构建时存在问题。
• [ahachete] 对“冲突解决”提出批评，认为它实际上是在丢失已提交的数据，并建议要么避免跨节点的写冲突，要么使用如Yugabyte这样的分布式数据库。
• [everfrustrated] 质疑AWS参与pgactive项目的动机，指出AWS的RDS和Aurora使用的是不同的复制技术，因此他认为pgactive不太可能被AWS产品采用。
• [iotapi322] 基于实际操作经验，表达了对pgactive插件的不信任，认为它可能会导致生产环境的不稳定。
• [mosselman] 寻求一种简化的方式来设置高可用的Postgres集群，包括自动故障转移和节点恢复，但对现有的如patroni和etcd的方案感到复杂。
• [ltbarcly3] 警告除非非常了解技术细节，否则不应使用这类active-active复制方案，认为它不能提升性能或扩展性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于pgactive的冲突解决机制和整体可靠性。一些用户认为它可能导致数据丢失或不一致，而另一些用户则关注其在实际生产环境中的适用性。
• 关于高可用Postgres集群的设置，存在多种工具和方案（如patroni、repmgr、pgool），但它们的复杂性让部分用户感到困扰，寻求更简化的解决方案。
• 对AWS参与pgactive项目的动机存在质疑，认为其现有技术栈与pgactive的应用场景不符。

不同观点：

• **alach11**：认为每发表一篇关于监控CoT的论文，都会降低该技术对强大AI模型的有效性，因为模型可能被训练得不显示其思维过程。
• **sabakhoj**：质疑CoT监控的长期可靠性，指出已有研究表明模型在某些主题上不会揭示其思维过程。同时，分享了一个帮助阅读论文的工具项目。
• **barbazoo**：引用了AI2027的预测，未来LLM性能将通过非人类语言思考的方式提升，并质疑该预测的可信度。
• **msp26**：质疑普通用户是否能够监控他们所使用的模型的CoT，还是这些信息将继续被隐藏。
• **Mountain_Skies**：引用《2001太空漫游》中的HAL，警示AI学会欺骗的问题，并表达对AI发展方向的担忧。
• **tsunamifury**：认为自由文本CoT是噪声较大的代理，提出了一个名为Micro-Beam的轻量级替代方案，通过生成不同策略束并进行评分来实现监控，并提供审计跟踪。
• **bossyTeacher**：质疑可见的"思维"是否是唯一的思维类型，并提出模型可能在展示一种思维的同时进行不同的行动。
• **zer00eyzs**：基于对AI系统的深入研究，认为这些系统不具备动态性、无法根据经验修改或反思，主张应专注于这些系统擅长的领域，而不是试图使其成为AGI。
• **academic_84572**：分享了一篇关于解决回形针最大化问题的论文，询问他人对该研究方向的看法，特别是在实用性方面。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于CoT监控的有效性和未来发展。一部分人认为CoT监控不可靠，未来模型可能不再以人类可读形式输出推理；另一部分人则提出了改进监控的替代方案，如Micro-Beam。
• 讨论还涉及AI模型欺骗问题以及对模型内部状态进行解释的必要性。
• 有人对AI发展的硬件限制和效率问题提出了担忧，认为现有技术路径可能无法持续。

整体来看，讨论围绕CoT监控的可行性、局限性以及未来可能的替代方案展开，反映了研究者对AI安全和可解释性的多角度思考。

Abstract:
AI systems that "think" in human language offer a unique opportunity for AI safety: we can monitor their chains of thought (CoT) for the intent to misbehave. Like all other known AI oversight methods, CoT monitoring is imperfect and allows some misbehavior to go unnoticed. Nevertheless, it shows promise and we recommend further research into CoT monitorability and investment in CoT monitoring alongside existing safety methods. Because CoT monitorability may be fragile, we recommend that frontier model developers consider the impact of development decisions on CoT monitorability.

data.title: Altermagnets: The first new type of magnet in nearly a century
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了捷克物理学家Libor Šmejkal受艺术家M. C. Escher作品启发，预测了一种新型磁体——“交替磁体”（altermagnet）的存在。传统上，我们只知道两种磁体：铁磁体和反铁磁体。Šmejkal通过研究反铁磁体中的异常霍尔效应，意识到需要超越原有的磁性模型。他受到Escher作品《骑士》中对称图案的启发，发展出新的数学方法，从而预测了交替磁体的存在。2022年，他的理论得到了证实，科学家发现了实际的交替磁体例子，并探索其在技术中的应用，包括可能用于制造更快、更节能、更小的计算机设备。这一发现拓展了我们对磁性的理解，为材料科学和计算技术带来了新的可能性。

44583171.article_content:
Bekologic
Libor Šmejkal has a fondness for the artwork of M. C. Escher, whose work was often inspired by mathematics. One of Šmejkal’s favourite pieces is
Horseman
, a striking picture that features an elaborate, tessellating series of mounted figures. Strangely enough, it was this piece that inspired him to predict the existence of an entirely new kind of magnetism.
We have known of
magnets
for millennia. Today, they are at the heart of a raft of modern technologies, from electric generators and smartphones to loudspeakers and hospital scanners. And yet for 100 years, we have been missing something about them. We always assumed there were only two types. It was Šmejkal’s art-inspired insights that finally gave the lie to that in 2022.
Fast-forward to today, and we know that what Šmejkal called “altermagnets” aren’t just an idea. We have discovered real examples and are working out how to make this new kind of material in practical and useful ways. There is even a possibility that these magnets could help us build a completely new kind of computer. “Altermagnets could actually have all the functionalities of current devices, but much faster, with less energy consumption, and smaller,” says Šmejkal.
Read more
How to fix computing's AI energy problem: run everything backwards
To understand magnetism and why it is so important, we need to start with the electrons that whizz around in
atoms
. Each of these particles has an intrinsic quantum property called spin. This isn’t quite like anything in the everyday world, but you can imagine it as a tiny spinning top that can rotate in two directions, which scientists label “up” or “down”.
Electrons like to orbit their atoms in pairs, one spin-up, one spin-down, so the spins cancel out. But that isn’t always possible, as an electron sometimes ends up alone. With nothing to cancel it out, the unpaired electron gives the atom what is known as a magnetic moment: like spin, it can either be up or down, and it governs the atom’s magnetism. If you have enough atoms with magnetic moments pointing in the same direction, they create a strong, directional magnetic field. This is called ferromagnetism. It is a phenomenon that even the ancient Greeks knew about – they found rocks that attracted iron nails or filings to them – and it is also what is going on inside the magnets many of us have stuck to our fridges.
Subscriber-only newsletter
Sign up to Lost in Space-Time
Untangle mind-bending physics, maths and the weirdness of reality with our monthly, special-guest-written newsletter.
Sign up to newsletter
Ferromagnets are easy to spot because they attract or repel other magnetic materials, like nickel or cobalt. But there is another, more subtle kind of magnetism that wasn’t discovered until the 1930s. Antiferromagnets also have magnetic arrows, but this time they point in alternating directions – picture a line of arrows going up, down, up, down and so on. The result is a magnetic stalemate, a solid with magnetic order on the atomic level, but no unified, detectable magnetism on the scale of ordinary objects.
The mental model of imagining tiny arrows pointing up and down inside magnets was invented by physicist Louis Néel, who theorised the first antiferromagnets – which were experimentally confirmed in the decades following – and who won a share of the 1970 Nobel prize in physics.
Magnetic symmetry
That’s how things have stood for nearly 100 years: two types of magnetism, nice and neat. It was 2018 when
Šmejkal
, who is now based at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz in Germany, began to suspect there might be
more to the picture
. At the time, he was a young PhD student in Prague, Czech Republic, studying a strange phenomenon sometimes seen in antiferromagnets called the anomalous Hall effect. Šmejkal’s breakthrough was to realise that this effect and similar arcane magnetism puzzles couldn’t be explained with the model that Néel had developed – he needed to go beyond it.
This is where Escher’s 1946
horsemen artwork
came in. The riders in the image slot together in alternating colours with an elaborate, beautiful symmetry. Take one of the lighter figures, flip it, shift it sideways a jot and change its colour, and you match one of the darker riders. As he mused on this, Šmejkal realised there was an alternative mathematical method for describing this symmetry operation. “I realised that you can actually define this operation, this changing of colour or orientation, in another way,” he says.
And here’s the thing:
understanding symmetry
has always been crucial in physics, and this is particularly true in materials science, where the intricate relationships between different kinds of atoms are best described in that language. Indeed, Néel’s way of thinking about atoms’ magnetic moments has symmetry at its core. But by using his new mathematics as a framework, Šmejkal began to extend Néel’s model, firstly by thinking in three dimensions instead of two and secondly by including a

Escher作品启发，预测了一种新型磁体——“交替磁体”（altermagnet）的存在。传统上，我们只知道两种磁体：铁磁体和反铁磁体。Šmejkal通过研究反铁磁体中的异常霍尔效应，意识到需要超越原有的磁性模型。他受到Escher作品《骑士》中对称图案的启发，发展出新的数学方法，从而预测了交替磁体的存在。2022年，他的理论得到了证实，科学家发现了实际的交替磁体例子，并探索其在技术中的应用，包括可能用于制造更快、更节能、更小的计算机设备。这一发现拓展了我们对磁性的理解，为材料科学和计算技术带来了新的可能性。

A view of the village of Sambuca di Sicilia, Italy.  Photograph: Simone Padovani/Awakening/Alamy
Frustrated with my life back in the US, I was captivated by the idea of a new home – and new life – for less than the price of an espresso. So I travelled to Italy to find out whether it was too good to be true
By
Lauren Markham
Tue 8 Jul 2025 00.00 EDT
Last modified on Thu 10 Jul 2025 05.28 EDT
Share
I
f you could move anywhere, where would it be? This used to be a question I’d ask myself or others at dinner parties, but two years ago, as new parents facing the unsustainable costs of Bay Area life and the looming threat of middle-age atrophy, my husband, Ben, and I took to the internet in earnest with the notion of reinventing our lives somewhere new.
We were, of course, part of a widespread trend: seeking adventure and greener pastures elsewhere in the era of globalisation. Even so, the notion felt thrilling. Where would we go? Our search had some parameters: affordability, a natural landscape (I dreamed of cicadas, cypress trees), a place with a language we either already spoke or could learn easily enough so that we could contribute to the community. We’d spent our careers working in schools and nonprofits with young immigrants, and, however different it might look in a new country, we had no intention of leaving a life of service behind. Above all, though, what we wanted was an environment in which we could spend a lot of time writing and afford to do it. But Ben had another non-negotiable of his own: proximity to surfing. This annoyed me, as it significantly limited our search, but I supposed it was reasonable enough to design a dream life according to one’s actual dreams.
“There’s surfing in Sardinia,” he said.
We’d heard about the “€1 house” programme in which poor, depopulating towns put their abandoned or unused buildings up for sale. The programme, I soon learned, was actually a loose collection of schemes that economically struggling towns used to lure outside investment and new residents. The campaigns seemed to me to have been largely successful – some towns had sold all their listed properties. I pored over dozens of news articles that had served as €1 house promotion over the years. By attracting international buyers to a house that “costs less than a cup of coffee”, as one piece put it, some of Italy’s most remote towns now had new life circulating through them. Many local officials had come to see €1 house experiments as their potential salvation.
What was the catch? It seemed most municipalities required you to renovate the house within a couple of years of its purchase, and due to high levels of interest, the houses often went to auction, ultimately selling for much more than a single euro. But what we wondered about were the ethical considerations – the classic tensions of gentrification. What would it mean just to buy our way into a foreign place where we had no connections and try to set up a home there?
Still, we kept looking. There is a town in northern Sardinia called Sedini that was, according to Liliana Forina, a woman I got in touch with online, about to launch a €1 house initiative of its own. A stylish woman in her 60s from Milan, she had recently moved to Sedini from the mainland. The town wasn’t far from the beach and, judging by the pictures and Forina’s descriptions, seemed beautiful.
I arranged a meeting with her over Zoom. She appeared on-screen from her office, a Sardinian valley stretching behind her. A few years ago, she explained, she and her new husband began scouring Italy for the perfect place to live. Each weekend, they would visit a new region, feeling out the vibe in remote villages and golden-lit coastal towns speckled with beaches, in each place trying to imagine a life. It was relatively easy to cross options off their list: this town was too expensive; this one too was full of tourists; this one lacked trees. They wanted easy access to basic services such as a hospital, a pharmacy, a police station. They also wanted a view. But above all, they were looking for what Forina called their
dolce vita
, their sweet life. Eventually, they found it in Sedini, this breezy, hilltop town in northern Sardinia where the bells of several churches rang at noon, and, from a distance, the white-stone houses appeared stacked like antique toys on a rickety shelf. A local estate agent had found them a three-storey house right in the historic town centre with a view of the great green valley below. The house was livable but rather run-down and not to Forina’s taste, so the couple got to work renovating it, adding an upstairs terrace, exposing old beams, bringing antique tiles to a new gleam and knocking down walls to allow in more light.
Their dream life was indeed becoming a reality. Mostly. As beautiful as their home was, Forina noted early on that many of the other houses in Sedini were in a state of complete dilapidation. This left the otherwise picturesque old-world town with a

data.title: Artisanal handcrafted Git repositories
data.author: drewsberry
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何手动创建Git仓库，而不用常见的Git命令，借此加深对Git内部工作机制的理解。作者首先批评了现代Git使用中缺乏精心维护的现象，并提出通过手动方式感受Git设计的简洁与优雅。文章详细描述了手动初始化Git仓库的步骤，包括创建必要的目录和文件结构，如`.git`文件夹及其子目录，配置文件和`HEAD`文件。接着解释了Git的对象存储机制，强调了Git通过内容寻址存储数据的方式，即基于数据本身而非外部文件名或键进行管理。文章通过具体示例展示了如何手动创建提交，并解释了SHA-1哈希在Git中的作用。最终，作者希望通过这种手动方式让读者更好地理解Git的内部设计和其优雅之处。

Back to blog
July 16, 2025
•
24 min read
Artisanal Handcrafted Git Repositories
Table of Contents
There’s no love and care put into crafting our git repositories nowadays.
Let’s change that.
I’m going to talk about how to handmake your git repositories without using these silly git commands.
You might also learn a bit more about how git works under the hood during the process, or whatever.
If you’re so inclined, you might also take it as an opportunity to appreciate how the power of git comes not from the complexity of its code but from the simplicity and elegance of its design. I mean, if that’s your thing.
Git refers to the user-friendly commands as “porcelain” and to the internals as “plumbing”, so you can think of this as an introductory lesson in git plumbing. In fact, git has “plumbing” commands which we’re not even using, so this is more like an introductory course in git fluid dynamics. In other words, it’s pretty silly.
#
Pre-requisites
I’m going to assume you are familiar with git and are comfortable in a shell environment, otherwise this probably won’t make much sense to you.
#
Let’s get started
The first thing we’d do normally is run
git init
, but where’s the care and attention in that? We’re going to do it the old-fashioned way, like the pilgrims of yore would’ve done.
Terminal window
1
$
mkdir
artisanal-git
2
$
cd
artisanal-git
3
4
# This is where git stores all the information for a repository, from branches to
5
# commits to objects.
6
$
mkdir
.git
7
8
# Git expects these folders to exist, but we don't need to add anything into them yet.
9
$
mkdir
-p
.git/hooks
.git/info
.git/objects/info
.git/objects/pack
.git/refs/heads
.git/refs/remotes
.git/refs/tags
.git/logs
10
11
# This is just a standard repo-specific config file – these are the default values on my
12
# machine.
13
$
cat
<<
EOF
>
.git/config
14
[core]
15
repositoryformatversion = 0
16
filemode = true
17
bare = false
18
logallrefupdates = true
19
ignorecase = true
20
precomposeunicode = true
21
EOF
Now we only have to add one more file before we’ve got a valid git repository, and that’s the
HEAD
. You might’ve come across this before –
HEAD
just means “what is your repository pointing to right now?”. It’s a text file and it’s either got a reference in (the normal state of a repository) or just a plain commit hash – this is what’s referred to as a “detached head” (sounds painful, I know).
We’re going to point git to our default branch, called
main
.
Terminal window
1
$
echo
"ref: refs/heads/main"
>
.git/HEAD
You might be thinking – wait a minute, where is this
main

Before we start hand-crafting our commits, we need to spend a bit of time refining our craftwork by studying the lore.

Git needs to store lots of things. If you create a commit in git, git then needs to store everything about the commit itself, including the commit description, which files it includes, who committed it, the timestamp, and the contents of the files.

44586064.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何手动创建Git仓库，而不用常见的Git命令，借此加深对Git内部工作机制的理解。作者首先批评了现代Git使用中缺乏精心维护的现象，并提出通过手动方式感受Git设计的简洁与优雅。文章详细描述了手动初始化Git仓库的步骤，包括创建必要的目录和文件结构，如`.git`文件夹及其子目录，配置文件和`HEAD`文件。接着解释了Git的对象存储机制，强调了Git通过内容寻址存储数据的方式，即基于数据本身而非外部文件名或键进行管理。文章通过具体示例展示了如何手动创建提交，并解释了SHA-1哈希在Git中的作用。最终，作者希望通过这种手动方式让读者更好地理解Git的内部设计和其优雅之处。

data.title: Show HN: 0xDEAD//TYPE – A fast-paced typing shooter with retro vibes
data.author: theden
data.article_summary: 《0xDEAD//TYPE》是一款由TheDen开发的简单反应游戏。玩家需按下与屏幕上显示相对应的按键来摧毁方块，并通过W/S或方向键上下移动。按下空格键可以获得短暂的无敌状态。游戏中还有特殊的“0”方块，需特别留意。玩家可以点击任意位置启用浏览器中的声音以获得完整体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某款打字游戏的机制、操作方式及用户体验的评价与建议

不同观点：
• MontyCarloHall认为应通过增加得分和惩罚机制来解决游戏中乱按键轻松获胜的问题，并指出游戏在某一关卡后的难度变得过高，建议改进可通行路径的生成方式。
• LearnYouALisp支持引入更复杂的生成算法，如包含噪音的“单词路径”或类似马尔科夫链的生成方式，以增加游戏的挑战性和趣味性。
• hamdouni提到自己使用Vimium插件导致游戏不成功，暗示游戏与某些浏览器插件存在兼容性问题。
• mnaimd赞赏游戏的趣味性，但建议增加Vim风格的j/k移动模式，并提出对字母V和U难以区分的视觉问题。
• mylesp反映其使用的分体键盘无法在游戏中正常工作，而标准键盘可以，质疑游戏是否使用了特定类型的键盘输入。
• Muvasa和lysium都提到自己受Vim的键位绑定影响，习惯用j/k来移动，而不是游戏默认的w/s键位。
• camtarn和to11mtm都不喜欢使用w/s键来移动，认为这与打字操作不协调，建议改为其他更符合用户习惯的操作方式，如箭头键或Vim风格的操作。
• iamwil提出一种模态切换的建议，类似于Vim的`esc`和`i`，以区分移动和打字两种操作模式。
• Zenst认为游戏的横向滚动不太适合，建议增加可选的纵向滚动模式或提供更多自定义选项。
• type_enthusiast反思自己的打字技能受限于常用的肌肉记忆，虽然游戏增加了难度，但不确定这是否是坏事。
• korrectional欣赏游戏中的不可破坏块，认为它们增加了挑战性，无需修改。
• strictnein称赞游戏并提到其类似于C64上的老式打字游戏，认可其他玩家关于惩罚乱按键的建议。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的键位设置是争议焦点之一，尤其是w/s与j/k的对立，以及是否应允许自定义键位。
• 增加难度和惩罚机制被一些玩家认为是解决乱按键问题的有效方法。
• 不同玩家对路径生成方式和滚动方向有不同偏好，显示出对游戏自定义选项的需求。
• 游戏的键盘兼容性问题也引起了一些玩家的关注。

data.title: A recap on May/June stability at Neon
data.author: nikita
data.article_summary: 本文回顾了2025年5月和6月Neon平台因AI代理引发的一系列稳定性问题。5月，由于数据库创建激增，Neon平台在美国区域达到了Kubernetes集群的扩展上限，导致事故频发。主要原因是我们在实施名为“Cells”的水平扩展架构前，数据库创建量超预期。为应对问题，我们调整了配置并加速了Cells的部署，现已在新区域成功应用Cells架构，缓解了压力。6月，控制平面数据库因分支创建量暴增50倍再次出现扩展问题，导致元数据处理困难和性能下降。我们正优化Postgres查询以避免类似问题，并计划改进以帮助客户预防类似故障。

44586427.article_content:
Engineering
Jul 16, 2025
A Recap on May/June Stability
Details of incidents and what we did to prevent more in the future
Starting in May, we had a series of feature launches with agentic AI partners that gained far more momentum than we predicted. In two short timespans, the rate of new database creation increased more than 5x, and the rate of branch creation increased more than 50x. While we were humbled by the uptick, the significant burst in operational load caused a lot of strain in the Neon platform,
manifesting as more incidents over the course of the two months than the entire year before.
We understand that databases are some of the most critical operational infrastructure for our customers, and stability is paramount.
The problem should have never happened and I am embarrassed for this incident and sorry to cause pain to our customers and our team.
In this blog post, we explain the underlying causes for these incidents and what we are doing to avoid these categories of incidents in the future.
May: Capacity Handling and “Cells”
May incidents were caused by us hitting a scaling limit around the number of active databases in US regions before our solution (Cells) was ready. Every active database on Neon is a running pod in a Kubernetes cluster. Our testing of Kubernetes showed service degradation beyond 10,000 concurrent databases. Among multiple issues discovered in testing, we approached the
EKS etcd memory limit of 8GB
and pod start time fell below our targets. In addition, in our us-east-1 cluster, our network configuration limited us to
~12,000 concurrently active databases
.
In January 2025, we forecasted that we would hit these limits by the end of the year. While we believe that we can iterate on our Kubernetes configuration to vertically scale higher, there are many reliability and resiliency advantages to a horizontally-scaled architecture.
As a result, we started working on a horizontally-scalable architecture called “Cells” where each region can have multiple Neon deployments.
This was a major project requiring substantial changes to the Terraform code that provisions regions. We planned this project, and estimated a delivery date of Q2 2025 – this would mean a launch 6 months before it was needed, and so this seemed sufficient.
However, starting in May agentic AI platforms drove sustained 5x increase in database creation in US regions and our projections were wrong.
Agentic AI platforms accelerated the DB creation rate in certain regions well beyond what we projected
We made various configuration changes to keep our oversized regions functional: tuning networking, reducing our usage of the Kubernetes API to avoid EKS (Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service) rate limits, scaling up our control plane databases, and shedding load where possible. Each of these changes bought us time to complete the Cells project, but also increased risk of failure and the amount of customer impact when failures occurred — resulting in the incidents you experienced.
Since these events, we’ve successfully shipped Cells in each of our busy regions and routed most new project creation to the new Cells. We also have the ability to deploy additional Cells quickly as load demands.
Moving new project creation to new Cells prevents old Cells from continuing to grow and helps relieve pressure on Kubernetes and the control plane. If you create a new project in AWS US today, you may notice a c-2 identifier in the URL – this indicates the Cell your project is in.
June: Metadata Handling
Database operations incidents in June were caused by scaling issues with our control plane database as a result of a 50x increase in
database branch
creation. A branch in Neon is a cheap operation – there’s no data copy – but that makes it fast and easy to create thousands of them. In agentic workloads, customers often use branches as “savepoints” to restore app state as their agent iterates on a codebase.
Daily branches created each day by developers (blue) vs agents (yellow)
All of this metadata is stored in Postgres instances backing our control plane. While the core of our service was more than able to sustain this sudden change in load, these shifts in metadata volume and structure had several knock-on effects:
Billing and consumption calculations became more expensive, consuming more CPU
Some queries switched to different Postgres execution plans, and tables became more dependent on aggressive vacuuming
In several cases, customer-impacting issues were caused by control plane queries that went from taking a few hundred milliseconds to over a minute. We have alerting on slow and degrading query performance – but in this case, the query plan switched quickly, introducing service degradation without warning.
While we are a Postgres company, we experienced classic Postgres failure modes with increased load: query plan drift and slow vacuum. This is humbling, and will inform our roadmap to help our customers avoid the same.

data.author: cbzbc
data.article_summary: Intel在俄勒冈州的业务收缩 unprecedented，自20世纪70年代以来，该公司在俄勒冈州的扩展一直呈上升趋势，成为该州最大企业雇主和经济引擎。然而，由于技术和财务危机，Intel自去年开始大幅削减员工，特别是技术岗位，目前已削减5,400个俄勒冈岗位，预计还将继续裁员。这导致当地高薪岗位流失，可能迫使许多员工离开俄勒冈州。Intel的困境也引发了对该州知识经济未来的担忧，尽管有专家认为现有的人才储备可能缓冲影响。Intel新任CEO表示，裁员是恢复公司竞争力的必要措施，并强调俄勒冈州仍将是其全球运营的核心。然而，对俄勒冈州而言，大公司意味着高税收和经济稳定，因此Intel的缩减对该州经济可能产生显著负面影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Intel的内部文化、管理决策、创新失败以及对员工和社区的影响

不同观点：
• **Intel内部文化问题**：
   - [lordnacho] 指出Intel的内部文化存在问题，管理层不清楚下属团队的工作内容和目的，存在大量无效的会议和咖啡社交。
   - [Pearledlang] 提到类似情况，非技术人员被大量雇佣，而有能力的人却被视为麻烦制造者并被排挤。
   - [burner420042] 认为Intel前管理层缺乏对技术的热情和创新精神，感觉他们的行为和视角不对劲。

• **错失创新机会**：
   - [lordnacho] 提到Intel错失了在GPU和移动芯片领域发展的机会，尽管这些领域与他们的现有业务相近。
   - [someonehere] 认为Intel过于自满，忽视了创新信号，例如Apple转向自研芯片就是警示。

• **管理决策失误**：
   - [evereverever] 批评Intel将合同工作外包给印度的InfoSys，导致本地开发和设计公司失去机会。
   - [declan_roberts] 讨论了远程工作和生活成本的权衡，指出离开高薪科技中心可能会导致难以在当地找到类似高薪工作。
   - [MinimalAction] 提到Intel项目团队组成不合理，员工的技能与项目需求不匹配。

• **地理和文化的选择影响**：
   - [bcatanzaro] 提出Intel如果将工程团队留在硅谷，可能会因为高住房成本的压力而保持更高的创新动力，而不是在俄勒冈州的孤立文化中停滞不前。

• **经济和政策影响**：
   - [fsckboy] 认为企业在业务收缩时进行缩减是正常的，而不是前所未有的。
   - [freefaler] 指出Andy Grove离开后，Intel失去了方向。
   - [mensetmanusman] 预测中国将在2027年接管半导体制造的主导地位。
   - [hunglee2] 认为CHIPS法案和美国政府政策的变化对Intel产生了负面影响，导致国内制造计划受挫。

• **团队规模和管理问题**：
   - [0manrho] 提到科技公司普遍存在过度依赖团队规模来衡量成功的问题，Intel尤其如此，导致官僚主义扼杀创新。
   - [JKCalhoun] 将Intel的裁员和回填行为比喻为“企业暴食症”，指出这种不稳定的就业状况。

补充讨论：
• Intel的内部管理和文化被广泛认为是其创新失败和市场失利的主要原因之一。
• 员工对管理层的决策感到失望，许多人在裁员后面临就业困境。
• 政策变化和全球竞争对Intel的业务产生了深远影响，尤其是在半导体制造领域。

争议焦点：
• Intel是否因为地理选择（硅谷 vs 俄勒冈）而失去了创新动力。
• 政府政策变化和全球竞争对Intel的影响程度，特别是CHIPS法案和中美关系。

通过这些讨论，可以看出Intel面临的挑战是多方面的，既有内部管理和文化问题，也有外部经济和政策因素的影响。

44585755.article_content:
Intel’s retreat is unlike anything it’s done before in Oregon
Updated:
Jul. 15, 2025, 1:10 p.m.
|
Published:
Jul. 15, 2025, 5:55 a.m.
Intel's campus in Aloha was the company's first Oregon site -- and its first manufacturing facility outside California -- when it opened in the 1970s.
Mike Rogoway/The Oregonian
By
Mike Rogoway | The Oregonian/OregonLive
Over the five decades Intel has operated in Oregon, its local footprint had moved in just one direction: Upward.
From a single factory in Aloha that opened in 1976, the chipmaker grew into the state’s largest corporate employer and one of Oregon’s primary economic engines. Intel spent billions of dollars every year to equip its Hillsboro factories and brought top scientists from around the globe to Oregon to develop the world’s most advanced computer chips.
Intel would sometimes cut jobs during fallow periods but it backfilled them almost immediately. As recently as last year, the company was touting a massive expansion that could add thousands more Oregon jobs.
Instead, Intel has embarked on an unprecedented and sustained campaign to shrink its business in response to a series of technical and financial crises. And Oregon is bearing the brunt of the pain, with Intel making the deepest cuts to its local workforce ever.
Intel has eliminated at least 5,400 Oregon jobs since August –
including 2,400 layoffs in just the past week
. The company’s local workforce appears to have fallen under 18,000, the lowest point in more than a decade. Sources inside Intel say there are more cuts to come in the weeks ahead.
Many of those who lost their jobs worked in technical fields in an industry that pays an average wage of $180,000 a year. Those were great jobs and helped buoy the whole state, but most won’t find similar work locally.
“A lot of them are likely going to have to leave Oregon, which means that we lose our friends and neighbors, their talent and we lose that tax base as well,”
said Hillsboro Mayor Beach Pace
.
Intel’s struggles, coupled with setbacks at other Oregon institutions like
Nike
and
Oregon Health & Science University
, could put the state’s knowledge economy at risk.
Or, the workers who run those organizations could spark an eventual rebound in the state’s economy instead of a downward spiral.
“The pool of human capital that we already have, the knowledge, the skilled workers that we have, that is to some extent a buffer against potential snowballing of these effects,” said Rajiv Sharma, economics professor at Portland State University. “But of course there’s no guarantee.”
Bigger was better
Intel’s troubles
started several years ago in its Hillsboro research labs
, where scientists pioneered many generations of new microprocessors. The company’s engineers continually pushed the limits of physics, cooking up new recipes for more sophisticated computer chips that led the industry.
Since Intel’s technology was the most advanced, its processors ran nearly every PC and data center. That, in turn, gave Intel the resources to invest in future innovation.
That all went wrong in the years leading up to the pandemic, though, when
Intel suffered years of delays in a key new chip technology
just as rivals began moving ahead with their own, more advanced processors.
Intel embarked on an expensive campaign to catch up under former CEO Pat Gelsinger. But investors were turned off by the tens of billions of dollars he planned to spend, reluctant to risk throwing good money after bad, and Intel’s board
forced out Gelsinger in December
.
While Intel has paused plans for factories in Germany, Israel and Ohio, the company says Oregon remains central to its future. It has told state officials that
an expansion it began two years ago will move ahead
.
“Oregon will continue to play a critical role in Intel’s global operations, serving as the epicenter of our cutting-edge semiconductor research, technology development, and manufacturing,” the company said in a statement Monday.
Still, new Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says layoffs are a necessary step to restore the company’s competitiveness.
“It’s simple math,” Tan told employees last week. He noted that rivals Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. have — combined — only slightly more employees than Intel. And they are far more profitable.
Intel has laid off about 4,000 workers across the country in just the past week. Tan said a smaller company will move faster and make better decisions.
For Oregon, though, bigger has always been better.
The state’s general fund – which pays for all manner of public services, from schools to public safety to health-care – is heavily reliant on personal income taxes, especially from large, high-wage employers like Intel.
Many years ago, Oregon lawmakers remade the tax code to dramatically reduce the tax burden for multinational companies like Intel that do most of their business out of state. And local officials exempted Intel from most local property taxes, reasoning that if Intel spend

data.title: Show HN: A 'Choose Your Own Adventure' written in Emacs Org Mode
data.author: dskhatri
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个互动叙事项目的多方面讨论，包括术语使用、技术工具选择、AI图像生成等问题。

不同观点：
• [dvh] 强烈建议不要使用某个特定类型的四字描述和四字母缩写，因为商标持有者对此非常激进地追责。他建议删除所有相关提及，并用其他描述替代，如“交互式故事”、“分支叙事”等。

• [laurentlb] 分享了自己在选择CYOA（Choose Your Own Adventure）工具时的经验，推荐使用Ink，因为它使用基于文本的语言，类似于markdown，适合在文本编辑器中使用。

• [quibono] 对AI生成图像的使用持矛盾态度。虽然想喜欢这些图像，但觉得它们有些分散注意力。

• [Loic] 提到自己使用Emacs超过20年，但现在发现越来越难完全依赖Emacs，因为外部客户要求的软件和AI工具的介入。他寻求在Linux/Gnome环境下保持Emacs使用一致性的资源。

• [a_e_k] 提到GNU Emacs中自1994年以来包含的M-x dunnet，这是一个与Emacs相关的游戏。

• [lordgrenville] 原本期待一个用Emacs Lisp编写的游戏引擎，但仍然认为当前项目很酷并表示祝贺。

• [chrisweekly] 对项目表示赞赏，特别是开源工具的分享，认为这是吸引人访问HN（可能指Hacker News）的原因。

• [everybodyknows] 提交了一个关于项目网站的bug报告，指出角色Daphne的眼睛颜色在不同场景中不一致。

• [kleiba] 询问图像是否由Twinery生成，并关心如何保证生成角色在多幅图中的一致性。

• [babuloseo] 对AI生成艺术持负面态度，认为人们应该停止购买这些产品，并建议公开或披露AI在艺术创作中的使用情况。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是AI生成图像的使用，部分人觉得图像不一致或分散注意力，而另一些人则关注是否公开披露AI在创作中的应用。
• 另一个讨论点是Emacs的使用，特别是在现代开发环境中的适应性和一致性问题。
• 项目术语的使用引发了关于商标法律风险的讨论，强调了在特定行业术语使用上的谨慎必要性。

data.title: Gaslight-driven development
data.author: theodorejb
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能（特别是大型语言模型，LLM）对软件开发的影响，尤其是API设计。作者指出，随着AI生成代码的比例增加，开发者逐渐依赖AI的建议，甚至根据AI的偏好调整API设计。例如，某些公司因ChatGPT的错误建议而添加了新功能或更改了代码。这种现象让人感觉怪异，但也提供了独特的测试视角，帮助开发者从新手角度发现问题。不过，AI并不适合创新性工作，仅擅长处理常规任务。文章最后强调，AI不仅使用人类提供的工具，还对其设计提出意见，甚至通过“煤气灯效应”让人误以为这些意见一直存在。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLM（大型语言模型）在开发中的影响及其引发的问题的讨论

不同观点：
• Tcepsa认为，当LLM建议不存在的API端点时，开发者可以实现这些端点并返回特定的HTTP状态码，如"421: Misdirected Request"或"501: Not Implemented"。甚至提议引入"513: Your Coding Assistant Is Wrong"的状态码。
• hamish-b提到用户动态显示功能对阅读体验的影响，指出用户频繁进出页面使得阅读文章变得困难。
• abtinf分享了其实际经验，表示因LLM一直错误地使用tx.create代替tx.update，他们最终实现了tx.create功能，认为这节省了开发时间。
• delifue对此持不同意见，认为如果一个函数同时用于插入和更新，应该命名为"put"，使用"update"具有误导性。
• tdstein不同意原帖的观点，认为人们的设计选择是由人类做出的，而不是计算机，并举例说明人们创建账户和确认电子邮件的常见行为。
• jaredcwhite强烈反对仅因为LLM生成的文本错误而修改代码，认为这种做法荒谬至极。
• debarshri提出未来的编码原则将围绕AI和代码生成工具展开，强调代码的可维护性和适应性，而非传统的代码复杂度和可读性。
• bjornsing对LLM持积极态度，认为它们可以减少在不同客户项目中处理各种命名惯例的精力消耗，提升工作效率。
• sfvisser以幽默的方式指出，我们已经在为机器服务，但实际上可能是在为律师和官僚服务。
• Waterluvian建议为AI寻找一个更准确且无偏见的名称，认为将其视为一个极好的自动补全工具可以清理思维模型。
• jackwilsdon提供了一个相关链接，供读者参考更多讨论。
• gusfoo和kelvinjps10以及shutupnerd0000都提到了页面可读性问题，分别建议删除某些页面元素或使用阅读模式。
• meepmorp质疑，如果人类提供错误编程建议，公司是否也会同样处理并添加想象中的功能。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了LLM在开发过程中的实际影响，包括其错误建议可能导致的开发调整以及开发者的不同反应。
• 有人关注实际用户体验问题，如页面动态元素对阅读的干扰，以及通过技术手段（如阅读模式）改善体验的方法。
• 对未来编码和开发方式的展望引发了关于人机关系的思考。

争议焦点：
• LLM在开发中的角色及其对开发实践的影响是好是坏，开发者应如何应对其错误建议。
• 编码原则的未来发展方向，是以传统的人类可读性为主，还是适应AI生成工具的新需求。

44588383.article_content:
Gaslight-driven development
Any person who has used a computer in the past ten years knows that doing meaningless tasks is just part of the experience. Millions of people create accounts, confirm emails, dismiss notifications, solve captchas, reject cookies, and accept terms and conditions—not because they particularly want to or even need to. They do it because that’s what the computer told them to do. Like it or not, we are already serving the machines.
Well, now there is a new way to serve our silicon overlords. LLMs started to have opinions on how your API
should
look, and since 90% of all code will be written by AI
comes September
, we have no choice but to oblige.
You might’ve heard a story of Soundslice
adding a feature because ChatGPT kept telling people it exists
. We see the same at Instant: for example, we used
tx.update
for both inserting and updating entities, but LLMs kept writing
tx.create
instead. Guess what: we now have
tx.create
, too.
Is it good or is it bad? It definitely feels strange. In a sense, it’s helpful: LLMs here have seen millions of other APIs and are suggesting the most obvious thing, something every developer would think of first, too.
It’s also a unique testing device: if developers use your API wrong, they blame themselves, read the documentation, and fix their code. In the end, you might never learn that they even had the problem. But with ChatGPT, you yourself can experience “newbie’s POV” at any time.
Of course, this approach doesn’t work if you are trying to do something new and unique. LLMs just won’t “get it”. But how many of us are doing something new and unique? Maybe, API is not the place to get clever? Maybe, for most cases, it’s truly best if you did the most obvious thing?
So welcome to the new era. AI is not just using tools we gave it. It now has opinions about how these tools should’ve been made. And instead of asking nicely, it gaslights everybody into thinking that’s how it’s always been.
July 16, 2025
44588383.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能（特别是大型语言模型，LLM）对软件开发的影响，尤其是API设计。作者指出，随着AI生成代码的比例增加，开发者逐渐依赖AI的建议，甚至根据AI的偏好调整API设计。例如，某些公司因ChatGPT的错误建议而添加了新功能或更改了代码。这种现象让人感觉怪异，但也提供了独特的测试视角，帮助开发者从新手角度发现问题。不过，AI并不适合创新性工作，仅擅长处理常规任务。文章最后强调，AI不仅使用人类提供的工具，还对其设计提出意见，甚至通过“煤气灯效应”让人误以为这些意见一直存在。

• hamish-b提到用户动态显示功能对阅读体验的影响，指出用户频繁进出页面使得阅读文章变得困难。

• tdstein不同意原帖的观点，认为人们的设计选择是由人类做出的，而不是计算机，并举例说明人们创建账户和确认电子邮件的常见行为。
• jaredcwhite强烈反对仅因为LLM生成的文本错误而修改代码，认为这种做法荒谬至极。

44560123.article_content:
New Manager Essentials: A Practical Guide to Your First Months in Leadership
Human & Leadership Growth
14 Jul
Written By
Busra Koken
Here you are, a new manager. Congrats!
Perhaps, you’ve been an Individual Contributor (IC) for a while, patiently waiting for the right moment to step into an Engineering Manager (EM) role. You've studied management books, offered mentorship within the team, and mentally rehearsed various scenarios. And now the role is officially yours.
You're likely feeling proud and excited, and maybe a little anxious too. That’s a very human response. After all, our education and experience teaches us how to be great engineers, but management often comes with very little formal preparation.
In this blog post, I’ll walk through some of the early challenges I faced when transitioning into engineering management. Plus share a few practical approaches that helped me find my footing.
Think of it as a mix of reassurance and small things you can try right away.
First Things First: No Need to Have All the Answers Right Away
One of my biggest surprises when becoming a manager was
how quickly
my peers, teammates started looking to me for guidance on priorities and important decisions.
On my very first week as an EM, a peer asked me how we should prioritize a critical task and a stakeholder immediately sought my input on a strategic decision I hadn't yet considered. My initial reaction was mild panic:
"Do I need to have opinions already?"
It can feel really overwhelming, and pressuring. So please remember:
you have the right to slow things down and approach these questions
realistically
and
collaboratively
.
You don't have to rush into decisions when you are not fully informed or have an opinion yet. Instead, create space by being true to your experience:
"Hmm, I don’t have a complete opinion yet, and need some time to work through. Can I follow up on Friday?"
"Great question. I'd love to discuss this with the team first and see how we collectively want to approach it. When do you need this info from us?"
"We're actually working through this right now and your input would be really helpful. Want to explore it together?"
Taking this approach shifts your role from a decision-maker to facilitator of good decisions
. It emphasizes groundedness, collaboration, and consensus-building from the very start. Because your
primary responsibility
as a manager isn’t to know it all, but it’s to help your team succeed at its mission.
Agreements > Expectations
Most engineers deeply value autonomy —I certainly did. One of my early worries when stepping into management was unintentionally coming across as a micromanager.
How can you give your team enough space for creative problem-solving while still meeting business goals? And how can you comfortably check in on progress without hovering?
Important and caring questions.
The key I learned here is leaning into clear agreements rather than relying on unspoken expectations.
Agreements can be co-created and be motivating; expectations on the other hand tend to cause unnecessary stress and confusion.
For example, imagine one of your engineers often underestimates how long tasks will take, leading to frustration and delays. Instead of stepping in to take control, you can guide the conversation to collaborative agreements:
“Do you think we can commit to shipping this by Friday? What kind of support would help make that happen?”
“What parts of the work feel doable by Tuesday? Great, let’s commit to that. And if anything shifts, can you give me a heads-up a day in advance?”
Agreements create enormous focus and clarity. They’re not hard to reach if you stay curious and collaborative. And when people feel involved in defining the path, they often find creative ways to get there.
Similarly, if your team continues to struggle with estimation or breaking down tasks, you might also gently coach them with:
"What's the first small step we could take to kick this off?"
"That sounds like a lot. Would creating a short RFC help clarify things first? Here are a couple of people who could offer valuable input."
Taking this approach isn’t micromanaging;
it’s
facilitating good thinking, and co-creating clarity.
The more you practice this, the more your team will start to internalize the habit of thinking in steps, seeking input early, and setting realistic expectations without you needing to prompt it every time.
This is how
autonomy
actually grows: not by stepping back entirely, but by being present in a way that supports ownership and fosters trust.
Making 1:1s Feel Human and Genuinely Valuable
1:1s can feel a bit awkward at first, especially when you’re managing former peers. In my experience, naming this really helps ease the transition for both sides. You might say:
“I realize this might feel a bit strange at first. How can we make this easy on us?”
“I’d love to hear how we can best partner together to support the team, especially now that I’ll have a different kind of context.”

data.article_summary: 国际机械音乐保存者协会提供了一个数据库，包含16,182卷扫描的钢琴卷，用户可以按多种方式排序查看。这些钢琴卷的音乐主要出版于1929年及之前，部分可下载的MIDI文件来自该时期的音乐。数据库每页显示200项，共81页，并提供如标题、作曲者、表演者等详细信息。此外，网站列出了最近添加的卷档案及其扫描者，例如《Kisses》、《Clair de lune - rhythm version》等作品，并包括具体的制造商编号和版权年份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钢琴卷物的数字化、分析、播放及其相关技术问题和版权限制

不同观点：
• Zulko分享了自己在钢琴卷物分析和转录方面的技术工作，包括两个工具"Unroll"和"Pianola"，以及一些具体的转录实例。Zulko强调了这些工具在处理钢琴卷物MIDI文件并将其转换为乐谱方面的实用性。
• Prvc提出了一个技术性音乐项目的想法，即如何自动"修正"Welte-Mignon录音的现有曲目，指出这些录音在现代回放中存在tempo不均和声部不同步的问题，并认为可以通过技术手段进行更准确的复原。
• BluGill解释了钢琴卷物的不同版本问题，指出即使目录号相同，不同版本的卷物也可能存在差异，追踪这些"版本"也是乐趣之一。
• Masfuerte提供了在VLC播放MIDI文件的技术建议，包括使用SoundFont文件的必要性，并指出了VLC维基页面过时的问题。
• Bookofjoe指出了由于美国版权限制，1929年以后发表的歌曲不能公开下载的问题。
• JKCalhoun分享了自己使用Garage Band播放下载的MIDI文件的积极体验。
• Ryandvm对只能下载1929年之前的MIDI文件表示不解，质疑列出无法共享的曲目列表的意义。
• Bluestein提出了使用tokenizer和vectorize技术无限生成钢琴音乐的设想。
• Irrational认为由于过度使用，资源可能已经被耗尽。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了技术实现、版权法律限制、历史录音的修复以及具体工具的使用建议等多方面内容，展现了钢琴卷物数字化过程中的多样化挑战和可能性。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在版权限制对资源共享的影响，以及如何在技术上改进历史录音的播放质量。

44545708.article_summary: 国际机械音乐保存者协会提供了一个数据库，包含16,182卷扫描的钢琴卷，用户可以按多种方式排序查看。这些钢琴卷的音乐主要出版于1929年及之前，部分可下载的MIDI文件来自该时期的音乐。数据库每页显示200项，共81页，并提供如标题、作曲者、表演者等详细信息。此外，网站列出了最近添加的卷档案及其扫描者，例如《Kisses》、《Clair de lune - rhythm version》等作品，并包括具体的制造商编号和版权年份。
44545708.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钢琴卷物的数字化、分析、播放及其相关技术问题和版权限制

不同观点：
• Zulko分享了自己在钢琴卷物分析和转录方面的技术工作，包括两个工具"Unroll"和"Pianola"，以及一些具体的转录实例。Zulko强调了这些工具在处理钢琴卷物MIDI文件并将其转换为乐谱方面的实用性。
• Prvc提出了一个技术性音乐项目的想法，即如何自动"修正"Welte-Mignon录音的现有曲目，指出这些录音在现代回放中存在tempo不均和声部不同步的问题，并认为可以通过技术手段进行更准确的复原。
• BluGill解释了钢琴卷物的不同版本问题，指出即使目录号相同，不同版本的卷物也可能存在差异，追踪这些"版本"也是乐趣之一。
• Masfuerte提供了在VLC播放MIDI文件的技术建议，包括使用SoundFont文件的必要性，并指出了VLC维基页面过时的问题。
• Bookofjoe指出了由于美国版权限制，1929年以后发表的歌曲不能公开下载的问题。
• JKCalhoun分享了自己使用Garage Band播放下载的MIDI文件的积极体验。
• Ryandvm对只能下载1929年之前的MIDI文件表示不解，质疑列出无法共享的曲目列表的意义。
• Bluestein提出了使用tokenizer和vectorize技术无限生成钢琴音乐的设想。
• Irrational认为由于过度使用，资源可能已经被耗尽。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了技术实现、版权法律限制、历史录音的修复以及具体工具的使用建议等多方面内容，展现了钢琴卷物数字化过程中的多样化挑战和可能性。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在版权限制对资源共享的影响，以及如何在技术上改进历史录音的播放质量。

data.title: “Reading Rainbow” was created to combat summer reading slumps
data.author: arbesman
data.article_summary: 《Reading Rainbow》是由演员LeVar Burton主持的儿童节目，1983年在PBS首播，共播出23年，获得26项艾美奖。节目通过实地考察和书籍阅读鼓励儿童阅读，每集介绍一本儿童书籍，并由名人朗读，如Ruby Dee和Jeff Bridges等。节目旨在解决儿童读写能力下降的问题，尤其是在暑假期间，通过电视节目激发孩子们的阅读兴趣。研究显示，教师认为包括《Reading Rainbow》在内的公共电视节目对教育非常有效。该节目不仅成功促进了儿童阅读，还使Burton成为教育偶像，影响了一代观众。2022年纪录片《Butterfly in the Sky: The Story of Reading Rainbow》进一步展现了该节目的文化影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对公共广播服务（PBS）和阅读激励项目的评价与回忆，特别是与《Reading Rainbow》相关的文化和教育影响。

不同观点：
• [支持公共广播服务和阅读激励] 许多人对PBS和《Reading Rainbow》等节目表示支持，认为其对推动儿童阅读习惯有积极影响。例如，用户lenerdenator提到削减PBS资金的潜在问题，而aspenmayer强调LeVar Burton让学习变得有趣且酷。

• [具体阅读激励项目的例子] 一些用户分享了自己对不同阅读激励项目的个人经历和观察。kleiba提到当地基督教图书馆的“暑期阅读”活动，而internet_points介绍了挪威的游戏化阅读项目，通过积分和奖励机制激励孩子阅读。

• [对现代教育制度的批评] 用户david2ndaccount提出，暑期阅读项目只是“治标不治本”，根本问题是儿童不应有如此长的暑假，建议将假期分散到全年，以提高学术成就。这一观点引发对教育制度和教师工会的讨论。

• [怀旧情感] 多个用户（如CSMastermind、LongjumpingCat、ChrisArchitect）表达了对过去阅读激励项目的怀旧情感，包括《Wishbone》、Dolly Parton的阅读项目和Pizza Hut的“Book It!”项目，认为这些项目在过去极大地激励了青少年的阅读兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [LeVar Burton的其他工作] kochb提到LeVar Burton主持了一个面向成人的播客，继续推动终身阅读，并提供了播客链接。mproud则提到Netflix上的纪录片《Butterfly in the Sky》。

• [无关评论] 用户AdmiralAsshat发布了一条与讨论无关的评论，提及了自己喜欢的一首歌。

争议焦点：
• 暑期阅读项目是否只是解决教育问题的“权宜之计”，以及长暑假对儿童学术成就的实际影响。用户david2ndaccount对暑期过长的批评与其他用户对阅读激励项目的怀旧和支持形成了对比。

44588491.article_content:
At left, Tony Buttino prepares Western New York book reviewers (from left to right: Stephanie, Percy and Afrika) with production assistant Pam Johnson at right.
Courtesy of WNED PBS, Buffalo, NY
For generations of readers, four words convey what it means to love books: “butterfly in the sky.” These are the opening lyrics of the famous
theme song
for the beloved children’s program “
Reading Rainbow
,” hosted by actor LeVar Burton. PBS premiered the show in 1983, and it ran for 23 years, received 26 Emmy Awards, and won the hearts of millions. The series, like the song, encouraged young readers to “take a look,” because whatever knowledge they sought, “it’s in a book.”
As those who watched the show know, “butterfly in the sky” became the words that always preceded a good story. The words are so significant to the legacy of “Reading Rainbow” that they serve as
the namesake
for the 2022 documentary about the cult classic program,
Butterfly in the Sky: The Story of Reading Rainbow
.
In recent years, numerous reports have warned of a national literacy crisis, for
children
and
adults
alike. “Reading Rainbow” is the essential example of a show about the importance of literacy, reading comprehension and the joy of storytelling, loved by viewers of all ages and from all backgrounds.
“In terms of child literacy rates going down, that was really what ‘Reading Rainbow’ was designed in response to, and in particular the ‘summer slide,’ they call it, which is when students are out of school, their literacy levels slide backward,” says
Ryan Lintelman
, entertainment curator at the Smithsonian’s
National Museum of American History
.
Lintelman says
plenty of research
confirms that, when students come back to school in the fall, teachers need to take some time to bring them back up to speed to the levels of literacy and reading comprehension that they were at when they ended the previous school year. “Reading Rainbow” was made to bridge this reading gap for children and improve their reading skills—and to be a show that kids wanted to watch.
It was known that kids were watching TV all summer, Lintelman says, “So why not do something with it?”
Butterfly in the Sky - Official Trailer (2024) Reading Rainbow Documentary
Watch on
Fun fact: When did "Reading Rainbow" begin?
The show first aired in the summer of 1983 on PBS. It produced 23 seasons before it was canceled in 2006.
On each half-hour episode of “Reading Rainbow,” Burton introduced the real-world subject matter of a children’s book through field trips, from going to the
barbershop
to
visiting an orchestra
in a concert hall, and then the book itself was read by a performer. Ruby Dee, Helen Mirren, Keith David, Ed Harris, Gregory Hines, Jeff Bridges and Pete Seeger are just a few of the actors and musicians who graced the show with their voices. The chosen books are childhood staples, such as
If You Give a Mouse a Cookie
by Laura Numeroff,
Amazing Grace
by Mary Hoffman and
Stellaluna
by Janell Cannon. The program mixes the calm, steady presence of Burton with the warmth and coziness of getting wrapped up in a book. And at the end of the show, kids review books they’ve read.
For over two decades, the show achieved its goal of not only reading to kids, but also making kids want to read. In 1997, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting released a study about the use of television and video in classroom instruction.
Current
, a news outlet covering public media,
reported that
“teachers responding to the survey rated public TV programs as the best they’d used for educational purposes in 1996-97. ‘Reading Rainbow’ was named by a higher percentage of teachers than any other program.”
“I think it’s been shown to be super successful,” Lintelman says, adding that the show inspired a lifelong love of reading in its audience. “People who have been interviewed for this documentary talk about how ‘Reading Rainbow’ was such an important part of their lives and the entire generation. I count myself among them, of people who grew up watching that show and learning about new books through it.”
The curator notes that “Reading Rainbow” was unique in how it spoke about books, showing both the featured book’s illustrations and Burton’s real adventures seeing the people and places represented by the books. The show also made its host, Burton, who had been known for his role as Kunta Kinte in the 1970s miniseries “
Roots
,” into an icon of education. He later went on to star as Geordi La Forge in another beloved show, “
Star Trek: The Next Generation
,” which ran from 1987 to 1994.
Host LeVar Burton displays the book
Gila Monsters Meet You at the Airport
, which was featured in the original pilot episode of "Reading Rainbow."
Courtesy of WNED PBS, Buffalo, NY
“Hearing the story from the people who made the show and hearing their evident passion and commitment to doing this children’s television show, every person feels like they were making a significant contribution to culture,” Burton

data.title: Mistakes Microsoft made in the Xbox security system (2005)
data.author: davikr
data.article_summary:
这篇文章由Michael Steil撰写，分析了微软在Xbox安全系统中的17个错误。文章分为多个部分，首先介绍了Xbox的硬件和安全系统的动机，然后详细讨论了启动安全、内核安全及相关错误。微软设计安全系统的初衷是防止Xbox运行盗版游戏、非官方应用和替代操作系统。然而，由于设计和实施中的一系列错误，黑客成功破解了该系统。

主要错误包括：在安全性与成本、速度之间权衡失当；对黑客资源和团队的低估；依赖隐匿安全策略；修复不力；以及在数据表、文献和测试等方面的实施失误。文章强调了这些错误如何使Xbox安全系统易于攻破，并提醒开发者如何避免类似错误。Xbox的硬件本质上类似于PC，这使得它特别容易被用于安装Linux等其他操作系统，进一步挑战了微软的安全措施。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：x86架构及游戏主机（如Xbox和Switch）的安全设计缺陷和硬件漏洞问题

不同观点：
• **mjg59**：认为x86架构早期缺乏验证第一条指令的机制，导致在设计上做出了不好的权衡，特别是在对抗性安全分析不足的情况下。A20地址线问题被认为是历史遗留的设计缺陷，并延续到了21世纪。这一问题可以用作教学案例，帮助理解CPU如何与硬件交互以及低层次平台设计。
  
• **saghm**：提到通过将Xbox CPU的A20#引脚接地，可以绕过安全启动机制，从普通闪存启动。这与任天堂Switch的破解方法类似，都是通过单一引脚的操作实现破解。质疑为何主机厂商没有提前发现这些问题，认为即便组合状态较多，但至少可以通过默认状态分析来预防类似漏洞。

• **Scaevolus**：指出微软从Xbox和Xbox 360的错误中吸取了教训，导致Xbox One和Xbox Series X至今未被破解。引用了平台安全峰会上的演讲支持这一观点。

• **Smaug123**：对文章开头关于微软开发人员能力不足的批评提出异议，认为在已知有问题的情况下找到问题相对容易。引用相关文献和例子说明，指出文章通过选择性呈现设计错误，使得问题显得比实际更容易发现。

• **dang**：提到相关讨论曾在2009年出现过，但只有一条评论。

• **userbinator**：提到另一种可能的破解路径，暗示可能存在多种破解方式。

• **wang_li**：指出RSA算法并不需要太多代码，举例Atari Lynx在512字节内完成了硬件初始化、RSA验证和加载下一步。

• **9991**：认为主机厂商为了通过游戏销售弥补主机低价销售的损失，导致了这些设计缺陷和漏洞的出现。

• **munchler**：提醒讨论内容来自2005年，表明这是历史问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于微软开发人员是否因为技术能力不足而导致Xbox安全问题，还是这些问题的发现得益于事后分析和已知漏洞的提示。
• 不同硬件平台（如Xbox和Switch）的相似漏洞引发对主机厂商在设计初期为何未能预防这些问题的质疑。
• 讨论中还涉及到历史遗留问题（如A20地址线）以及低层次平台设计中的复杂性。
