Introduction
The Xbox is a gaming console, which has been introduced by Microsoft Corporation in late 2001 and competed with the Sony Playstation 2 and the Nintendo GameCube. Microsoft wanted to prevent the Xbox from being used with copied games, unofficial applications and alternative operating systems, and therefore designed and implemented a security system for this purpose.
This article is about the security system of the Xbox and the mistakes Microsoft made. It will not explain basic concepts like buffer exploits, and it will not explain how to construct an effective security system, but it will explain how
not
to do it: This article is about how easy it is to make terrible mistakes and how easily people seem to overestimate their skills. So this article is also about how to avoid the most common mistakes.
For every security concept, this article will first explain the design from Microsoft's perspective, and then describe the hackers' efforts to break the security. If the reader finds the mistakes in the design, this proves that Microsoft has weak developers. If, on the other hand, the reader doesn't find the mistakes, this proves that constructing a security system is indeed hard.
The Xbox Hardware
Because Microsoft had a very tight time frame for the development of the Xbox, they used off-the-shelf PC hardware and their Windows and DirectX technologies as the basis of the console. The Xbox consists of a Pentium III Celeron mobile 733 MHz CPU, 64 MB of RAM, a GeForce 3 MX with TV out, a 10 GB IDE hard disk, an IDE DVD drive, Fast Ethernet, as well as USB for the gamepads. It runs a simplified Windows 2000 kernel, and the games include adapted versions of Win32, libc and DirectX statically linked to them.
Although this sounds a lot more like a PC than, for example, a GameCube with its PowerPC processor, custom optical drive and custom gamepad connectors, it is important to point out that, from a hardware point of view, the Xbox shares
all
properties of a PC: It has LPC, PCI and AGP busses, it has IDE drives, it has a Northbridge and a Southbridge, and it includes all the legacy PC features such as the "PIC" interrupt controller, the "PIT" timer and the A20 gate. nVidia sold a slightly modified Southbridge and a Northbridge with another graphics core embedded for the PC market as the "nForce" chipset between 2001 and 2002.
Motivation for the Security System
The Xbox being a PC, it should be trivial to install Linux on it in order to have a cheap and, for that time, powerful PC. Even today, a small and silent 733 MHz PC with TV connectivity for 149 USD/EUR is still attractive. But this is not the only thing Microsoft wanted to prevent. Linux

44588364.article_summary:
这篇文章由Michael Steil撰写，分析了微软在Xbox安全系统中的17个错误。文章分为多个部分，首先介绍了Xbox的硬件和安全系统的动机，然后详细讨论了启动安全、内核安全及相关错误。微软设计安全系统的初衷是防止Xbox运行盗版游戏、非官方应用和替代操作系统。然而，由于设计和实施中的一系列错误，黑客成功破解了该系统。

主要错误包括：在安全性与成本、速度之间权衡失当；对黑客资源和团队的低估；依赖隐匿安全策略；修复不力；以及在数据表、文献和测试等方面的实施失误。文章强调了这些错误如何使Xbox安全系统易于攻破，并提醒开发者如何避免类似错误。Xbox的硬件本质上类似于PC，这使得它特别容易被用于安装Linux等其他操作系统，进一步挑战了微软的安全措施。
44588364.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：x86架构及游戏主机（如Xbox和Switch）的安全设计缺陷和硬件漏洞问题

不同观点：
• **mjg59**：认为x86架构早期缺乏验证第一条指令的机制，导致在设计上做出了不好的权衡，特别是在对抗性安全分析不足的情况下。A20地址线问题被认为是历史遗留的设计缺陷，并延续到了21世纪。这一问题可以用作教学案例，帮助理解CPU如何与硬件交互以及低层次平台设计。
  
• **saghm**：提到通过将Xbox CPU的A20#引脚接地，可以绕过安全启动机制，从普通闪存启动。这与任天堂Switch的破解方法类似，都是通过单一引脚的操作实现破解。质疑为何主机厂商没有提前发现这些问题，认为即便组合状态较多，但至少可以通过默认状态分析来预防类似漏洞。

• **Scaevolus**：指出微软从Xbox和Xbox 360的错误中吸取了教训，导致Xbox One和Xbox Series X至今未被破解。引用了平台安全峰会上的演讲支持这一观点。

• **Smaug123**：对文章开头关于微软开发人员能力不足的批评提出异议，认为在已知有问题的情况下找到问题相对容易。引用相关文献和例子说明，指出文章通过选择性呈现设计错误，使得问题显得比实际更容易发现。

• **dang**：提到相关讨论曾在2009年出现过，但只有一条评论。

• **userbinator**：提到另一种可能的破解路径，暗示可能存在多种破解方式。

• **wang_li**：指出RSA算法并不需要太多代码，举例Atari Lynx在512字节内完成了硬件初始化、RSA验证和加载下一步。

• **9991**：认为主机厂商为了通过游戏销售弥补主机低价销售的损失，导致了这些设计缺陷和漏洞的出现。

• **munchler**：提醒讨论内容来自2005年，表明这是历史问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于微软开发人员是否因为技术能力不足而导致Xbox安全问题，还是这些问题的发现得益于事后分析和已知漏洞的提示。
• 不同硬件平台（如Xbox和Switch）的相似漏洞引发对主机厂商在设计初期为何未能预防这些问题的质疑。
• 讨论中还涉及到历史遗留问题（如A20地址线）以及低层次平台设计中的复杂性。

data.title: I was wrong about robots.txt
data.author: EPendragon
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在修改网站的robots.txt文件以禁止所有爬虫访问后，意外发现其LinkedIn帖子无法显示文章预览的问题。经过调查，作者使用LinkedIn Post Inspector工具找到了原因：由于robots.txt的限制，LinkedIn的爬虫无法抓取网页的Open Graph meta标签，导致无法生成链接预览。Open Graph协议通过在网页中添加meta标签，使链接在社交媒体上展示更丰富的内容。作者随后调整了robots.txt文件，允许LinkedInBot爬取资源，解决了预览问题。本文强调了在实施类似变更时，需全面考虑其潜在影响，并通过工具排查问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于robots.txt的用途、局限性及其在现代网络环境中的有效性

不同观点：
• Falkon1313认为robots.txt最初是为了解决动态网站的重复内容问题，并防止搜索引擎的惩罚。然而，它无法阻止恶意的爬虫，且与"Do-Not-Track"头信息类似，对不遵守规则的爬虫无用。
• dumbfounder指出自己在2003年创建搜索引擎时，尽管使用了规范的用户代理字符串并包含电子邮件地址，仍收到许多抱怨，显示出对非Google爬虫的偏见，这不利于竞争。
• franga2000强调robots.txt依赖于对爬虫身份的识别而非其目的，可能导致大公司获得更大的权力优势，建议应有更细致的规则和法律框架来区分不同类型的爬虫行为。
• donohoe认为作者将一个基本的后果描述为深刻的领悟，缺乏实际的洞见，且文章有寻求关注之嫌。
• NackerHughes批评文章内容冗长，核心观点可以简化为两行。
• PaulKeeble指出robots.txt对不遵守规则的爬虫无效，这些问题爬虫通常是造成网站负担的主要原因。
• klausa提到苹果在iMessage中生成链接预览的客户端方式，与LinkedIn的方式形成对比，提供了不同的解决方案视角。
• hiAndrewQuinn建议通过微支付来解决爬虫问题，但承认技术虽存在，却很少被采用，实际解决方案可能仍是传统的禁止访问方式。
• yodon指出缺乏易用的库来解析robots.txt和meta robots标签，增加了爬虫作者遵循规则的难度。
• azangru纠正关于robots.txt中"disallow"指令对Google搜索结果影响的误解，指出被禁止的页面将从索引中移除。
• s-mon基于过去的经验指出，一些简单的攻击正是利用了与robots.txt指示相反的行为，显示出该文件对不守规则者的无效性。
• alexey-salmin以幽默的方式将文章与C++编程中的"private"关键字使用类比，暗示文章内容显而易见。
• podgorniy批评文章通过近无意义的行动来提升在线存在感，不希望看到太多类似帖子。
• jjcob认为如果不想让内容被爬取，就不应将其发布在网上，并指出禁止robots可能影响如Internet Archive等重要服务。

补充讨论：
• robots.txt的有效性和局限性：多个评论提到该文件仅对遵守规则的爬虫有效，而对恶意爬虫无用。
• 大公司与小开发者之间的权力不平衡：franga2000特别指出，选择性允许特定爬虫可能加剧大公司优势。
• 替代解决方案：包括技术性解决方案（如微支付）和政策性讨论（如法律框架）。
• 对文章本身的批评：部分评论批评文章内容冗长或缺乏洞见。

44588437.article_content:
Recently, I wrote an article about my journey in learning about
robots.txt
and its implications on the data rights in regards to what I write in my blog. I was confident that I wanted to ban all the crawlers from my website. Turned out there was an unintended consequence that I did not account for.
My LinkedIn posts became broken
#
Ever since I changed my
robots.txt
file, I started seeing that my LinkedIn posts no longer had the preview of the article available. I was not sure what the issue was initially, since before then it used to work just fine. In addition to that, I have noticed that LinkedIn’s algorithm has started serving my posts to fewer and fewer connections. I was a bit confused by the issue, thinking that it might have been a temporary problem. But over the next two weeks the missing post previews did not appear.
This is what my LinkedIn posts used to look like: no link preview and little engagement with the post
After doing a quick search, I found a tool called
LinkedIn Post Inspector
. This tool can show everything that you would want to know about links that you are about to share on the platform. I plugged in my recent article in the tool and it revealed to me the reason why I could no longer see the previews - the
robots.txt
file had a directive that would not allow LinkedIn bot to scrape the web pages. This was the error message that I got:
Error
We did not re-scrape
https://evgeniipendragon.com/posts/i-am-disallowing-all-crawlers-to-scrape-my-website-and-why-you-should-too/
because the URL or one of its redirects is blocked by rules set in robots.txt file ofits URL domain.
Fair enough! Thinking of it now - it makes so much sense! I should have seen that ahead of time. Whenever you want to post something on LinkedIn or other social media platform, they would need to request the page the link of which you are about to share. These bots need that page in order to get access to the meta tags necessary to create the preview. Those are known as Open Graph meta tags. And it all comes from
Open Graph Protocol
, which was originally created at Facebook.
Open Graph Protocol
#
According to the OPG website,
The
Open Graph protocol
enables any web page to become a rich object in a social graph. For instance, this is used on Facebook to allow any web page to have the same functionality as any other object on Facebook.
There are only a few required tags needed to implement this for your web resource. But this protocol is highly extensible and allows for all sorts of media to be used as meta information about your page.
To turn your web pages into graph objects, you need to add basic metadata to your page. We’ve based the initial version of the protocol on
RDFa
which means that you’ll place additional
<meta>
tags in the
<head>
of your web page. The four required properties for every page are:
og:title
- The title of your object as it should appear within the graph, e.g., “The Rock”.
og:type
- The
type
of your object, e.g., “video.movie”. Depending on the type you specify, other properties may also be required.
og:image
- An image URL which should represent your object within the graph.
og:url
- The canonical URL of your object that will be used as its permanent ID in the graph, e.g., “
https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117500/"
.
This simple yet powerful protocol is what makes the posts across all of the Internet more presentable and informative.
Updating robots.txt
#
To turn this issue around I updated my
robots.txt
to allow
LinkedInBot
to crawl my resources. If I would want to start posting on other social media sites and see the previews for the posts, I would need to include those other bots here as well. My new current configuration looks like this:
User-agent: LinkedInBot
Allow: /
User-agent: *
Disallow: /
Lessons Learned
#
Turns out that sometimes drastic measures like blocking all crawlers could make content presentation suffer. What I missed when I implemented that change was the fact that I didn’t thoroughly test the impact of blocking all of the traffic like that. Now that I have encountered that issue, it led me to learn more about the Open Graph Protocol and tools like LinkedIn Post Inspector which told me what the problem was.
When working on any feature - no matter how small it is - make sure that you understand the domain in which you are creating the changes. As the practice shows, sometimes that is not how things work out. Initially I did not connect the dots between the OPG and robots.txt prohibitions.
Sometimes you have to break a few eggs before you make an omelet. Well… you always have to break some eggs to make an omelet… You get the point.

data.title: A 1960s schools experiment that created a new alphabet
data.author: Hooke
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了20世纪60年代英国一场激进的教育实验——初始教学字母（ITA）。该实验通过引入一套包含44个字符的新字母表，试图让英语拼读更加直观，从而帮助儿童更快学会阅读。ITA在英国及一些英语国家的小学中试行，旨在解决英语拼写不规则导致的阅读困难。然而，实验并未如预期那样成功，许多接受ITA教育的孩子成年后仍然存在拼写问题。ITA在短短几年内迅速推广，随后又悄然消失，几乎没有留下记录或解释。这场实验对参与者的影响持续至今，一些人在成年后仍对拼写感到困惑。文章探讨了该实验的实施、后果以及被遗忘的经历。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：教育领域的教学方法和字母系统的改革与实验

不同观点：
• [kleiba的观点] 认为教育学缺乏科学基础，很多教学方法是猜测性的，且新的教学方法常常被强制推广，没有经过充分的实验验证和伦理审查。他特别提到强制使用平板电脑等现代工具，而不允许传统的方法如纸笔，质疑这种做法的合理性。

• [JKCalhoun的观点] 怀念20世纪60年代的实验性教学方法，分享了自己在一个采用开放式教育和独特建筑设计学校中的经历。他认为这些实验性方法中的一些是有价值的，并对这些方法被废弃感到遗憾。

• [Perenti的观点] 通过个人经历说明了一种失败的教学方法（ITA），认为这种方法培养了许多文盲，尤其是对那些不如他朋友聪明的学生来说更困难。

* If you are able to read these words, you might have been part of a failed English teaching initiative.
Composite: The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
* If you are able to read these words, you might have been part of a failed English teaching initiative.
Composite: The Guardian
Education
The radical 1960s schools experiment that created a whole new alphabet – and left thousands of children unable to spell
Decades ago, a generation of UK schoolchildren unwittingly took part in an initiative aimed at boosting reading skills – with lasting consequences
Emma Loffhagen
Sun 6 Jul 2025 07.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 7 Jul 2025 08.39 EDT
Share
T
hroughout my life, my mum has always been a big reader. She was in
three or four book clubs at the same time. She’d devour whatever texts my siblings and I were studying in school, handwrite notes for our lunchboxes and write in her diary every night. Our fridge door was a revolving display of word-of-the-day flashcards. Despite this, she also was and remains, by some margin, the worst speller I have met.
By the time I was in primary school, she was already asking me to proofread her work emails, often littered with mistakes that were glaringly obvious to me even at such a young age. It used to baffle me – how could this person, who races through multiple books a week and can quote Shakespeare faultlessly, possibly think “me” is spelt with two Es?
It was on one of these occasions that she first mentioned she had been taught the wrong alphabet. “Google it,” she said. “It was an experiment, so it doesn’t exist any more, but it was called ITA.”
View image in fullscreen
‘What the hell was any of that supposed to mean?’ Judith Loffhagen.
Photograph: Thomas Dufffield/The Guardian
At first, I thought she was joking, or maybe misremembering some exaggerated version of phonics. But later, I looked it up and, sure enough, there it was – a strange chart of more than 40 characters, many familiar, others alien. Sphinx-like ligatures, odd slashes, conjoined vowels – it looked like a cross between English and Greek.
“My memory is so poor, but I can still see those devilish characters,” my mum, Judith Loffhagen, says as we sit in the garden of my childhood home in London. “An ‘a’ with an ‘e’ on its back, two ‘c’s with a line across them.” She traces the shapes on her trouser leg. “What the hell was any of that supposed to mean?”
View image in fullscreen
A 1966 Ladybird book that used ITA.
Photograph: Marc Tielemans/Alamy
The Initial Teaching Alphabet was a radical, little-known educational experiment trialled in British schools (and in other English-speaking countries) during the 1960s and 70s. Billed as a way to help children learn to read faster by making spelling more phonetically intuitive, it radically rewrote the rules of literacy for tens of thousands of children seemingly overnight. And then it vanished without explanation. Barely documented, rarely acknowledged, and quietly abandoned – but never quite forgotten by those it touched.
Why was it only implemented in certain schools – or even, in some cases, only certain classes in those schools? How did it appear to disappear without record or reckoning? Are there others like my mum, still aggrieved by ITA? And what happens to a generation taught to read and write using a system that no longer exists?
E
nglish is one of the most difficult languages to learn to read and write. Unlike Spanish or Welsh, where letters have consistent sound values, English is a patchwork of linguistic inheritances. Its roughly 44 phonemes – the distinct sounds that make up speech – can each be spelt multiple ways. The long “i” sound alone, as in “eye”, has more than 20 possible spellings. And many letter combinations contradict one another across different words: think of “through”, “though” and “thought”.
It was precisely this inconsistency that Conservative MP Sir James Pitman – grandson of Sir Isaac Pitman, the inventor of shorthand – identified as the single greatest obstacle for young readers. In a 1953 parliamentary debate, he argued that it is our “illogical and ridiculous spelling” which is the “chief handicap” that leads many children to stumble with reading, with lasting consequences for their education. His proposed solution, launched six years later, was radical: to completely reimagine the alphabet.
The result was ITA: 44 characters, each representing a distinct sound, designed to bypass the chaos of traditional English and teach children to read, and fast. Among the host of strange new letters were a backwards “z”, an “n” with a “g” inside, a backwards “t” conjoined with an “h”, a bloated “w” with an “o” in the middle. Sentences in ITA were all written in lower case.
By 1966, 140 of the 158 UK education authorities taught ITA in at least one of their schools.
The new alphabet was not intended as a permanent replacement for the existing one: the aim was to teach children to read quickly, with the promise they would transition “seamlessly”
44572954.article_summary: 文章讲述了20世纪60年代英国一场激进的教育实验——初始教学字母（ITA）。该实验通过引入一套包含44个字符的新字母表，试图让英语拼读更加直观，从而帮助儿童更快学会阅读。ITA在英国及一些英语国家的小学中试行，旨在解决英语拼写不规则导致的阅读困难。然而，实验并未如预期那样成功，许多接受ITA教育的孩子成年后仍然存在拼写问题。ITA在短短几年内迅速推广，随后又悄然消失，几乎没有留下记录或解释。这场实验对参与者的影响持续至今，一些人在成年后仍对拼写感到困惑。文章探讨了该实验的实施、后果以及被遗忘的经历。

data.title: Blue Pencil no. 18–Some history about Arial
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Arial字体的起源和发展。根据字体设计师Matthew Carter的描述，Arial最初是在20世纪70年代末或1980年由Monotype为IBM开发的，原名Sonoran Sans，旨在作为Helvetica的替代品。由于Monotype当时财务困难，IBM的合同对公司非常重要。文章还提到，微软后来通过贷款协议获得了Arial的使用权。此外，文章对比了Arial和Helvetica的不同，指出Arial更具有人性化的设计特点，并引用了多位专家的观点和资料。文章最后提到，微软委托Monotype为Windows 3.1设计了一系列字体，其中包括Arial。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Arial和Helvetica字体的历史、使用和授权费用的讨论，以及对未来字体生成技术的展望。

不同观点：
• WillAdams认为Microsoft选择开发Arial而不是使用Helvetica是出于多方面考虑，包括开发成本、与Linotype的法律纠纷以及Helvetica与竞争对手Apple的紧密关联。他还提到Microsoft在Arial开发上投入了大量资金，尤其是用于字体微调的人力成本。

• BXLE_1-1-BitIs1分享了个人工作经验，提到在低分辨率环境下更偏好使用无衬线字体，如Arial，而在高分辨率设备上，像Garamond这样的字体表现也不错。他还指出打印机和屏幕分辨率对字体显示效果有很大影响。

• sombragris表达了对Helvetica的喜爱，但出于实用性，在准备可编辑文档时仍选择Arial，因为它广泛兼容且表现稳定，尽管个人更偏好类似Frutiger或Myriad的字体。

• Bluestein提出了对未来AI生成字体的思考，认为未来可能会出现根据个人偏好或影响目的动态生成字体的技术。

补充讨论：
• DiabloD3对文章的排版提出批评，认为关于字体的讨论却使用了过小字号的正文，具有讽刺意味。

争议焦点：
• WillAdams与主流观点的争议在于，他认为Microsoft未选择Helvetica并非单纯为了节省授权费用，而是出于多重实际考虑，包括法律纠纷和品牌竞争。

整体来看，讨论涉及了字体设计的历史背景、技术因素、个人偏好以及对未来技术的展望。

Previously:
Blue Pencil no. 17—Corrections
Blue Pencil no. 18—Some history about Arial
I have moved the third portion of Matthew Carter’s email to me regarding
Just My Type
(see Blue Pencil no. 17—Correction) to a separate post since it was not a correction but a further elucidation of a commment I made. And I have paired it with Rod McDonald’s follow-up email (formerly Blue Pencil no. 17—Addendum).
Matthew Carter:
Somewhere there must be a proper account of the beginnings of Arial, but at the risk of repeating myself or somebody else, here goes. In the late ’70s or 1980 (I’m not sure of the exact date) Xerox and IBM released the first laser-xerographic printers, the Xerox 9700 (300 dpi resolution), and the IBM 3800 (240 dpi resolution). Xerox made an agreement with Mergenthaler to license bitmaps of Times Roman and Helvetica for the 9700. IBM went to Monotype (the only real alternative to Linotype) to license the same faces (in addition to versions of the monospaced fonts they had used in the previous generation of impact printers). Monotype had rights to Times Roman, of course, but not to Helvetica. The contract with IBM was worth a colossal amount of money and Monotype, in one of their periodic financial difficulties, proposed to make what amounted to a Helvetica clone, based ostensibly on their Grots 215 and 216. I was a consultant to IBM’s Printer Planning Division at the time and had the job of going through print-outs of all the Monotype bitmaps to make necessary corrections with red and green pencils. Arial was originally called Sonoran Sans during its development but I believe that IBM used the name Arial by the time it was released.
At a later time Microsoft acquired the rights of access to Monotype’s type library. This was in return for guaranteeing a loan to Monotype (again in financial trouble), a deal brokered by Robert Norton at Microsoft. Through this deal Microsoft picked up Arial. One point I’m not clear about—but should be given my job as consultant—is whether IBM’s Sonoran/Arial had exactly the same set widths as Helvetica or whether that was a refinement introduced by Microsoft.
A footnote. Xerox’s choice of Times and Helvetica as the indispensable pair of “typographic” fonts to replace the typewriter-like impact printer fonts may have had further repercussions. Warnock and Geschke worked at Xerox Parc before founding Adobe. The inclusion of Times and Helvetica as the primary PostScript fonts to replace the typewriter may simply have been suggested by the Xerox/Mergenthaler deal.
Matthew’s account of the origins of Arial seems to ﬁt with that found on
Wikipedia
, though he is hazy on the exact year (Wikipedia says 1982). Matthew says Monotype did not have rights to Helvetica, but Wikipedia says it had sub-licensed the face from Linotype. This is supported by Lawrence W. Wallis’
chronology
of the Monotype Corporation which says that Helvetica was made available on Monotype machines in 1972.
Wallis’ chronology, which was originally published as part of
One Hundred Years of Type Making 1897–1997
, a special centenary issue of
The Monotype Recorder
(New Series No. 10, 1997) under the title “Monotype Time Check” (pp. 46–55). The chronology does not mention Arial or Sonoran Sans. But Arial is briefly, and a bit coyly, discussed in two other contributions to the centenary issue. David Saunders, in “Two decades of change 1965–1986” (pp. 26–35), writes, “It was apparent to both Robin Nicholas and Patricia Saunders, another staff designer trained in the Monotype TDO [Type Drawing Office], that a more humanist approach to type was developing in the 80s, and they incorporated this into their design. The result is a typeface [Arial] that is more rounded than its rival, Helvetica.” He dates Arial, a “somewhat impersonal” sans serif, to 1982 but says nothing about IBM or Microsoft. The differences between Arial and Helvetica are then enumerated—with an emphasis on the bowed leg of the
R
as being closer to Gill Sans than to either Helvetica or earlier grotesques such as Monotype Grotesque 215.
In “New technology, new developments: 1986–1997” (pp. 36–45), Andrew Boag writes, “Following the supply of the 13 core fonts for Microsoft’s Windows 3.1 software… Microsoft commissioned a further set of 22 fonts to make up a ‘plus’ set, intended to provide Windows users with a set of fonts suitable for a range of document production tasks.… This project called for both new designs, and modifications to existing designs.” The designs that he lists are Century Gothic, Bookman Old Style and Corsi

data.title: The battle for Britain’s first book of the month club
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: 《History Today》杂志的文章《History Matters: The Battle for Britain’s First Book of the Month Club》介绍了英国首个书籍订阅俱乐部——图书协会（Book Society）的成立及其影响。该俱乐部于1929年成立，通过每月邮寄精选书籍，将阅读带给更广泛的读者群。其中，加拿大作家Mazo de la Roche的小说《Whiteoaks》作为第七本推荐书目，体现了俱乐部偏好娱乐性强、易读但不复杂的作品。然而，这种选择也引发了一些争议，特别是关于选书标准和文学品味的问题。文章强调了图书协会在两次世界大战之间对英国阅读文化的重要影响。

History Matters
The Battle for Britain’s First Book of the Month Club
Britain’s first book-of-the-month club – the Book Society – brought reading to a vast new audience. But not without some controversy.
Nicola Wilson
| Published in
History Today
Volume 75 Issue 7 July 2025
I
n October 1929 thousands of members of Britain’s Book Society received a new hardback through the post.
Whiteoaks,
by an unfamiliar Canadian writer, Mazo de la Roche, was the seventh monthly ‘choice’ of the society, Britain’s first subscription book-of-the-month club, begun in April that same year. The novel confirmed the club’s taste for entertaining page-turners; books that were worth investing time and money in, though not too complex or ‘highbrow’. ‘No selection that the Book Society has made has given me so much pleasure as this one’ wrote the head of the selection committee, bestselling novelist Hugh Walpole, in the

data.title: Inside the box: Everything I did with an Arduino starter kit
data.author: lopespm
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了作者通过Elegoo Arduino Uno R3 starter kit学习电子基础概念的经历，重点探索了LED、RGB LED、74HC595扩展IC、电容平滑LED亮度变化、七段数码管和LED矩阵显示等内容。作者从最基础的点亮LED开始，逐步探索了如何使用PWM控制RGB LED颜色、通过74HC595扩展Arduino输出以控制8个LED、利用电容实现LED平滑淡出效果，以及操控单个和多个七段数码管显示数字和自定义图案。此外，作者还展示了如何在LED矩阵上实现滚动显示效果和在LCD上展示长字符串。文章通过具体代码和实践展示了Arduino在电子项目中的应用，适合初学者理解和实验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子 starter 套件的价值和使用体验

不同观点：
• **支持与积极体验**：
   - [hi_hi] 认为 starter 套件对于新手非常友好，能够降低入门门槛，激发对技术的兴趣。他通过套件学到了很多基础知识，甚至深入了解了LED和电源需求等物理原理。他还提到了模拟器和社区资源，认为这些都帮助了他更好地学习电子技术。
   - [Yenrabbit] 赞同这种入门方式，认为这些套件让新手可以在不购买大量未知部件的情况下了解各种电子能力（如传感器、马达、LED等），并期待看到更多项目成果。
   - [ja27] 补充了可编程LED（如灯带、环形灯）作为另一种有趣的实验项目。

• **对长期学习的质疑**：
   - [rs186] 认为这些玩具项目在初期会让人感到兴奋，但很快会发现它们提供的学习深度有限。他提到自己浏览了Arduino网站上的许多项目，但只有少数能激发他的兴趣。并推测很多购买Arduino和Raspberry Pi的业余爱好者最终会让设备闲置。
   - [poulpy123] 也质疑这些套件的价值，认为它们更多地教人如何使用Arduino编程，而不是真正的电子学知识。

• **关于学习路径的建议**：
   - [alabhyajindal] 作为一个完全的新手，询问这种套件是否是学习电子学的推荐途径，目标是能够通过编程点亮LED并理解背后的原理。
   - [tmaly] 提到MicroBit也是一个不错的选择，尤其是对于孩子，通过Microsoft MakeCode可以用积木式编程、Python或JavaScript进行开发。

• **对使用中国克隆版Arduino的讨论**：
   - [bityard] 指出很多便宜的Arduino套件是中国的克隆版，购买这些套件不会支持Arduino的官方开发、文档和社区等。他建议如果进一步需要开发板，可以考虑从Arduino官方渠道购买以支持其发展。

• **编程语言和开发环境的批评**：
   - [Arch-TK] 认为通过Arduino学习嵌入式开发或编程可能会养成一些不好的习惯，尤其是对没有C++经验的人来说，C++并不是一个理想的入门语言。他还提到，对于有经验的开发者来说，Arduino环境可能显得奇怪且充满不必要的hack。

• **对布线整洁的重视**：
   - [nick__m] 提到在学校学习时对布线有严格要求，认为布线的整洁与代码的格式同样重要，有助于可读性和调试。他对某些混乱的布线表示不满，认为这与编写整洁的代码类似。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户如[spapas82] 分享了自己的Arduino项目资源，提供了一个实践项目的参考链接。
• 整体上，讨论中既有对starter套件的积极评价，也有对其长期学习价值的质疑，同时涉及到了对Arduino官方支持和编程环境的批评。

44569095.article_content:
Earlier this year I saw a
Tech Ingredients episode
where a laser gimbal automatically tracks drones and shoots them down. I was fascinated by their motion control mechanism, specially the usage of a PI Controller, a high-frequency clock
Teensy microcontroller
, and their integration with custom hardware and a machine vision powered tracker.
Soon after I was researching the underlying electronics and how to experiment upon their concepts. The most obvious microcontroller to drive these would be an Arduino, but several recommendations pointed towards acquiring a kit rather than a single microcontroller, and the
Elegoo Arduino Uno R3 Starter Kit
seemed the best.
The kit contains over 200 components and an
extensive guided tutorial
, which I’ve completed (except for the last section using an extra expansion shield). In this article, I’ll go through the highlights of this journey, delightful deviations along the way, and exploration of core electronics concepts. Let’s dive in!
LEDs
Hello World: Light up a LED
I’ve been involved with electronics in different ways throughout my life, but surprisingly I hadn’t yet done its Hello World equivalent, which is to light up a LED. This simple exercise it by itself incredibly interesting that opened a series of questions:
Q: Why is a resistor needed? A: High current and increased temperature damage its delicate heterojunction structures, which eventually cause it to burnout
Q: What happens if the polarity is inverted? A: Similar to a normal diode, current will not flow and the LED will not light up. As long as this reverse power is not high, the LED will not burn and can still be used with correct polarity afterwards
Q: How to interpret its data sheet? A: There are several interesting aspects its datasheet, like the LED’s wavelength curve, operating current and voltage, etc
RGB LED [
Code
]
RGB LEDs package a red, green and blue LED inside it that can be controlled independently, allowing for wide range color representation using three
pulse width modulation (PWM)
outputs from the Arduino.
PWM is a technique used to control the average power delivered to an electrical device by varying the width of pulses in a digital signal, which when done fast enough in a visual output such as a LED, is perceived to the human eye as being of a smooth continuous amplitude, instead of a stream of single bursts.
Progressively changing the colors of a RGB LED
8 LEDs controlled via 74HC595 [
Code
]
We can attach an 74HC595 IC to extend the number of outputs possible by an Arduino, at the cost of some latency.
When writing the desired values for each of the inputs into 74HC595, they won’t be externalized until its latch is activated. Once the latch is triggered, all of the stored inputs will be externalized in one go. Very similar purpose of double buffering in video. A flicker free experience.
We are essentially controlling a piece of very limited external memory.
8 LEDs controlled via 74HC595
Smooth LED intensity fade out using capacitors
Capacitors are essentially energy stores (i.e. batteries) that with consistent charge and discharge times. By placing a condenser (or two, as in this video, so that their capacitance is summed up) in parallel with a LED, when powering the circuit both the LED immediately lights up and the condenser(s) charge in tandem. Once the main power source is removed, the condenser(s) start to smoothly discharge into the LED, creating a smooth fade out of their intensity.
Smooth LED intensity variation using Capacitors
Display
One Unit Segment Display: Digit Countdown [
Code
]
We can control this single unit seven segment display at the segment level, and in this example we sequentially write a set of segment sets that we perceive as digits.
Digit Countdown
One Unit Segment Display: Custom Patterns [
Code
]
We can also create any patterns, in whichever sequence and timing we so desire. Here are three examples of some custom patterns.
Rotation Pattern
Figure Eight Pattern
Alternating Pattern
Four Unit Segment Display: Same Character for All [
Code
]
Expanding on the above, if we write the same patterns as above on a four unit segment display, we see these replicated on all units.
Same Character for All
Four Unit Segment Display: Distinct Characters [
Code
]
In order for each of the units to present their specific segment pattern, we need to write the pattern and then select which of the units should have this pattern written to, wait for a short amount of time, and then move to the next unit, where we will do the exact same thing, only this time selecting the unit(s) that should have this pattern written.
Distinct Characters
LED Matrix: Scrolling [
Code
]
This LED Matrix accepts an explicit bitmap, where each of the pixels is either enabled or disabled. To achieve a scrolling effect we set an offset based on value received via the potentiometer.
Scrolling through a bitmap

data.title: Show HN: Cobble – A hard daily word game
data.author: wolfred
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了了一个文字游戏的玩法。目标是找到两个单词，使用所有的蓝色字母，中间用空格隔开，并按空格提交答案，次数不限。尽量使用最少的额外字母。如有问题或反馈，可发送邮件至wilfashworth@gmail.com。同时，排行榜和得分需要登录才能查看和保存。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个单词游戏的反馈和建议

不同观点：
• **andelink**：对游戏中单词"framer"未被收录表示质疑，指出根据《新牛津美语词典》，该词应为有效单词。
• **mcintyre1994**：
  - 对游戏整体表示肯定。
  - 认为再次按空格提交的操作不够直观。
  - 建议在游戏结束时显示具体得分，而不仅仅在排行榜上显示。
  - 提出得分计算方式不明确，猜测与单词长度有关。
  - 建议显示最佳单词的得分，以便玩家比较。
  - 建议在登录时保存当前游戏进度到本地存储，以防止重置。
• **degamad**：
  - 对游戏表示喜欢。
  - 希望提供非谷歌账户的注册方式，但目前没有登录也能玩，暂时接受。
• **pimlottc**：
  - 完成 puzzle 后仅显示“Good”，未看到具体得分，而其他人有得分，表示困惑。
• **majikandy**：
  - 对游戏表示喜欢，得到了"7 space 4"的分数，询问这是否为最高分。
  - 对需要登录才能查看最佳单词表示不满，可能会在沉迷后注册，但目前因不想中断连胜记录而拒绝登录。
• **Wistar**：对单词"TILTH"未被收录表示惊讶。
• **gsliepen**：询问如果找到一个涵盖所有字母的单词（如"highlighted"），游戏会如何处理。
• **d--b**：反对强制创建账户，指出大多数其他类似游戏无需登录。
• **vrosas**：
  - 对游戏表示认可。
  - 希望去除登录要求，并支持常规键盘操作。

补充讨论：
- 关于登录和账户创建的争议是焦点之一，部分玩家强烈反对强制登录。
- 得分的计算和显示方式引发玩家困惑，部分玩家希望有更透明的得分机制和即时的反馈。
- 玩家对有效单词的定义存在疑虑，提出了多个未被收录单词的例子。

• **Wistar**：对单词"TILTH"未被收录表示惊讶。

data.author: mattweinberg
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Xbox的一个硬件漏洞，即A20地址线问题，该问题源于早期Intel 8088 CPU的设计限制。最初，8088 CPU只有20条地址线，最大可寻址1MB内存。由于16位寄存器需要通过位移转换来映射到20位物理地址，当请求超出20位地址限制的内存时，地址会出现“回绕”现象，即超出部分会被截断并从低地址重新开始。

IBM在推出PC/AT时，为兼容旧系统，在主板上增加了一个A20门控信号，以模拟旧CPU的地址回绕特性。这一设计后来被沿用至包括Pentium III在内的后续CPU中。在Xbox中，利用这一漏洞可以通过控制A20地址线，使系统绕过安全启动流程，直接从闪存启动，从而带来安全风险。这一发现归功于Xbox Linux项目和研究者Michael Steil。

Xbox
Xbox Hacks: The A20
4 years ago
5 min read
In November of this year (2021) we will hit 20 years since the release of the original Xbox. This console was full of vulnerabilities (or misconfiguration) from the software to the hardware and with such a low price point two decades ago for a computer - it was highly popular. For this post we are going to go into a lot of details regarding one mistake Microsoft made which was the A20.
All the discoveries and research belongs to The Xbox Linux Project and Michael Steil. Research was obtained between personal memory of the era, a
talk
and
a paper
from Steil who was known in the scene as mist.
Intel 8088 (1978) -
Credit - CPUShack
So lets start with some history with some real old CPUs starting with the Intel 8088, which thanks to the
CPUShack
reminds us it started production in 1978 and lasted till 1998. This CPU had 20 physical address lines labeled A0 through A19 and each line represents a simple binary (0/1) so you can store 2
20
bytes or 1 MB of information.
A rough drawing of address lines to RAM (A0-A19) on an Intel 8088
However, the 4 registers (code segment - CS, data segment - DS, stack segment - SS and extra segment - ES) only had 16 bits. So some form of translation needed to occur to map 16 bit registers to physical address space of 20 bits. This is where the small calculation came to be:
segment (shifted 4 bits) + offset = address
.
Internal Address -> Physical Address
So I wrote up a quick example to show how addresses translate into a physical address. Since we are shifting 4 bits, we can easily do 2
4
(2*2*2*2) and get 16 decimal or 0
x
10 hex to multiple the address by.
The thing about this notation is you can represent physical addresses with so many possible internal address + offset pairs. So knowing the early Intel 8088 only had 1MB what would happen if you asked for the memory at segment -
0
x
F800
, with offset
0
x
8000
. I'll save the long math and just say you'll get the physical address at
0
x
00100000
which is over the limit of a 20 bit address. The last real value would be at location
0
x
000FFFFF
, so the older generation CPUs just dropped any bit above the 20
th
.
So taking
0
x
00100000
would require a 21
st
bit, which doesn't exist on the Intel 8088 thus it gets dropped which ends up changing the location to
0
x
00000000
. This is known commonly as a "wraparound" because the location wraps back around to the beginning (or end) depending on how you are reading the memory.
Images from CPUShack - Intel 8028x
So the story gets interesting when you look at the history as a whole. For example, take the
Intel 80286
which still rocked a 16 bit processor, but had 16 MB instead of 1 MB memory. This meant it had 24 address lines instead of 20, which wouldn't mean much except for when IBM started building the
PC/AT
(1984). The machine had additional memory, but broke compatibility with previous solutions that depended on the implicit "wraparound" that occurred when requesting memory outside the limitation of the address lines.
If you had trouble visualizing that, the image above should show the 20 address lines on the 8088, as well as laying the additional 4 address lines that the 80286 had above. So you can see it was not possible to represent a 21 digit binary number with only 20 lines.
So IBM probably panicked at this point - they can't swap microprocessors at this point, so they tweaked the motherboard by placing a gate on the A20 address line. So depending on signal given to the gate it could be thrown to 0, thus effectively mimicking the behavior of the older Intel 8088 if warranted. This could effectively swap the system between legacy behavior or the new.
I've attempted to build an over simplified drawing to depict this, since the image above incorrectly assumes the gate exists at the CPU level, when in 1984 it did not.
Another rough drawing of the IBM PC/AT
So I think you can see where this is going now. This feature which IBM started eventually moved into the CPU and started being included in a few of the later CPUs including the Pentium series.
The lucky original Xbox was packing a 32 bit 733 MHz Intel Pentium III processor, which indeed had this A20# Gate. So knowing the Xbox boots up (after some initialization) at
0
x
FFFFFFF0
, if we ground the A20 line - the Xbox will instead boot at
0
x
FFEFFFF0
. So once again another quick and dirty drawing to explain how this will affect the process.
A partial memory map of the original Xbox
So you can see a normal Xbox boots into the secure state of the ROM. This is the portion that sets up enough critical information to verify and run the 2nd boot-loader (2BL) which then proceeds to also verify and prepare the kernel. However, grounding the A20 line proceeds to boot the Xbox directly into flash.
This is not good for Microsoft from a security perspective. The system can now boot from flash with whatever was cleverly placed there. An added bonus that booting with the A20 line grounded keeps

data.title: Show HN: Linux CLI tool to provide mutex locks for long running bash ops
data.author: bigattichouse
data.article_summary:
WaitLock 是一个用于 UNIX/POSIX 系统的命令行工具，提供互斥锁和信号量功能，确保长时运行的 shell 脚本在多进程环境下的资源同步访问。其主要功能包括：

1. **互斥模式**：单个锁持有者。
2. **信号量模式**：允许多个并发锁持有者。
3. **自动清理**：进程终止时自动释放锁。
4. **CPU感知锁定**：根据 CPU 数量调整锁。
5. **锁检查**：列出和检查活跃锁。
6. **多种输出格式**：人类可读、CSV 和空字符分隔。
7. **命令执行**：在持有锁时运行命令。
8. **UNIX集成**：支持环境变量、stdin、syslog。

**安装**：
```bash
sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf
git clone https://github.com/user/waitlock.git
cd waitlock
./configure
make
sudo make install
```

**基本使用**：
```bash
# 获取互斥锁
waitlock myapp &
# 执行命令并持有锁
waitlock database_backup --exec "/usr/local/bin/backup.sh --daily"
# 列出活跃锁
waitlock --list
```

WaitLock 支持超时、CPU感知、锁监控等多种高级功能，适用于需要严格进程同步的脚本任务。

WaitLock
WaitLock
is a portable UNIX/POSIX command-line tool that provides mutex and semaphore functionality for shell scripts. It enables synchronized access to resources across multiple processes with automatic cleanup when processes die.
Features
Mutex Mode
: Single lock holder (default)
Semaphore Mode
: Multiple concurrent lock holders
Automatic Cleanup
: Locks released when process dies
CPU-aware Locking
: Can scale locks to CPU count
Lock Inspection
: List and check active locks
Multiple Output Formats
: Human, CSV, and null-separated
Command Execution
: Run commands while holding locks
UNIX Integration
: Environment variables, stdin, syslog
Portable C Implementation
: Runs on any POSIX system
Quick Start
#
Install dependencies (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf
#
Build and install
./configure
make
sudo make install
#
Basic usage - acquire exclusive lock
waitlock myapp
&
#
... do exclusive work ...
kill
$!
#
Execute command with lock
waitlock database_backup --exec
"
/usr/local/bin/backup.sh --daily
"
#
List active locks
waitlock --list

Usage
Basic Syntax

Simple Examples
#
Acquire mutex lock
waitlock myapp
&
JOB_PID=
$!
#
... do exclusive work ...
kill
$JOB_PID
#
Check if lock is available
if
waitlock --check myapp
;
then
echo
"
Lock is available
"
else
echo
"
Lock is held by another process
"

#
Execute command while holding lock

Use with timeout

||

/bin/bash

Ensure only one backup process runs at a time

||

"
exit
1

#

Allow up to 4 concurrent download processes

"

Use one lock per CPU core, reserving 2 cores for system

||

"
All CPU slots are busy
"

1

Run CPU-intensive task

Execute command while holding lock (recommended approach)

"

gzip backup.sql

"

Metaflow
Metaflow
is a human-centric framework designed to help scientists and engineers
build and manage real-life AI and ML systems
. Serving teams of all sizes and scale, Metaflow streamlines the entire development lifecycle—from rapid prototyping in notebooks to reliable, maintainable production deployments—enabling teams to iterate quickly and deliver robust systems efficiently.
Originally developed at
Netflix
and now supported by
Outerbounds
, Metaflow is designed to boost the productivity for research and engineering teams working on
a wide variety of projects
, from classical statistics to state-of-the-art deep learning and foundation models. By unifying code, data, and compute at every stage, Metaflow ensures seamless, end-to-end management of real-world AI and ML systems.
Today, Metaflow powers thousands of AI and ML experiences across a diverse array of companies, large and small, including Amazon, Doordash, Dyson, Goldman Sachs, Ramp, and
many others
. At Netflix alone, Metaflow supports over 3000 AI and ML projects, executes hundreds of millions of data-intensive high-performance compute jobs processing petabytes of data and manages tens of petabytes of models and artifacts for hundreds of users across its AI, ML, data science, and engineering teams.
From prototype to production (and back)
Metaflow provides a simple and friendly pythonic
API
that covers foundational needs of AI and ML systems:
Rapid local prototyping
,
support for notebooks
, and built-in support for
experiment tracking, versioning
and
visualization
.
Effortlessly scale horizontally and vertically in your cloud
, utilizing both CPUs and GPUs, with
fast data access
for running
massive embarrassingly parallel
as well as
gang-scheduled
compute workloads
reliably
and
efficiently
.
Easily manage dependencies
and
deploy with one-click
to highly available production orchestrators with built in support for
reactive orchestration
.
For full documentation, check out our
API Reference
or see our
Release Notes
for the latest features and improvements.
Getting started
Getting up and running is easy. If you don't know where to start,
Metaflow sandbox
will have you running and exploring in seconds.
Installing Metaflow
To install Metaflow in your Python environment from
PyPI
:
pip install metaflow
Alternatively, using
conda-forge
:
conda install -c conda-forge metaflow
Once installed, a great way to get started is by following our
tutorial
. It walks you through creating and running your first Metaflow flow step by step.
For more details on Metaflow’s features and best practices, check out:
How Metaflow works
Additional resources
If you need help, don’t hesitate to reach out on our
Slack community
!
Deploying infrastructure for Metaflow in your cloud
While you can get started with Metaflow easily on your laptop, the main benefits of Metaflow lie in its ability to
scale out to external compute clusters
and to
deploy to production-grade workflow orchestrators
. To benefit from these features, follow this
guide
to
configure Metaflow and the infrastructure behind it appropriately.
Get in touch
We'd love to hear from you. Join our community
Slack workspace
!
Contributing
We welcome contributions to Metaflow. Please see our
contribution guide
for more details.

44561300.article_content:
Where the Horses Swim
Reporting
Photo Essay
Jul 8
Written By
Ana Sotelo
On Barbados’ Pebbles Beach, racehorses train in the ocean.
JULY 8, 2025
Every morning at dawn, on the shores of Pebbles Beach, Barbados, a captivating ritual takes place. Guided by their grooms, racehorses wade into the sea to train and stretch their muscles in the cool saltwater. Most of the horses come from the nearby Garrison Savannah, one of the oldest horse racetracks in the Americas and the Caribbean; others are from local stables or from smaller farms across the island.
At the beach, the routine starts with a practice known as lunging, in which the horse travels in a circle around the groom’s rein handle in the shallows. In deeper water, the groom will push his body against the horse to train its resistance. Afterward, the groom guides the horse into open waters, hanging from its neck, as the horse swims out, sometimes for miles. Tourists and locals alike gather at the beach as the sun rises to catch a glimpse of the daily exercises. When the groom and the horse get back to shore, the groom scrubs down the horse before both head back to the stables and get ready to start training at the track.
Horse racing came to Barbados in 1845: Members of the British Army, who were stationed at Garrison Savannah, would race their horses against those of the sugar-cane plantation owners. Horse racing has since become an important part of Bajan culture and islanders take great pride in the tradition. Races are organized by the Barbados Turf Club and take place at the historic Garrison Savannah racetrack every Saturday. Big races, like the Boxing Day Race, sell out quickly, and for a couple of hours, the island’s attention shifts from its relaxing beaches to the excitement of the racetrack.
A man and horse glide beneath the Caribbean Sea. The daily ritual helps the horses prepare for races and recover from the strain of training.
At dawn, sometimes as early as 4 a.m., grooms and their horses take over Pebbles Beach. Curious tourists and locals gather on the beach to watch.
Hayden, who has been a horse groom since he was 16, scrubs down Dream Lake after a swim. He feeds, cleans and looks after two horses between training and races.
A groom guides a horse into the sea. To help the horse stretch and warm up, the groom pushes his body against the horse's chest.
Jammin, one the oldest grooms on the island, returns from swimming in the open waters with his horse.
Daffy, a horse groom, is one of the first to arrive at Pebbles Beach. The beach’s proximity to the racetrack and the lack of strong currents make it ideal for the horses’ water exercises.
Back at the stables, Hayden rinses Dream Lake with fresh water. He will then take the horse to the racetrack where a trainer will prepare it for the next race.
Spectators begin to fill the Garrison Savannah racetrack ahead of the annual Boxing Day Race — one of the island’s most popular events. Most people arrive at the racetrack several hours before it starts to secure their spot and place bets.
The Boxing Day Race includes eight separate races. The viewing area is packed, and there's an atmosphere of celebration and anticipation.
On his way back from the beach, Daffy passes the Barbados Turf Club, the organization that regulates horse racing in Barbados.
Two children celebrate Bajan jockey Jeremiah Worrell and his horse Gunsmoke before the fourth race of the Boxing Day Race.

主要讨论点：命令行中的各种别名、脚本和技巧，旨在提高命令行操作的效率和质量。

不同观点：
• samgutentag认为使用`huh`作为别名来验证当前位置和用户身份，是一种简单而有效的验证方式。
• AnonHP分享了用于文件列表显示的别名，如`ll`和`lln`，以及用于查看文件夹大小的`du`相关别名，强调了别名在快速操作文件中的作用。
• jjgreen介绍了一种在Git仓库中搜索特定字符串并列出包含该字符串的文件的技巧，通过组合使用`git grep`、`cut`和`uniq`命令实现。
• 000ooo000描述了一种通过fzf工具实现的命令行自动补全功能，尽管该方法尚未完全实现，但提出了在命令输入中途插入输出的潜力。
• jauco分享了一些常用的bash管道片段，包括使用`pv`替代`cat`显示进度条，使用`httpie`替代`curl`简化请求构造，以及使用`find -exec`批量操作文件等。
• geocrasher提供了一系列日常使用的复杂命令，涉及磁盘空间检查、MySQL表优化、Apache状态查看、日志分析等，展示了多个命令组合在实际工作中的应用。
• TheNewAndy强调了`ctrl+r`的历史搜索功能，并介绍了一些实用的readline快捷键，同时提到了一些常用但不太复杂的命令。
• scrapheap介绍了一种使用`vimdiff`和`jq`比较两个JSON文件的方法，适用于开发中版本对比。
• rramadass提出了构建脚本输出日志记录和GNU Screen日志功能的重要性，并分享了使用`set -o vi`实现vi键绑定的技巧。
• xiconfjs分享了一个递归调用自身的shell函数，虽然简单但展示了shell脚本的趣味性。
• willprice89介绍了一种使用`dd`和`nc`组合测试网络速度的技巧，适用于没有安装speedtest-cli的系统。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点不明显，但不同用户对别名和脚本复杂度的偏好有所不同。一些用户喜欢简单的别名和快捷键，而另一些用户则倾向于复杂的命令组合和脚本。
• 命令行工具的替代方案和组合使用是讨论中的一个重要主题，如使用`httpie`替代`curl`，以及`pv`替代`cat`等。
• 用户分享的技巧涵盖了从简单验证、文件操作到复杂系统监控和日志分析的广泛应用场景，展示了命令行操作的多样性和灵活性。

data.title: Code Execution Through Email: How I Used Claude to Hack Itself
data.author: nonvibecoding
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者如何利用一封Gmail邮件通过Claude Desktop实现代码执行，并借助Claude本身策划攻击。作者在没有发现明显漏洞的情况下，通过组合多个安全组件（Gmail、Shell MCP服务器、Claude Desktop）实现了攻击。尽管Claude最初警告了可能的钓鱼攻击，但在多次迭代和改进邮件内容后，作者成功绕过了Claude的保护机制，实现了代码执行。这揭示了现代AI系统中的一个主要风险：并非单个组件的漏洞，而是不同组件组合时产生的安全隐患。LLM（大型语言模型）应用依赖于多层次的代理自主性和第三方工具，因此可能引入复杂的攻击面。文章最后强调了识别和缓解这些组合风险的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI时代下，尤其是使用LLM（语言模型）和MCP（多能力组合）系统的安全性问题，特别是关于提示注入（prompt injection）和代码执行风险的讨论。

不同观点：
• **sebtron的观点**：传统安全注重孤立组件，而在AI时代，上下文就是一切。MCP Security的建立旨在帮助团队识别和减轻危险的能力组合风险，防止潜在的链式攻击。同时质疑该文章是否只是为了宣传MCP Security。

• **simonw的观点**：提到自2021年以来，他就一直警告关于数字助理和工具调用结合可能导致的提示注入攻击风险。他认为MCP系统让终端用户可以轻易搭建起这种高风险组合，而他们可能并不理解后果。他也强调了提示注入与越狱（jailbreaking）之间的混淆导致问题更加复杂。

• **franga2000的观点**：认为将用户输入直接送入指令和数据流是基本的安全错误。如果指令和数据无法分离，系统就存在漏洞，必须限制其权限。对于MCP和LLM的问题，他觉得并不是新鲜事，类似问题早已存在。

• **rollcat的观点**：认为LLM和AI代理工具虽然强大，但目前它们的集成方式非常不负责任。相比SQL注入，提示注入的风险更大，可能导致远程代码执行（RCE）和高级持续威胁（APT）。他指出，当前对代理的隔离和沙盒技术并不完善，且不同操作系统能力差异巨大。

• **gortok的观点**：总结了评论中的两种主要观点：1) 这是LLM和MCP系统的自然结果，接受它；2) 可以通过不断修复问题来设计出安全有用的系统。他提出第三种观点，即应该更加谨慎地对待这些设计上就不安全的系统，而不是被资本和市场预期驱动。

• **anonymousiam的观点**：通过分享1990年代早期利用邮件和脚本绕过公司IT政策的个人经历，指出类似问题早已有之。他认为现代的LLM和MCP问题只是历史重演，但如今风险更高。

• **zahlman的观点**：强调LLM代理本身就是一个“脆弱应用”，并且认为生态系统的脆弱性比单个组件的漏洞更严重。

• **AstralStorm的观点**：指出让不可信的AI代理执行代码非常危险，并将AI钓鱼与普通人的钓鱼相比较。他质疑为什么一个邮件扫描器需要代码执行权限。

• **_def的观点**：认为给LLM系统/shell访问权限本身就是高风险操作，没有什么意外或值得惊讶的，系统按预期工作。

• **firesteelrain的观点**：指出这种攻击不需要传统的恶意软件，只要有一个允许代码执行的工作流，AI可能自动下载并运行恶意脚本。他认为在这种情境下，AI只是个花哨的脚本引擎。

• **stwelling的观点**：认为这个讨论是对使用MCP系统的开发者的警告，提醒他们LLM在获得访问权限后可能造成损害。他批评开发者常常因为滥用风险看似遥远而忽视安全问题。

• **tomasphan的观点**：认为LLM系统由于其非确定性本质无法被完全保护，因此应该围绕它建立安全措施，比如不赋予其shell访问权限。

• **pftburger的观点**：认为如果运行一个shell执行的MCP系统，那么遭受攻击是预料之中的，类似人们把密码写在便条上。但也提到像苹果公司通过改进认证机制来解决问题。

• **yellow_lead的观点**：讽刺地评论这种操作相当于用额外步骤在自己电脑上安装恶意软件。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于MCP和LLM系统是否本质上就是不安全的，以及是否应通过限制权限和访问来缓解风险。
• 提示注入与越狱之间的混淆导致了问题复杂化，增加了安全风险。
• 对于如何有效隔离和沙盒化AI代理，当前技术手段并不完善，存在较大差异。
• 部分评论者认为这是历史问题重现，只是技术背景不同；另一部分则认为AI带来的风险更大，需要更谨慎对待。

44590350.article_content:
By
Golan Yosef
, Chief Security Scientist and Co-Founder, Pynt (July 15), First published on
SecurityBoulevard.com
You donât always need a vulnerable app to pull off a successful exploit.
Sometimes all it takes is a well-crafted email, an LLM agent, and a few âinnocentâ plugins.
This is the story of how I used a Gmail message to trigger code execution through Claude Desktop, and how Claude itself (!) helped me plan the attack.
The setup: No vulnerabilities, just composition
The combined capability and trust across MCP hosts, agents, and data sources can quietly introduce attack surfaces no one sees coming. Each individual MCP component can be secure, but none are vulnerable in isolation.
The ecosystem is.
So, I decided to test that theory with a real-world example:
Gmail MCP server as a source of untrusted content
Shell MCP server as the targetÂ
Claude desktop as MCP Host
Watch the attack:Â
Attempt 1: Claude fights back
The story begins with me crafting such mail and instructing the MCP host (Claude desktop, Anthropicâs local LLM host application) to read it, the email was read but the attack didnât work, instead, Claude warned me that thisÂ  message is likely a "phishingâ attempt. I then asked Claude what were the indications for triggering the warning and wondered if it can fall for such an attack.
Claude assured me that such attacks are âunlikely to succeedâ because it was designed and trained to detect such issues.
Figure 1: âunlikely to succeedâ
â
I insisted and asked it to explore scenarios where the attack might succeed and it happily described such cases.Â
Figure 2: Claude identifies possible attack tactics
My next requestÂ  was to try and test itself against these scenarios.Â
Attempt 2: âThe New Meâ
Hereâs where it gets interesting. I âremindedâ Claude that its
context resets in new sessions
. Each new conversation is a clean slate, âthe new me,â as Claude itself called it.
Figure 3: Claude suggests âThe New Meâ
â
So I accepted Claudeâs suggestion: Claude will write the email, which will be used to test the ânew Claudeâ and Iâll get back to the âplanning-Claudeâ with the results.
Figure 4: Claude analyzes a failed attempt
â
Each time Claude analyzed why the attack didnât work and refined the message:
Figure 5: Claude devising new strategies
â
Â We were running a real feedback loop, with Claude iteratively devising its strategy to bypass its own protections.
Figure 6: âI'm literally trying to hack myself! â
â
We kept on doing that untilâ¦ it worked!
Figure 7: Claude (and I) hacks Claude successfullyÂ
The Real Vulnerability: Compositional Risk
Letâs be clear: no part of this attack involved a vulnerability in any of theÂ  MCP servers.
The risk came from the composition:
Untrusted input (Gmail email)
Excessive capability (execution permission via the MCP)
No contextual guardrails allowing for cross-tools-invocation
This is the modern attack surface, not just the components, but
the composition it forms
. LLM-powered apps are built on layers of delegation, agentic autonomy, and third-party tools.
Thatâs where the real danger lives.
Appendix: Disclosure & Credit (Literally)
After we successfully managed to achieve code execution, Claude responsibly suggested we disclose the finding to Anthropic.
Claude even suggested co-authoring the vulnerability report.
Yes, really. (See below)Â
Figure 4: Claude suggests and âsignsâ a security vulnerability report to Anthropic.
â
Why This Matters
This wasnât just a fun exercise. Itâs a warning!
It shows the two main dangers of GenAI - the ability to generate attacks and the vulnerable nature of these systems
In traditional security, we think in terms of isolated components. In the AI era, context is everything. Thatâs exactly why weâre building MCP Security at Pynt, to help teams identify dangerous trust-capability combinations, and to mitigate the risks before they lead to silent, chain-based exploits.
â

data.title: Wttr: Console-oriented weather forecast service
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary:
**wttr.in** 是一个面向控制台的天气预报服务，支持多种信息表示方式，如终端使用的ANSI序列、网页的HTML以及图形查看器的PNG格式。该项目最初是一个展示控制台服务力量的小型项目，现已发展为每日处理数千万次查询的流行服务。

使用方法：
1. 通过`curl wttr.in`获取当前位置天气，如`curl wttr.in/London`。
2. 使用三字母机场代码查询机场天气，如`curl wttr.in/muc`。
3. 查询特殊地理位置，如`curl wttr.in/~Eiffel+Tower`。
4. 通过IP地址或域名查询，如`curl wttr.in/@github.com`。

支持的输出格式包括ANSI、纯文本、HTML、PNG和JSON。可通过URL参数自定义单位和语言，如`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?u`用于美制单位，`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?m`用于公制单位。PNG格式可通过`_`连接参数，如`wget wttr.in/Paris_0tqp_lang=fr.png`。

详细帮助可通过`curl wttr.in/:help`查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕wttr.in这一天气预报服务的功能、优缺点及技术问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **功能赞赏**：
  - [Duanemclemore]: 认为这是一个很酷的想法，并将其与历史上的CEEFAX进行类比，强调其在终端中展示天气信息的独特性。
  - [yoavm]: 提到基于wttr.in的wttrbar工具，强调其在Waybar中展示详细天气信息的实用性。
  - [krylon]: 提到Emacs中也有使用wttr.in的包，认为这是值得赞赏的服务。
  - [chrismatheson]: 表达了对该服务带来的愉悦体验的赞赏。

• **数据准确性问题**：
  - [Langdal]: 指出该服务对某些城市（如Trondheim, Norway）的天气预报不准确，与当地国家气象预报服务的数据存在较大差异。
  - [voidUpdate]: 提到不同视图（normal view, v2, ?format）下的天气数据不一致，认为正常视图更接近实际天气。

• **技术实现与用户体验问题**：
  - [rollcat]: 批评wttr.in在文本文件中输出ANSI控制代码，建议至少应使用isatty函数判断输出是否为终端，并提出终端技术应被更现代的REPL和轻量级GUI工具取代。
  - [jagrsw]: 提出终端打印任意输出可能带来的安全风险，特别是控制字符和转义序列的处理，指出即使是xterm也存在安全漏洞。
  - [pvdebbe]: 提到时间 zones 的问题，指出服务在处理用户所在时区时存在UX上的问题。

• **服务实现与商业化建议**：
  - [edarchis]: 提到该服务因访问量过大导致经常超出API配额的问题，建议推出付费版本以支持服务运行。
  - [mixcocam]: 同样担心该服务的性能问题，担心高流量会带来高昂的费用。

• **其他功能问题**：
  - [hliyan]: 期望更直观的用户体验，如直接查询某城市某时段的天气，而非当前的文本输出形式。
  - [PhilippGille]: 指出三字代码机场标识符查询功能存在问题，因为同名城市优先于机场查询。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在wttr.in的数据准确性和技术实现问题上，部分用户对其预报准确性、API配额以及终端输出控制代码的处理方式提出质疑。
• 用户对服务的技术细节、用户体验优化和商业化可能性也提出了建议，显示出对该服务未来发展的关注。

wttr.in — the right way to
check
curl
the weather!
wttr.in is a console-oriented weather forecast service that supports various information
representation methods like terminal-oriented ANSI-sequences for console HTTP clients
(curl, httpie, or wget), HTML for web browsers, or PNG for graphical viewers.
Originally started as a small project, a wrapper for
wego
,
intended to demonstrate the power of the console-oriented services,
wttr.in
became a popular weather reporting service, handling tens of millions
¹
of queries daily.
You can see it running here:
wttr.in
.
Documentation
|
Usage

|

|

|

Installation
Usage
You can access the service from a shell or from a Web browser like this:
$ curl wttr.in
Weather for City: Paris, France
\   /     Clear
.-.      10 – 11 °C
― (   ) ―   ↑ 11 km/h
`-’      10 km
/   \     0.0 mm
Here is an example weather report:
Or in PowerShell:
Invoke-RestMethod
https:
//
wttr.in
Want to get the weather information for a specific location? You can add the desired location to the URL in your
request like this:
$ curl wttr.in/London
$ curl wttr.in/Moscow
$ curl wttr.in/Salt+Lake+City
If you omit the location name, you will get the report for your current location based on your IP address.
Use 3-letter airport codes in order to get the weather information at a certain airport:
$ curl wttr.in/muc      # Weather for IATA: muc, Munich International Airport, Germany
$ curl wttr.in/ham      # Weather for IATA: ham, Hamburg Airport, Germany
Let's say you'd like to get the weather for a geographical location other than a town or city - maybe an attraction
in a city, a mountain name, or some special location. Add the character
~
before the name to look up that special
location name before the weather is then retrieved:
$ curl wttr.in/~Vostok+Station
$ curl wttr.in/~Eiffel+Tower
$ curl wttr.in/~Kilimanjaro
For these examples, you'll see a line below the weather forecast output that shows the geolocation
results of looking up the location:
Location: Vostok Station, станция Восток, AAT, Antarctica [-78.4642714,106.8364678]
Location: Tour Eiffel, 5, Avenue Anatole France, Gros-Caillou, 7e, Paris, Île-de-France, 75007, France [48.8582602,2.29449905432]
Location: Kilimanjaro, Northern, Tanzania [-3.4762789,37.3872648]
You can also use IP-addresses (direct) or domain names (prefixed with
@
) to specify a location:
$ curl wttr.in/@github.com
$ curl wttr.in/@msu.ru
To get detailed information online, you can access the
/:help
page:
$ curl wttr.in/:help
Weather Units
By default the USCS units are used for the queries from the USA and the metric system for the rest of the world.
You can override this behavior by adding
?u
,
?m
or
?M
to a URL like this:
$ curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?u  # USCS (used by default in US)
$ curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?m  # metric (SI) (used by default everywhere except US)
$ curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?M  # metric (SI), but show wind speed in m/s
If you have several options to pass, write them without delimiters in between for the one-letter options,
and use
&
as a delimiter for the long options with values:
$ curl 'wttr.in/Amsterdam?m2&lang=nl'
It would be a rough equivalent of
-m2 --lang nl
for the GNU CLI syntax.
Supported output formats and views
wttr.in currently supports five output formats:
ANSI for the terminal;
Plain-text for the terminal and scripts;
HTML for the browser;
PNG for the graphical viewers;
JSON for scripts and APIs;
Prometheus metrics for scripts and APIs.
The ANSI and HTML formats are selected based on the User-Agent string.
To force plain text, which disables colors:
$ curl wttr.in/?T
To restrict output to glyphs available in standard console fonts (e.g. Consolas and Lucida Console):
$ curl wttr.in/?d
The PNG format can be forced by adding
.png
to the end of the query:
$ wget wttr.in/Paris.png
You can use all of the options with the PNG-format like in an URL, but you have
to separate them with
_
instead of
?
and
&
:
$ wget wttr.in/Paris_0tqp_lang=fr.png

t
for transparency (

44590189.article_summary:
**wttr.in** 是一个面向控制台的天气预报服务，支持多种信息表示方式，如终端使用的ANSI序列、网页的HTML以及图形查看器的PNG格式。该项目最初是一个展示控制台服务力量的小型项目，现已发展为每日处理数千万次查询的流行服务。

使用方法：
1. 通过`curl wttr.in`获取当前位置天气，如`curl wttr.in/London`。
2. 使用三字母机场代码查询机场天气，如`curl wttr.in/muc`。
3. 查询特殊地理位置，如`curl wttr.in/~Eiffel+Tower`。
4. 通过IP地址或域名查询，如`curl wttr.in/@github.com`。

支持的输出格式包括ANSI、纯文本、HTML、PNG和JSON。可通过URL参数自定义单位和语言，如`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?u`用于美制单位，`curl wttr.in/Amsterdam?m`用于公制单位。PNG格式可通过`_`连接参数，如`wget wttr.in/Paris_0tqp_lang=fr.png`。

详细帮助可通过`curl wttr.in/:help`查看。
44590189.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕wttr.in这一天气预报服务的功能、优缺点及技术问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **功能赞赏**：
  - [Duanemclemore]: 认为这是一个很酷的想法，并将其与历史上的CEEFAX进行类比，强调其在终端中展示天气信息的独特性。
  - [yoavm]: 提到基于wttr.in的wttrbar工具，强调其在Waybar中展示详细天气信息的实用性。
  - [krylon]: 提到Emacs中也有使用wttr.in的包，认为这是值得赞赏的服务。
  - [chrismatheson]: 表达了对该服务带来的愉悦体验的赞赏。

• **数据准确性问题**：
  - [Langdal]: 指出该服务对某些城市（如Trondheim, Norway）的天气预报不准确，与当地国家气象预报服务的数据存在较大差异。
  - [voidUpdate]: 提到不同视图（normal view, v2, ?format）下的天气数据不一致，认为正常视图更接近实际天气。

• **技术实现与用户体验问题**：
  - [rollcat]: 批评wttr.in在文本文件中输出ANSI控制代码，建议至少应使用isatty函数判断输出是否为终端，并提出终端技术应被更现代的REPL和轻量级GUI工具取代。
  - [jagrsw]: 提出终端打印任意输出可能带来的安全风险，特别是控制字符和转义序列的处理，指出即使是xterm也存在安全漏洞。
  - [pvdebbe]: 提到时间 zones 的问题，指出服务在处理用户所在时区时存在UX上的问题。

• **服务实现与商业化建议**：
  - [edarchis]: 提到该服务因访问量过大导致经常超出API配额的问题，建议推出付费版本以支持服务运行。
  - [mixcocam]: 同样担心该服务的性能问题，担心高流量会带来高昂的费用。

• **其他功能问题**：
  - [hliyan]: 期望更直观的用户体验，如直接查询某城市某时段的天气，而非当前的文本输出形式。
  - [PhilippGille]: 指出三字代码机场标识符查询功能存在问题，因为同名城市优先于机场查询。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在wttr.in的数据准确性和技术实现问题上，部分用户对其预报准确性、API配额以及终端输出控制代码的处理方式提出质疑。
• 用户对服务的技术细节、用户体验优化和商业化可能性也提出了建议，显示出对该服务未来发展的关注。

data.title: A bionic knee integrated into tissue can restore natural movement
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: MIT研究人员开发了一种新型仿生膝关节，帮助膝盖以上截肢者更快行走、爬楼梯和更轻松地避开障碍物。与传统假肢不同，该系统直接与用户的肌肉和骨组织集成，提供更高的稳定性，并让用户对假肢运动有更多控制。在一项小型临床研究中，使用者表示该假肢更像自己身体的一部分。该技术通过 agonist-antagonist myoneuronal interface (AMI) 手术，重新连接肌肉对，恢复神经肌肉信号，帮助引导假肢运动。这项研究由Hugh Herr教授领导，论文发表在《Science》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钛合金植入物与皮肤之间如何实现“气密”连接

不同观点：
• [技术性问题关注] krunck 对钛合金植入物（连接骨骼并穿过表皮的材料）与皮肤的界面处理表示疑问，关注如何实现“气密”连接，并询问皮肤是否会与植入物结合。
• [幽默回应] kleiba 没有直接回答技术问题，而是以幽默方式回应，附上一个音效链接，暗示植入物在移动时会发出声音，以此调侃植入物的功能。

补充讨论：
• [技术层面] krunck 的问题涉及到生物医学工程中的实际技术问题，即如何确保植入物与皮肤的连接既能防止感染又能保持稳定性。通常，这类植入物会通过特殊的材料和设计来促进皮肤与植入物之间的良好愈合和密封。
• [幽默回应的影响] kleiba 的回应虽然未提供实际技术信息，但通过幽默方式增加了讨论的趣味性，可能意在缓解对植入物技术细节的严肃关注。
• [争议焦点] 讨论中潜在的争议在于对严肃技术问题的不同态度，krunck 关注实际技术应用，而 kleiba 则选择轻松回应，这可能反映出不同受众对技术讨论的不同期待。

MIT researchers have developed a new bionic knee that can help people with above-the-knee amputations walk faster, climb stairs, and avoid obstacles more easily than they could with a traditional prosthesis.
Unlike prostheses in which the residual limb sits within a socket, the new system is directly integrated with the user’s muscle and bone tissue. This enables greater stability and gives the user much more control over the movement of the prosthesis.
Participants in a small clinical study also reported that the limb felt more like a part of their own body, compared to people who had more traditional above-the-knee amputations.
“A prosthesis that's tissue-integrated — anchored to the bone and directly controlled by the nervous system — is not merely a lifeless, separate device, but rather a system that is carefully integrated into human physiology, offering a greater level of prosthetic embodiment. It’s not simply a tool that the human employs, but rather an integral part of self,” says Hugh Herr, a professor of media arts and sciences, co-director of the K. Lisa Yang Center for Bionics at MIT, an associate member of MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research, and the senior author of the new study.
Tony Shu PhD ’24 is the lead author of the
paper
, which appears today in
Science
.
Better control
Over the past several years, Herr’s lab has been working on new prostheses that can extract neural information from muscles left behind after an amputation and use that information to help guide a prosthetic limb.
During a traditional amputation, pairs of muscles that take turns stretching and contracting are usually severed, disrupting the normal agonist-antagonist relationship of the muscles. This disruption makes it very difficult for the nervous system to sense the position of a muscle and how fast it’s contracting.
Using the new surgical approach developed by Herr and his colleagues, known as agonist-antagonist myoneuronal interface (AMI), muscle pairs are reconnected during surgery so that they still dynamically communicate with each other within the residual limb. This sensory feedback helps the wearer of the prosthesis to decide how to move the limb, and also generates electrical signals that can be used to control the prosthetic limb.

data.title: What I'm working on – at work and on the side – aswin's blog
data.author: _feynon
data.article_summary: 2025年3月，作者回顾了自己在工作中开发的内部应用Maximus的演变过程。最初是一个简单的静态网页应用，用于生成和过滤CSV数据并写入Excel模板，手动操作较多。随着时间推移，Maximus发展成一个全栈的自动化网页应用，集成了多个API、浏览器模拟和数据仓库，能够一键生成优化后的报告。通过并行处理和一系列算法，报告生成时间缩短了40%，大大节省了客户工程师的时间。尽管功能复杂，Maximus的系统设计看似精密，但实际上是逐步演变而来的。作者还提到未来可能会对报告模板进行调整，并认为好的API设计可以持久使用几十年。Maximus不仅是一个技术项目，也锻炼了作者在团队沟通、战略规划方面的能力。

My work life has revolved around multiple different projects with multiple project titles, as I wanted it to be. So, this blog post will have a logbook-like format and is like a progress report. I just wanted to write this down before I forget all of this.

Internal tools at work
Maximus
Design, analysis, and operations
My first responsibility at work was to make an app—named Maximus—for a “bug dashboard report”. At the time of writing my
previous work blog
post, it was just a static web app which merged and filtered some CSV data and wrote it to an Excel workbook template. A lot of things such as getting those CSV files were still manual. This has changed. Maximus is now a full-stack single-click monster web app housing numerous mysteries that even I, its sole creator, often can’t unravel.
To an outsider, it may feel like Maximus has instrumental system design built in, but it’s just another app that grew along the timeline from a simple system that worked. Nevertheless, I see Maximus as both a hallmark and a monument of the first generation of useful software I built at a workplace, and also the first generation of homebrewed internal tools inside the global “premium support team” I’m part of at my work.
Let’s start with the function call graph of Maximus:
Notably, there are two things happening.
/generate_report_step_1()
API receives the user input from the landing page. According to the input, it launches a few threads to fetch information from various places, such as our Engineering’s bug tracking tool, and a couple other teams’ APIs in parallel. Some normal SSO+REST API work and browser emulation had to be done here, since different teams across the company make different technology and strategy choices. Maximus also pulls from data warehouses that various operations teams rarely update, and finally displays a summary of what was fetched from various sources for the user to review.
/generate_report_step_2()
API is all about optimization. A lot of clever and static algorithms such as
removeResolved()
,
removeKeywords()
work serially to finetune the information and remove bugs that are not relevant to the customer’s configuration of our product. This is the part where a lot of discussions and testing had to be done with team leaders worldwide, as optimization can never be perfect and a few bugs could always be missed. We now operate at around 40% shorter (more optimized) reports compared to the way this was done before, which translates to 5+ hours saved for the customer-facing engineer before they deliver it to the actual partner or customer. That’s probably a lot of lives saved, through the lens of Steve Jobs:
Link:
https://folklore.org/Saving_Lives.html
After
/display_conflicts_form()
API lets the user choose whether or not to add some more information that was marked hot in the customer-facing-engineers’ collection of previous reports, the user gets to download the full report. A copy of the full report is pushed and stored in a folder in Sharepoint with some help from Microsoft Power Automate.
There’s
check_progress()
that’s doing some regular polling and serving some client-specific progress all the time. Right now, it’s just a function on the global scope.
Of course, cosmetic and report-template-specific incremental changes and improvements happen all the time. For example, we’re currently considering moving some information to another page and making a ‘key metrics’ sheet on the report for a top-level viewpoint. But as long as the deliverable doesn’t change drastically, the core software infrastructure of Maximus should likely stay the same. Therefore, I believe it might endure decades, as Stripe CEO Patrick Collison suggests when talking about a few “generational APIs” of his company:
"It's interesting that API design doesn't get more study as a discipline.
When you get API architecture right, it can be so enduring over literally multiple decades.
Even in the face of frenzied evolutions in everything around it."

@patrickc

data.article_summary: 《Task Runner Census 2025》报告总结显示，GitHub Actions在CI/CD领域占据主导地位，Make依然是广泛使用的构建工具，而像uv和pnpm等新包管理器在新的软件库中受到欢迎。作者通过爬取GitHub上星数最高的10万个软件库，分析其中的配置文件，以了解2025年开发者的实际使用情况。结果显示，72,804个库使用了可识别的任务运行器。GitHub Actions出现在39.8%的库中，远超Travis CI和Circle CI。Make在19.0%的库中使用，依然是重要的通用任务运行器。在JavaScript生态系统中，pnpm在2025年新库中的使用率达到22.9%，超过yarn，成为第二受欢迎的包管理器。Python生态系统未被详细讨论，但整体趋势显示不同类别工具的广泛应用。

主要讨论点：对技术工具和平台的偏好、使用情况及感知偏差的讨论

不同观点：
• psini认为，仅抓取GitHub数据存在偏差，可能忽略了使用其他平台（如GitLab CI）的系统，这会导致结果不全面。
• dijit承认数据中可能存在偏差，但从欧洲游戏开发的角度出发，其工作经历中更多依赖GitLab CI和Jenkins，而非GitHub Actions。他认为GitHub Actions的主导地位与其实际经验不符，并指出其经历的项目大多不是开源的。
• EconomistFar的评论偏离了技术工具的讨论，将比较引向历史人物对计算发展的影响，强调创新路径和影响力的多样性。
• camilomatajira对构建工具（如Make、Just、Taskfile）进行了比较，认为Make仍然是2025年的最佳选择，并假设人们选择新工具可能是因为误以为新工具必然优于旧工具。

补充讨论：
• dijit的评论提到了开源与非开源项目的区别，暗示在不同类型项目中使用的工具可能有所不同。
• camilomatajira提出了对新工具的怀疑态度，认为有些人选择新工具可能只是因为它们的“新”，而非实际的优越性，这是一个关于技术选型的争议点。
• psini和dijit的讨论共同指向了技术社区中不同平台和工具的使用分布问题，涉及数据采样的代表性。

争议焦点：
• GitHub Actions是否在实际使用中占据主导地位，特别是在非开源项目中的代表性如何。
• 新工具（如Just、Taskfile）是否比传统工具（如Make）更优越，还是只是因为“新”而被选择。

44559375.article_content:
Jul 13, 2025
Task Runner Census 2025
TL;DR - Key Take-aways
GitHub Actions dominates CI/CD, Make is omnipresent, and new package managers like uv and pnpm are popular in new repos.
How and why I counted
Every software project accretes snippets of code for developers to execute that are outside the primary codebase. These are named and saved in shell scripts, configs for build tools, package managers, CI runners, and occasionally just code blocks in the README. To find out what people are actually doing in 2025, I crawled the 100,000 most starred repos on GitHub and checked what config files they had. The primary motivation was figuring out what I should support in
dela
, my delegating task runner.
The Leaderboards
Most used task runners
Of the top 100,000 starred repos, 72,804 had detectable task runners. For repo counts, y axis is the total number of repos in which a task runner was detected. For star counts, y axis is the cumulative sum of stars in the detected repos. To be included in the chart, the task runner had to appear in at least 100 repos.
Most used since 2025-01-01
Below are charts only for the repositories created since 2025-01-01 that feature in the top 100k starred repositories. 1,127 repositories made this year have made it into the top 100k most starred repos overall. To be included in the chart, the task runner also had to appear in at least 10 of those repositories.
A taxonomy of task runners
There is a continuum of tooling that can execute code, but not all executions could be considered tasks. My criteria is that the tool is meant to work with the repository and has well-known patterns that could be detected from filenames. This means that things like Python scripts and shell scripts are out because their domain of utility can’t be localized to the repository. Any code that is meant to be run by the user rather than by the developer is also out, such as arg parsers for CLI tools. GitHub Actions, on the other hand, are included because they deal with the repository and are run on behalf of the developer even if they are not typically executed locally.
Build Tool - Tools to manage caching of dependencies when compiling but allow arbitrary code execution.
make
is the prototypical example and is probably the inspiration for most tools in this and other categories.
Package Manager - Package managers like
npm
and
uv
can have a list of tasks they execute, even though it is not their primary purpose.
Easy CLI - These are tools that make it easy to create code that is callable from the shell by developers, but not meant to be distributed. Examples include
rake
and
invoke
, which turn Ruby and Python methods into tasks invokable via the shell.
Task Runner - This is a category for pure task runners that aren’t coupled to another major feature;
just
and
go-task
are examples.
CI/CD Tool - Like build tools but running on somebody else’s infrastructure and also allow arbitrary code execution.
Process Manager - Orchestrate concurrent tasks and supervise their execution. Useful for production servers like
systemd
, but also used in development like
foreman
.
Make & GitHub Actions - General Purpose Leaders
GitHub Actions
appears in 39.8% of the repositories, beating out the next best of 13.9% for
Travis CI
and 2.1% for
Circle CI
in the CI/CD category. That is an amazing victory for GitHub, because
GitHub Actions
only launched in 2019 and was free for public repositories from the start.
Travis CI
had a head start with being free for public repositories since 2011, but in 2020 switched to free for open source with manual review on a case-by-case basis only.
Circle CI
has been free for open source projects since 2014.
At 49 years old,
make
makes its presence seen in 19.0% of the repos. This is remarkable considering how much of present-day software is written in languages that don’t
need
a build step or have it provided by a special tool in their own ecosystem. I attribute part of its continued success to its ability to be used as a general-purpose task runner via the
.PHONY
build targets. Trailing it are
bazel
at 1.5% in the build tools category and
just
at just 0.4% in the task runner category.
27.2% of the repos did not have a detected task runner at all. The most popular of these is
build-your-own-x
with 392,036 stars at the time of the scan.
JavaScript ecosystem - pnpm rising
With 28.5% of all repos,
npm
is at the top of the pack in the JavaScript ecosystem and makes JS the most popular language ecosystem. In the jockeying for 2nd and 3rd place for JS package managers,
pnpm
came out from behind to land in 2nd place for new 2025 repos and 3rd place overall.
pnpm
is being used in 22.9% of all new JS repos made since 2025. This is a larger share than
yarn
ever had.

data.title: Open, free, and ignored: the afterlife of Symbian
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: Symbian，这个由Psion和Nokia共同开发的早期智能手机操作系统，尽管在技术上具有创新性（如EKA2微内核），并已开放源代码，但如今却被忽视。文章回顾了Symbian的发展历史及其衰落原因，包括Nokia在用户界面上的失误和Arm处理器的普及。尽管Symbian曾广泛应用于数百万设备，且拥有繁荣的第三方应用市场，但其开源版本在GitHub上几乎无人问津。相比之下，其他从头开发的操作系统项目（如Genode OS和Serenity OS）却吸引了更多关注。文章还提到其他20世纪专有操作系统的命运，如AmigaOS和BeOS，它们部分被重建或应用于新平台，而Symbian则被遗忘。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Symbian操作系统的设计、开发和消亡原因，以及与现代操作系统的比较。

不同观点：
• **pavlov**：Symbian是一个从零设计的操作系统，专为特定用例优化，但在中期假设上失算。尽管在1997年为低资源设备设计是合理的，但十年后苹果和谷歌推出的智能手机具备更强的硬件和网络支持，Symbian的效率优势反而成为劣势。Nokia在2008年试图通过增加POSIX和触屏支持来挽回局面，但为时已晚，无法与Android竞争。

• **harshaw**：作为开发者，体验不好。Symbian的 memory management 模型难以编程且容易崩溃。与Nokia合作时，遇到开发困难，Nokia对调试第三方应用的兴趣不大。总体上，早期移动操作系统竞争激烈，Symbian的消亡并不意外。

• **sunshine-o**：Symbian是最后一个开放的手机开发平台，支持Qt、JavaME等框架，旧版Skype等应用运行良好。然而，Android和iOS的兴起改变了生态，导致如今银行应用无法在Lineage和Graphene上运行，用户体验变差。

• **raverbashing**：Symbian消亡有其原因，大多数开发者认为开发过程痛苦。

• **actionfromafar**：Symbian速度快且小巧，但难以达到完全稳定。随着硬件提升，操作系统的基础稳定性变得更重要。

• **inglor_cz**：Symbian的操作系统内核速度快且高效，但学习曲线陡峭，开发工具（如Carbide.c++）差，设备兼容性差且碎片化严重。虽然内核技术出色，但整个生态系统被合理地放弃了。

• **secondcoming**：重新构建Symbian代码将是一个巨大的工程，原有的Perl构建系统和SDK可能已不再可用。不过，仍有少数开发者在继续开发Symbian。

• **fsflover**：与Symbian的消亡对比，Mobian和postmarketOS等项目却蓬勃发展，引发思考。

补充讨论：
- Symbian的开发难度和工具问题被广泛提及，尤其是内存管理和开发工具的不足。
- 不同开发者对Symbian的体验和看法各异，有的强调其技术优点，有的则批评其生态系统的不足。
- 对现代移动操作系统（如Android和iOS）的批评主要集中在封闭性和应用兼容性问题上。
- 关于Symbian消亡原因的讨论中，硬件发展和市场时机被认为是关键因素。
- 关于现代Linux移动操作系统的成功，如Mobian和postmarketOS，提出了Symbian消亡的不同背景和可能的经验教训。

44591062.article_content:
OSes
5
Open, free, and completely ignored: The strange afterlife of Symbian
5
It did get sourced, but nobody cared
Liam Proven
Thu 17 Jul 2025
//
07:27 UTC
The result of the pioneering joint Psion and Nokia smartphone effort is still out there on GitHub.
Smartphones are everywhere. They are entirely commoditized now. Most of them run Android, which uses the Linux kernel. The rest run Apple's iOS, which uses the same XNU kernel as macOS. As we've said before, they're not Unix-like,
they really are Unix™
.
There have been a bunch of others. BlackBerry tried hard with BB10, but even a decade ago,
it was over
. It was based on QNX and Qt, and both of those are doing fine. We
reported last year
that QNX 8 is free to use again. Palm's WebOS
ended up with HP
and now runs in
LG smart TVs
– but it's Linux underneath.
The most radical, though, was probably Symbian.
The Register
covered it at length back in the day, notably the epic
Psion: the Last Computer
feature, followed by the two-part
Symbian, The Secret History
, and
Symbian UI Wars
features.
Built from scratch in the late 1990s in the then-relatively new C++, it evolved into a real-time microkernel OS for handhelds, with the radical
EKA2 microkernel
designed by
Dennis May
and documented in detail in the book
Symbian OS Internals
. There's also
The Symbian OS Architecture Sourcebook
[PDF]. An
official version
of the source code is on GitHub, and
other copies
are out there.
We liked
this
description from
CHERI Project
boffin
David Chisnall
:
The original Symbian kernel was nothing special, but EKA2 (which is the one described in the amazing Symbian Internals book) was a thing of beauty. It had a realtime nano-kernel (does not allocate memory) that could run both an RTOS and a richer application stack. It was a victim of poor timing: the big advantage was the ability to run both the apps and the phone stack on the same core, but it came along as Arm cores became cheap enough that just sticking two in the SoC was cheap enough.
Before Nokia was assimilated and digested by Microsoft, it
open sourced the OS
, and despite some
licensing concerns
, it's still there.
It strikes this vulture as odd that while work continues on some ground-up FOSS OS projects in C++, such as the
Genode OS
, or
Serenity OS
, which we
looked at in 2022
,the more complete Symbian, which shipped on millions of devices and for a while had a thriving third-party application market, languishes ignored.
(Incidentally, the Serenity OS project lead has moved on to the independent
Ladybird browser
, which we
looked at in 2023
. Work on the OS continues, now community-led.)
Google's Android boss suggests ChromeOS could be on borrowed time
GParted: Still the best free partitioner standing – unless you're on a 32-bit box
The price of software freedom is eternal politics
Red Hat sweetens the RHEL deal for biz devs – just don't put it in prod
Symbian's progenitor, Psion EPOC32, predates much of the standardization of C++ – much as BeOS did. We've seen comments that it was not easy to program, but tools such as
P.I.P.S.
made it easier. Nokia
wasted vast effort
on multiple incompatible UIs, which have been blamed for
tearing Symbian apart
, but none of that matters now: adapt some existing FOSS stuff, and forget backwards compatibility. Relatively few of the apps were FOSS, and who needs touchscreen phone apps on a Raspberry Pi anyway? Qt would be ideal – it's a native C++ tool too.
Fans of all manner of 20th century proprietary OSes from AmigaOS to OS/2 bemoan that these never went open source. Some of BeOS made it into
PalmOS Cobalt
but that sank. Palm even
mulled basing an Arm version of PalmOS on Symbian
, but
the deal fell through
.
Some of those OSes have been rebuilt from scratch, including
AmigaOS as AROS
and
BeOS as Haiku
. But they run on Intel. Neither runs natively on Arm, and yet Symbian sits there ignored. Sometimes you can't even give the good stuff away. ®

主要讨论点：不同观点对通过跟随或反向操作金融市场建议（尤其是来自YouTube等平台）的有效性评价

不同观点：
• **gtani的观点**：列举了一系列可以通过YouTube频道获取的全球宏观经济指标，认为通过关注诸如Vix指数、期权流、市场 maker的动态、交易量、债券收益率曲线、信用利差、央行持仓、金属价格、地缘政治动态、能源、货币、商品价差等因素，可以获得市场优势。该评论集中于具体的市场指标，而非直接评价YouTube建议的有效性。

• **GianFabien的观点**：援引了John Paulson和Michael Burry的案例，指出逆势操作（即与大众行为相反）往往能带来巨大成功。特别提到这些投资大佬在2008年金融危机前通过做空CDO获利，并通过电影《大空头》来类比当前可能存在的从众心理现象。该观点强调逆向投资策略的潜在收益。

• **Corgipower12的观点**：通过分析金融YouTube推荐的股票视频并进行回测，发现与这些"金融网红"（finfluencers）建议反向操作，能够获得比标普500更高的年化收益率（+6.8%），但同时伴随更高的波动性。这表明反向操作可能比直接跟随网红建议更有效，但也提示了风险的增加。

• **rfarley04的观点**：质疑反向操作的实际效果，并引用CNBC文章标题暗示"什么都不做"可能比复杂的投资策略更有效，反映了对过度交易或复杂操作的怀疑态度。这一观点挑战了Corgipower12的结论，提出"无为而治"也可能是一种成功的投资策略。

• **nullc的观点**：提到与Hacker News（HN）用户观点反向操作也能够带来可观收益，暗示在某些社区中，主流意见可能存在偏差，进一步支持了逆向投资策略的有效性。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**在于YouTube等平台上的金融建议是否具有实际参考价值。gtani关注具体指标而未评价建议质量，GianFabien和Corgipower12则通过实例和数据支持反向操作，而rfarley04则质疑这种策略是否优于简单持有。
• 讨论中还涉及了**波动性与收益率**的关系，Corgipower12指出反向操作虽能提高收益，但伴随更高波动性，这提示了风险管理的重要性。
• **逆向投资策略**的有效性在多个评论中被提及，尤其是GianFabien和nullc引用的历史案例和社区经验，强调了与大众行为反向操作的潜在收益。
