data.author: mildlyhostileux
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为“Claude for Financial Services”的综合金融分析解决方案，旨在改变金融专业人士分析市场、进行研究和做出投资决策的方式。该方案统一金融数据，从市场信息到Databricks和Snowflake等平台的内部数据，整合到一个界面中，并提供直接链接以快速验证信息。方案包括Claude 4模型的领先金融能力，支持Excel任务和复杂分析如蒙特卡罗模拟和风险建模。它还提供预构建连接器，访问Box、Daloopa、FactSet、Morningstar等数据源。此外，方案确保数据保护，不会用于训练模型。多家咨询公司如Deloitte和KPMG提供实施支持，加速企业采用。Claude可用于尽职调查、市场研究、竞争基准测试、财务建模和投资备忘录生成等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在金融服务领域的应用及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• jasonthorsness认为，在信任Claude提供的投资建议之前，其自动售货机项目可能需要先取得成功。他还提出，金融和代码都依赖于小细节，但金融是否具有类似于代码的检查机制（如linting、编译、测试）来捕捉问题，这一点值得怀疑。

• injidup持怀疑态度，引用其父亲的观点，认为任何声称能帮助赢得赌场、赛马或股票交易的系统都是骗局，如果系统真的有效，就不会被出售。

• mildlyhostileux指出，Anthropic推出了“Claude for Financial Services”，新的模型在金融特定任务上表现更好，并与多种数据源集成。但金融业不同于纯文本工作，日常工具仍然是Excel和PowerPoint。他们质疑一个侧边聊天窗口是否足够，以及金融从业者是否会完全迁移到Claude上。

• hbcondo714提到，OpenAI也有针对金融服务的解决方案，表明Anthropic并非唯一涉足此领域的公司。

• gyosko警告说，“感觉投资”即将到来，可能会让很多人变穷。

• osn9363739认为，金融服务的范围很广，不仅仅是原始数据，还包括如何利用数据讲述想要的故事情节。他提到与四大的人交流，发现分析结果往往需要与客户反复讨论才能达成一致。

• dang引用了Hacker News的指南，指出提交的标题已被修改，强调标题不应误导或夸大。

• yodon呼应了“感觉投资”的主题。

• AdieuToLogic担心这可能会导致类似于2021年GameStop轧空事件的重演。

• asdev质疑Anthropic为何专注于垂直解决方案，而不是尝试成为所有人都能基于其构建的最佳水平平台。

• tom_m预测，初期可能会很痛苦，但最终可能会很酷，不过肯定会有人因此损失金钱。

• the_arun支持这一举措，并希望看到其他业务领域的特定服务。

• khurs指出，LLM在2022年推出，金融作为一个高利润且技术密集的行业已有2.5年的时间来推进。他询问现有的竞争情况，如JP Morgan的内部项目和Bloomberg的 offerings。

• eddythompson80认为，AI应被视为一种应用界面，改变的是交互方式，而不是功能本身。他举例说明AI如何简化财务分析工具的使用，无需学习复杂的软件操作。

• kaycebasques提到Bloomberg的模式，并询问其用户使用情况。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI在金融领域的应用是否可靠以及其潜在的负面影响，如“感觉投资”和市场操纵。
• 讨论还涉及金融服务的复杂性和AI如何融入现有的工作流程，特别是与Excel和PowerPoint等传统工具的竞争。
• 对Anthropic和OpenAI在金融服务领域竞争的关注，以及对垂直与水平解决方案的战略选择。

Today, we're introducing a comprehensive solution for financial analysis that transforms how finance professionals analyze markets, conduct research, and make investment decisions with Claude.
The Financial Analysis Solution unifies your financial data—from market feeds to internal data stored in platforms like Databricks and Snowflake—into a single interface. Access your critical data sources with direct hyperlinks to source materials for instant verification, all in one platform with expanded capacity for demanding financial workloads.

Claude’s industry-leading financial capabilities:
Claude 4 models outperform other frontier models as research agents across financial tasks in Vals AI's Finance Agent
benchmark
. When deployed by FundamentalLabs to build an Excel agent, Claude Opus 4 passed 5 out of 7 levels of the Financial Modeling World Cup competition and scored 83% accuracy on complex excel tasks.
Claude Code and Claude for Enterprise with expanded usage limits

Pre-built MCP connectors:
Access financial data providers and enterprise platforms for comprehensive market data and private market intelligence.
Expert implementation support
: Tailored onboarding, training, and best practices for rapid value realization.
Financial institutions require the highest standards of data protection. By default, your data is not used for training our generative models, maintaining confidentiality of your intellectual property and client information.
The AI ecosystem for financial services
We've built the Financial Analysis Solution with leading financial and enterprise technology providers, giving Claude the ability to instantly check information across multiple sources. This creates a fundamentally more reliable way to analyze financial data—information is verified across sources to reduce errors, every claim links directly to its original source for transparency, and complex analysis that normally takes hours happens in minutes.

provides an easy, connected, and trusted data and AI platform that allows global enterprises to unlock value across all of their data – including structured, unstructured, and semi-structured
All of these integrations will be available today or in the coming weeks.
Accelerating enterprise adoption

Deloitte
enhances research productivity across equity research, private credit, and municipal bonds through their 10X Analyst
KPMG
helps financial services companies deploy AI assistants and agents to their developers and analysts

breaks down regulations into discrete obligations, analyzes internal compliance gaps, and generates policy updates through their Regulatory Pathfinder
Slalom
accelerates legacy code modernization through their AI Accelerated Engineering program, and provides solutions for end-to-end insurance operations transformation
TribeAI
helps investment teams automate deal material review, financial analysis, and entity resolution with VDR integration
Turing
offers auto-generation of compliance requirements in PRDs and Compliance Benchmarking-as-a-service

Claude accelerates critical investment and analysis workflows including due diligence and market research, competitive benchmarking and portfolio deep dives, financial modeling with full audit trails, and generating institutional-quality investment memos and pitch decks. data.title: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 Incident on July 14, 2025
data.author: nomaxx117
data.article_summary: 2025年7月14日，Cloudflare因服务拓扑更改导致1.1.1.1公共DNS解析服务中断62分钟，影响全球大多数用户，并造成Gateway DNS服务间歇性降级。中断原因是6月6日为未来数据本地化服务（DLS）准备时错误包含了1.1.1.1的配置，导致1.1.1.1的IP前缀被错误撤下。中断并非由于攻击或BGP劫持。事件从21:48开始，21:52时1.1.1.1的DNS流量开始下降，22:01检测到问题，22:54恢复。Cloudflare对此致歉并采取措施防止类似事件再次发生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 DNS 服务中断事件的影响及技术问题分析

不同观点：
• v5v3 提出疑问，为什么用户在主 DNS 服务器 1.1.1.1 失效时没有自动切换到备份 DNS 服务器，质疑配置中的第二个 DNS 服务器为何没有生效。
• chrismorgan 对 Cloudflare 内部监控系统在事件发生后超过五分钟才检测到问题表示惊讶，并好奇为何警报系统没有及时触发。
• kachapopopow 指出 Cloudflare 频繁出现类似问题，而 Google 的 DNS 服务（8.8.8.8 和 8.8.4.4）在过去近十年几乎没有宕机，暗示 Cloudflare 在基础设施稳定性方面可能存在不足。
• jallmann 提到自己受到了影响，尽管已配置 Cloudflare 的 DoH（DNS-over-HTTPS），但仍遇到了解析问题，最终通过将 DNS 改为 8.8.8.8 解决了问题。
• homebrewer 建议使用 dnsmasq 设置多个 DNS 服务器并进行竞争响应，认为这样可以避免单个服务中断导致的问题。
• i_niks_86 指出许多用户假设 DNS 提供商之间存在故障转移机制，但实际上，操作系统或路由器级别的 DNS 客户端很少实现健壮的 DoH 故障转移，用户容易因此被困在无法解析的状态。
• CuteDepravity 建议在 1.1.1.1 出现问题时切换到其他提供商（如 8.8.8.8 或 9.9.9.9）作为备份，并对同时影响 1.1.1.1 和 1.0.0.1 的情况表示惊讶。
• perlgeek 从 SLO（服务级别目标）角度分析此次中断，指出此次中断可能导致 Cloudflare 服务降级至 99.9% 以下的可用性，并讨论了用户可能因此获得的赔偿。
• Mindless2112 提到自己使用了同时配置 Cloudflare 和 Google DNS 的工具，因此未受影响，并指出 DoH 未完全受到影响。
• aftbit 对多位工程师审核后仍未发现路由配置错误表示惊讶，并建议对 1.1.1.1/32 和 1.0.0.1/32 等关键 IP 进行特殊保护以避免类似问题。
• alyandon 根据自己的监测数据指出，Cloudflare 的中断时间可能比官方声明更长，质疑其声明的时间范围。
• cadamsdotcom 对 Cloudflare 的技术写作和事件处理表示赞赏，认为其声明透明且负责，展示了公司对问题的重视。
• chrisgeleven 反思自己过于依赖单一 DNS 提供商，建议设置不依赖上游解析服务的 DNS 服务器（如 Unbound），以提高网络稳定性。
• neurostimulant 提到自己的 ISP 会劫持 UDP 53 端口的流量并重定向到其 DNS 服务器，因此未受此次中断影响，但暗示这种行为是出于政府审查的目的。
• wreckage645 认为 Cloudflare 频繁出现全球性中断，显示其变更管理流程存在问题，建议对问题管理进行集中化处理，而不是每个团队各自为战。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点主要集中在 DNS 服务中断的影响、故障转移机制的缺失、Cloudflare 内部监控和响应的延迟、以及对类似问题的长期解决方案（如多 DNS 配置或自建解析服务）的建议。
• 部分用户质疑 Cloudflare 基础设施的健壮性，并建议用户使用多个 DNS 服务商以减少类似事件的影响。
• 也有用户对 Cloudflare 的处理和沟通方式表示肯定，认为其在事件后及时且透明地进行了说明。

44578490.article_content:
Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 incident on July 14, 2025
2025-07-15
Ash Pallarito
Joe Abley
8 min read
On 14 July 2025, Cloudflare made a change to our service topologies that caused an outage for 1.1.1.1 on the edge, resulting in downtime for 62 minutes for customers using the 1.1.1.1 public DNS Resolver as well as intermittent degradation of service for Gateway DNS.
Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 Resolver service became unavailable to the Internet starting at 21:52 UTC and ending at 22:54 UTC. The majority of 1.1.1.1 users globally were affected. For many users, not being able to resolve names using the 1.1.1.1 Resolver meant that basically all Internet services were unavailable. This outage can be observed on
Cloudflare Radar
.
The outage occurred because of a misconfiguration of legacy systems used to maintain the infrastructure that advertises Cloudflareâs IP addresses to the Internet.
This was a global outage. During the outage, Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 Resolver was unavailable worldwide.
Weâre very sorry for this outage. The root cause was an internal configuration error and
not
the result of an attack or a
BGP hijack
. In this blog, weâre going to talk about what the failure was, why it occurred, and what weâre doing to make sure this doesnât happen again.
Background
Cloudflare
introduced
the
1.1.1.1
public DNS Resolver service in 2018. Since the announcement, 1.1.1.1 has become one of the most popular DNS Resolver IP addresses and it is free for anyone to use.
Almost all of Cloudflare's services are made available to the Internet using a routing method known as
anycast
, a well-known technique intended to allow traffic for popular services to be served in many different locations across the Internet, increasing capacity and performance. This is the best way to ensure we can globally manage our traffic, but also means that problems with the advertisement of this address space can result in a global outage.Â Â Â
Cloudflare announces these anycast routes to the Internet in order for traffic to those addresses to be delivered to a Cloudflare data center, providing services from many different places. Most Cloudflare services are provided globally, like the 1.1.1.1 public DNS Resolver, but a subset of services are specifically constrained to particular regions.Â
These services are part of our
Data Localization Suite
(DLS), which allows customers to configure Cloudflare in a variety of ways to meet their compliance needs across different countries and regions. One of the ways in which Cloudflare manages these different requirements is to make sure the right service's IP addresses are Internet-reachable only where they need to be, so your traffic is handled correctly worldwide. A particular service has a matching "service topology" â that is, traffic for a service should be routed only to a
particular set of locations
.
On June 6, during a release to prepare a service topology for a future DLS service, a configuration error was introduced: the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service were inadvertently included alongside the prefixes that were intended for the new DLS service. This configuration error sat dormant in the production network as the new DLS service was not yet in use,Â  but it set the stage for the outage on July 14. Since there was no immediate change to the production network there was no end-user impact, and because there was no impact, no alerts were fired.
Incident Timeline
Time (UTC)
Event
2025-06-06 17:38
ISSUE INTRODUCED - NO IMPACT
A configuration change was made for a DLS service that was not yet in production. This configuration change accidentally included a reference to the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service and, by extension, the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service.
This change did not result in a change of network configuration, and so routing for the 1.1.1.1 Resolver was not affected.
Since there was no change in traffic, no alerts fired, but the misconfiguration lay dormant for a future release.Â
2025-07-14 21:48
IMPACT START
A configuration change was made for the same DLS service. The change attached a test location to the non-production service; this location itself was not live, but the change triggered a refresh of network configuration globally.
Due to the earlier configuration error linking the 1.1.1.1 Resolver's IP addresses to our non-production service, those 1.1.1.1 IPs were inadvertently included when we changed how the non-production service was set up.
The 1.1.1.1 Resolver prefixes started to be withdrawn from production Cloudflare data centers globally.
2025-07-14 21:52
DNS traffic to 1.1.1.1 Resolver service begins to drop globally
2025-07-14 21:54
Related, non-causal event: BGP origin hijack of 1.1.1.0/24 exposed by withdrawal of routes from Cloudflare. This
was not
a cause of the service failure, but an unrelated issue that was suddenly visible as that prefix was withdrawn by Cloudflare.Â
2025-07-14 22:01
IMPACT DETECTED
Internal service health alerts

• jallmann 提到自己受到了影响，尽管已配置 Cloudflare 的 DoH（DNS-over-HTTPS），但仍遇到了解析问题，最终通过将 DNS 改为 8.8.8.8 解决了问题。
• homebrewer 建议使用 dnsmasq 设置多个 DNS 服务器并进行竞争响应，认为这样可以避免单个服务中断导致的问题。
• i_niks_86 指出许多用户假设 DNS 提供商之间存在故障转移机制，但实际上，操作系统或路由器级别的 DNS 客户端很少实现健壮的 DoH 故障转移，用户容易因此被困在无法解析的状态。
• CuteDepravity 建议在 1.1.1.1 出现问题时切换到其他提供商（如 8.8.8.8 或 9.9.9.9）作为备份，并对同时影响 1.1.1.1 和 1.0.0.1 的情况表示惊讶。
• perlgeek 从 SLO（服务级别目标）角度分析此次中断，指出此次中断可能导致 Cloudflare 服务降级至 99.9% 以下的可用性，并讨论了用户可能因此获得的赔偿。
• Mindless2112 提到自己使用了同时配置 Cloudflare 和 Google DNS 的工具，因此未受影响，并指出 DoH 未完全受到影响。
• aftbit 对多位工程师审核后仍未发现路由配置错误表示惊讶，并建议对 1.1.1.1/32 和 1.0.0.1/32 等关键 IP 进行特殊保护以避免类似问题。
• alyandon 根据自己的监测数据指出，Cloudflare 的中断时间可能比官方声明更长，质疑其声明的时间范围。
• cadamsdotcom 对 Cloudflare 的技术写作和事件处理表示赞赏，认为其声明透明且负责，展示了公司对问题的重视。
• chrisgeleven 反思自己过于依赖单一 DNS 提供商，建议设置不依赖上游解析服务的 DNS 服务器（如 Unbound），以提高网络稳定性。
• neurostimulant 提到自己的 ISP 会劫持 UDP 53 端口的流量并重定向到其 DNS 服务器，因此未受此次中断影响，但暗示这种行为是出于政府审查的目的。
• wreckage645 认为 Cloudflare 频繁出现全球性中断，显示其变更管理流程存在问题，建议对问题管理进行集中化处理，而不是每个团队各自为战。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点主要集中在 DNS 服务中断的影响、故障转移机制的缺失、Cloudflare 内部监控和响应的延迟、以及对类似问题的长期解决方案（如多 DNS 配置或自建解析服务）的建议。
• 部分用户质疑 Cloudflare 基础设施的健壮性，并建议用户使用多个 DNS 服务商以减少类似事件的影响。
• 也有用户对 Cloudflare 的处理和沟通方式表示肯定，认为其在事件后及时且透明地进行了说明。

data.author: hhs
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了美国债务问题及其对经济的潜在影响。经济学家创建了一个美国经济模型，但在当前债务预测下，该模型无法预测出长期 functioning 的经济体系。债务不断上升可能导致利率上升，政府大部分税收将用于支付债务利息，而非投资于经济增长或基础设施。经济学家Kent Smetters警告，若不采取措施，20年后美国经济可能会开始萎缩。他提出了一些改革建议，如提高退休年龄至70岁、征收碳税、减少社保福利，但认为政府采纳这些建议的可能性仅为5%。尽管如此，这仍比当前路径的成功率（0%）要高。

44591622.article_content:
Jul 14, 2025
Economists made a model of the U.S. economy. Our debt crashed the model
Under current debt projections, economists cannot even model out a functioning long-term economy.
National Debt
by
Stacey Vanek Smith
Play
Listen Now
Save
Share
Download
“We cannot even model out a functioning long-term economy under current debt projections," said Jessica Riedl, an economist with the Manhattan Institute who studies the federal budget.
Kent Nishimura/Getty Images
People have been worrying about U.S. debt basically ever since there even was a U.S. “The accumulation of debts is a most fearful evil,”
Thomas Jefferson wrote in 1787
. At the time, U.S. debt was around
$40 million
. Today, it’s closer to
$40 trillion
. At the same time, the U.S. economy is bigger and more powerful than Jefferson could have ever imagined, and things are looking pretty good: unemployment is near record lows, inflation is under control… so what’s the problem?
“Part of the problem is it's been this kind of ‘boy who cries wolf’ type thing, and people just get tired of it,” says Kent Smetters, an economist at Wharton, who has been crying wolf about the debt for years. He started to wonder: What exactly happens if the U.S. just doesn’t deal with its debt? He got a few economists and mathematicians together to build a computer model of the economy to play out scenarios.
They made a model of the entire U.S. economy, which required a lot of computing power. “This math problem was a big one,” Smetters said. “And the model computations are about 20,000 times bigger than our standard model.”
Smetters borrowed some computing help from Amazon and NASA and then he and his colleagues then fed the entire U.S. economy in all of its complicated glory into this mega-model. And the U.S. economy… could not compute.
“Their economic models crashed when trying to project out the economy over the long term,” said Jessica Riedl, an economist with the Manhattan Institute who studies the budget. “We cannot even model out a functioning long-term economy under current debt projections.”
The crash itself: not super cinematic, said Smetters. No flashing red letters, no skull and crossbones, no lightning bolt, just a few words that make a macroeconomist’s blood run cold:
Model not converging.
“The model's trying to find what's called a fixed point where everything just adds up, everything's consistent, and it's not able to do that,” Smetters explained.
In other words, if the debt keeps rising at its current rate and we just do not deal with it, even thousands of NASA and Amazon computers all working together cannot get the math to math.
“Really, it's a question of how far can we go before the bond market says, ‘I just don't believe that you're gonna pay us back,’” explained Smetters.
Bonds are like little loans. And the U.S. government sells billions of dollars worth of bonds every week. The interest rate it pays on those loans? Super low. Because people know the U.S. is good for the money.
If this were “The Simpsons,” the U.S. would be like Mr. Burns taking out a loan. The bank would very likely give him a really good interest rate: he’s rich, he’s got a great job, he’s got a big house. The bank could feel pretty sure it’s not going to lose its money.
Homer Simpson on the other hand, with his credit card debt, modest income, and some (donut related) impulse control issues would probably have to pay a much higher interest rate for the same loan.
Economist Jessica Riedl said the U.S. might be entering its Homer Simpson era. The country’s got so much debt that’s it’s outpaced what the economy earns.
“
The debt is projected to go from $30 trillion to $200 trillion over the next 30 years,” said Riedl. “That will cause interest rates to rise. Within a decade, interest is going to be one third of all of your taxes, and in a couple decades, interest could be 80% of your taxes.”
If most of the country’s money is going to paying interest on the debt, it can’t be invested into growing the economy, or filling potholes, or improving schools. It’s just going to pay interest. In cases like that, an economy will typically start to shrink: Services shut down, things stop working, businesses stop growing, they start laying people off.
So how long do we have before this happens? According to Kent Smetters’ model, about 20 years.
”The good news is we can actually make decisions now today that actually would stabilize the amount of debt relative to the size of the economy,” said Smetters.
Smetters and his colleagues published a
list of suggested reforms
that they think could help to fix the budget: raise the retirement age to 70, add a carbon tax, reduce social security benefits.
The chances of the government doing all of that? Smetters put it at about 5%. Not great, he said, but still better than the odds of our current path working out, which Smetters put at 0%.

data.title: Plasma Bigscreen rises from the dead with a better UI
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: KDE项目Plasma Bigscreen正在复兴。该项目是一个用于电视的Plasma界面，最初支持现已停止运营的Mycroft AI助手。由于长期未更新，大多数发行版已放弃该项目，且在Plasma 6转型期间未及时移植。现在，Plasma Mobile贡献者Devin决定花时间对其进行全面改造。他清理了代码库，重新设计了界面，去除了面板背景，增加了背景模糊效果，并引入了搜索功能以快速查找和启动应用。设置应用也经过重新设计，采用双窗格布局，并修复和更新了多个模块。目前，该项目仍在开发中，计划在未来纳入官方Plasma发布计划，可能在6.5版本中实现。用户可以在Raspberry Pi上通过postmarketOS测试该项目。

不同观点：
• [giancarlostoro] 希望找到预装Linux的电视设备，并倾向于使用Arch或Debian系发行版。他目前使用Apple TV，但希望有一个兼具Linux功能和电视操作系统视觉效果的设备。
• [MattTheRealOne] 认为优化的界面很重要，但应用的优化同样关键，否则改进有限。他目前使用常规的Plasma连接电视。
• [whazor] 指出目前Linux缺乏优秀的电视界面，现有的Android TV和Steam大屏模式都有不足。他希望结合媒体观看和游戏功能的界面能出现在强大且价格合理的迷你PC上。
• [aquova] 对Plasma Bigscreen的复活感到兴奋，之前因其开发停滞而放弃使用，期待它能成为Roku的替代品。
• [imiric] 希望新系统能允许使用外部播放器如mpv播放媒体，并支持加载远程库。

• [FuriouslyAdrift] 认为nVidia Shield Pro加Kodi是最可靠和高效的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• [ListeningPie] 和 [tocs3] 关心该系统是运行在电视硬件上还是通过HDMI连接外部计算机。
• [raffael_de] 和 [WorldPeas] 询问项目的具体使用方法和硬件要求，如是否需要USB安装或特定硬件支持。
• [stuaxo] 提到Android TV令人失望，希望新系统能解决如远程输入和屏幕键盘的问题，并通过Waydroid运行Android TV应用。
• [porridgeraisin] 指出Plasma Bigscreen项目刚复活，尚未达到公开发布的稳定阶段。

• 是否能实现一个兼具Linux功能和电视操作系统视觉效果的设备。
• 自定义电视系统能否支持Netflix和Prime等商业服务。

44573752.article_content:
Lately, some KDE projects have seen a revival, like
Karton (the native virtual machine manager for KDE)
and the
improved ISO Image Writer.
Now, another abandoned KDE project, Plasma Bigscreen, is looking to return from the dead after long-time Plasma Mobile contributor Devin decided to spend a week overhauling the thing.
If you have not heard of it,
Plasma Bigscreen
is a Plasma shell for televisions, with original support for the now-defunct Mycroft AI assistant. It used to provide a simple launcher for apps and custom "Mycroft Skills" before development stalled, causing most distributions to drop it.
The project was left behind during the big transition to Plasma 6 last year because no one had ported it in time for the megarelease. After a friend of his started poking at the code,
Devin stepped in
to tackle the much-needed work.
He started by cleaning up the repository and then jumped into redesigning the interface, drawing inspiration from older Breeze mockups. The homescreen has been flattened, removing panel backgrounds. Here's a before-and-after comparison (click to enlarge):
One of the more visible changes is that the UI now has a background blur when you are navigating menus, giving focus to the foreground elements.
For actually finding what you want to run, you are no longer stuck scrolling through a long list, as Devin added a new search view, searching using KRunner to quickly find and launch applications.
The Settings application also got a complete redesign, adopting a simple two-pane look with a sidebar for categories. A lot of the settings modules (KCM) used hardcoded layouts, so Devin built a small component library for TV-focused UIs and ported everything over.
The rewritten Display KCM now uses the libkscreen backend, and the Wi-Fi and KDE Connect modules have been fixed and updated. Startup feedback for launching applications was also broken, and when you start up an application, a small animation now plays, similar to the one on Plasma Mobile.
For anyone who wants to test this out, you can do as Devin did by installing Plasma Bigscreen on a Raspberry Pi using postmarketOS, though you would have to compile it yourself or pull from the nightly repos to get the latest changes.
Applications like Kodi and
VacuumTube (smart TV version of YouTube)
work well with remote navigation, and some games like
SuperTuxKart
are playable.
Controller support exists, but getting TV remotes to work over HDMI CEC is still untested. The project is far from finished; it still needs an arrow-navigable virtual keyboard and a clearer long-term direction now that Mycroft is gone. Still, the goal is to get it back into the official Plasma release schedule, possibly for version 6.5.

data.author: DyslexicAtheist
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Lorem Gibson，一个基于威廉·吉布森作品的网站填充文本生成器。用户可以通过刷新页面获得不同的文本内容。文章还提到对@davidtweaver的改进建议，并欢迎捐款支持。该工具类似于传统的Lorem Ipsum文本生成器，但特别针对吉布森的风格和主题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“Lorem Gibson”文本生成器的想法及其相关技术实现的讨论，包括格式、语言风格、技术改进建议以及对类似文本生成器的回顾。

不同观点：
• **对文本格式和风格的改进建议**：
  - [allenu] 认为句子的首字母应大写，破折号的格式需要修正，建议去掉破折号间的空格，以避免如"cyber- neon"或"bomb- ware"这样的显示问题。
  - [mNovak] 同样希望生成器能生成语法正确的句子，并认为正确的大小写并不难实现。

• **对Lorem Gibson风格的评价**：
  - [nodefortytwo] 非常喜欢这个想法，分享了使用Grok生成类似William Gibson风格的段落，描述了富有赛博朋克风格的场景。
  - [ashoeafoot] 认为Gibson的作品常包含对垃圾和漂浮物的描写，而当前的生成内容没有体现这一点。

• **技术实现与改进讨论**：
  - [dzdt] 提到大型语言模型（LLM）让人们变得挑剔，建议使用如nanoGPT训练Gibson语料库，认为这样可以得到更好的结果。
  - [adregan] 回忆早期使用ipsum生成器的经历，质疑如今这类工具使用减少的可能原因，如从博客转向应用程序、信息密度降低或文本内容减少。

• **对其他类似文本生成器的提及**：
  - [hungryhobbit] 提到Lorem Gibson在其他地方被引用，询问发帖者是否参考了特定文章。
  - [hi_hi] 推荐具有“澳洲风味”的boganipsum。
  - [Brajeshwar] 回顾了过去多种类型的ipsum生成器，如Monty Python、Star Wars、Douglas Adams等，并提到自己仍在使用Alfred的Snippets功能。

• **幽默与创意**：
  - [tshaddox] 开玩笑说可能会选择Henrik Ibsen而不是Gibson。
  - [ilikecakeandpie] 和 [f4c39012] 以幽默方式回应，提到与文本生成无关的内容。
  - [wheybags] 和 [rcarmo] 用创意语句或引用经典台词进行调侃。

- 评论中不仅讨论了Lorem Gibson生成器的具体技术问题和风格，还引发了对其他类似文本生成器的怀旧和推荐，同时夹杂了一些幽默和创意回应。争议焦点主要在于文本的语法和格式是否应该更加规范化，以及技术实现上的改进空间。

data.title: New battery has life so long you may never have to recharge
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 韩国大邱庆北科学技术院（DGIST）的Su-Il In教授领导的研究团队开发了一种新型核电池——钙钛矿贝塔伏特电池（PBC），可为小型设备供电数十年而无需充电。该电池使用碳-14（放射性碳）和钙钛矿材料，结合量子点和双重氯基添加剂，增强了能量转换效率和长期稳定性。通过将碳-14应用于电极，并利用二氧化钛和钌基染料增强电子反应，电池的能量转换效率从0.48%提升至2.86%。尽管输出仍低于锂离子电池，但该技术被认为在生物安全性、耐用性和环保性方面具有优势，未来可应用于心脏起搏器、太空探测器和无人机等领域。研究团队计划加速商业化并进一步提升电池性能。

44591585.article_content:
Image by ThisIsEngineering via
Pexels
A research group at the Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), led by Professor Su-Il In, has developed a new type of nuclear battery called a perovskite betavoltaic cell (PBC), which could power small devices for decades without the need for recharging. The team used carbon-14—an unstable form of carbon known as radiocarbon—and combined it with perovskite materials to create a hybrid battery with improved energy conversion and long-term stability.
The new battery uses radioactive carbon-14 nanoparticles and quantum dots (14CNP/CQD) as electrodes. These were embedded into the device along with a perovskite film treated with dual chlorine-based additives: methylammonium chloride (MACl) and cesium chloride (CsCl). These additives helped strengthen the crystal structure of the perovskite, making it more stable and better at moving electric charges. Compared to older designs, the team recorded a roughly 56,000-fold improvement in electron mobility and a maximum continuous operation of nine hours during testing.
“This study represents the first successful integration of perovskite into a betavoltaic cell, pioneering perovskite betavoltaic cells,” the researchers stated.
Betavoltaic cells work by turning beta particles—emitted during radioactive decay—into electricity. Since beta rays can’t penetrate human skin and can be blocked by materials like aluminum, the technology is considered biologically safe. Professor In explained, “I decided to use a radioactive isotope of carbon because it generates only beta rays.” Carbon-14 is also a by-product from nuclear reactors, making it cheap, widely available, and recyclable. Because it breaks down very slowly, it could power devices for hundreds or even thousands of years.
To raise energy conversion efficiency—the measure of how well a battery turns electrons into usable power—the team turned to a titanium dioxide semiconductor, often found in solar cells, and enhanced it with a ruthenium-based dye. The bond between the dye and titanium dioxide was made stronger through a citric acid treatment. When beta rays from radiocarbon hit the dye, they triggered a chain of electron reactions known as an avalanche. These electrons were then captured by the titanium dioxide and sent through a circuit to generate electric current.
The battery was also designed with radiocarbon in both the anode and cathode, increasing the amount of beta radiation and reducing energy loss over distance. This approach helped boost its energy conversion efficiency from 0.48% in older models to 2.86%.
Still, the system only converts a small portion of radioactive energy into electricity, meaning its output remains lower than standard lithium-ion batteries. Professor In suggests improving the shape of the beta emitter and finding better absorbers could further raise power output.
“This research marks the world’s first demonstration of the practical viability of betavoltaic cells,” said In. “We plan to accelerate commercialization of next-generation power supply technologies for extreme environments and pursue further miniaturization and technology transfer.”
Doctoral student Junho Lee added, “Although this research involves daily challenges that often seem impossible, we are driven by a strong sense of mission, knowing that the future of our nation is closely tied to energy security.”
The team believes that, with further development, these radiocarbon-powered batteries could be used in areas ranging from pacemakers to space probes and drones. As In puts it, “We can put safe nuclear energy into devices the size of a finger.”

data.title: MacPlusDancer: Microsoft Plus! Dancers for macOS
data.author: archagon
data.article_summary: MacPlusDancer 是一个将 2003 年微软 Plus 舞者带回 macOS 的怀旧应用。用户可以从菜单栏图标选择不同风格的舞者，并将其拖动到屏幕任何位置，舞者会保持在其他窗口上方。除了 Seth 必须一直跳舞外，用户可以开关舞者的舞蹈。该项目为粉丝制作，使用了 2003 年微软的舞者动画，但未获微软官方认可。应用采用 Apache-2.0 许可，欢迎贡献代码。

Get to know Amanda, Cobey, and all the other Plus! dancers by reading their bios online, and then download more of your favorite dancers to your computer.
MacPlusDancer is a delightfully nostalgic macOS app that brings back the dancers from Microsoft Plus! (their exclamation point, not mine).
Choose from a variety of dancers with different styles
Drag and position dancers anywhere on your screen
Dancers stay on top of other windows for maximum visibility
Toggle dancing on and off (except for Seth, he must dance forever)
Installation and Usage
Download the latest release from the
Releases
page.
Select a dancer from the menu bar icon (a dancing figure).
Position your dancer by dragging them around the screen.
Contributing
Contributions are welcome! Please feel free to submit a Pull Request.
NOTE: If you submit a PR to make Seth stop dancing, it will be rejected.
Legal Note
The dancer animations are from the original Microsoft Plus 2003 application. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. It's a fan-made port created for educational and nostalgic purposes.
Credits
This website
from the early 2000s was very useful in building this app. Shoutout to whoever made that website, I suppose.
FAQ
Q: Why should I use this?
You should not.
Q: Why can't I make Seth stop dancing?
We cannot legally answer that.
Q: Why is this app so big?
This app is 52 video files in a trench coat.
Q: Is there dancer lore?
Yes.
About
At long last, a macOS-native version of the Microsoft Plus Dancers from 2003. Thank god.

data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary:
**GPUHammer: Rowhammer Attacks on GPU Memories are Practical**

本文介绍了一种名为GPUHammer的攻击方法，首次展示了在GPU内存（具体为NVIDIA A6000 GPU的GDDR6内存）上实施Rowhammer比特翻转攻击的可行性。尽管GDDR6内存具有更高的延迟和更快的刷新速度，且内存映射不透明，GPUHammer仍通过逆向工程DRAM地址映射和利用GPU的SIMT并行性，成功实现了跨所有测试DRAM bank的比特翻转。攻击者可利用这些翻转篡改共享GPU环境中其他用户的数据。实验显示，单个比特翻转可使DNN模型准确率从80%降至0.1%。尽管ECC可缓解此风险，但会造成ML推理工作负载最高10%的性能下降。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对硬件漏洞（如锤击攻击）及其影响的技术讨论

不同观点：
• PeterStuer认为锤击攻击（hammering attacks）非常令人满意，因为它通过操作虚拟宇宙中的模式，直接影响了底层的物理层面，而不是通过传统意义上的漏洞突破。他还提出这种攻击方式让人联想到是否存在对我们现实宇宙的类似操作。
• Userbinator指出，过去GPU仅用于图形渲染时，偶尔的VRAM比特翻转并不受关注。他还提到ECC（错误校正码）在某些情况下会影响性能，尤其是当存在需要纠正的错误时。此外，他提到使用比特翻转来破坏深度神经网络（DNN）模型的概念验证，具有一定的讽刺意味，因为这些模型原本是用来模拟有错误和不精确的现实。
• Privatelypublic质疑是否存在大量分割GPU计算工作负载的情况，并询问是否有实际的例子，因为他能想到的多数情况都是使用专用GPU。
• Perching_aix作为一个硬件新手，好奇这样一个问题是如何在开发过程中的电磁模拟中被遗漏的，并提到尽管现代芯片非常复杂，难以进行完全的形式验证，但内存模块因其高度结构化的特点，可能有机会通过验证。
• IFire直接询问自己的Nvidia RTX 4090显卡上的ECC模式是否能防止这种攻击。
• Sylware提到，优化过的汇编代码相较于编译器生成的代码，可能更容易引发“锤击”问题，因为优化的代码可能更频繁地操作内存。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是ECC对性能的影响，以及在不同硬件（GPU与CPU）上的表现差异。
• 另一个讨论点是锤击攻击的实际应用场景和普遍性，尤其是对共享GPU计算资源的质疑。
• 还有人关注硬件漏洞在开发和验证过程中的检测问题，以及个人硬件（如iFire的4090显卡）如何防御此类攻击。
• 最后，讨论涉及了代码优化与硬件漏洞之间的关系，特别是汇编代码可能带来的风险。

GPUHammer: Rowhammer Attacks on GPU Memories are Practical
#
Chris (Shaopeng) Lin
†
, Joyce Qu
†
, Gururaj Saileshwar,
from University of Toronto
Published at
USENIX Security 2025
(link to
paper
). Artifact available on
GitHub
and
Zenodo
.
†
equal contribution
TL;DR
#
GPUHammer
is the first attack to show
Rowhammer bit flips on GPU memories
, specifically on a
GDDR6 memory in an NVIDIA A6000 GPU
. Our attacks
induce bit flips across all tested DRAM banks
, despite in-DRAM defenses like TRR, using user-level CUDA code. These bit flips allow a malicious GPU user to
tamper with another user’s data on the GPU
in shared, time-sliced environments. In a proof-of-concept, we use these bit flips to tamper with a victim’s DNN models and
degrade model accuracy from 80% to 0.1%, using a single bit flip
. Enabling Error Correction Codes (ECC) can mitigate this risk, but ECC can introduce up to a 10% slowdown for ML inference workloads on an A6000 GPU.
🔍 What’s New in Rowhammer for GPUs?
#
Rowhammer
is a hardware vulnerability where rapidly activating a memory row introduces bit flips in adjacent memory rows.
Since 2014, this vulnerability has been widely studied in CPUs and in CPU-based memories like DDR3, DDR4, and LPDDR4.
However, with critical AI and ML workloads now running on discrete GPUs in the cloud, it is vital to assess the vulnerability of GPU memories to Rowhammer attacks.
Rowhammer is uniquely more challenging on GPU-based GDDR memories for the following reasons:
⏱️  GDDR6 has higher latency and faster refresh than CPU-based DDR4, making hammering harder.
🧩 Unknown DRAM address mappings in GDDR memories complicate crafting effective patterns.
🛡️  In-DRAM mitigations in GDDR are opaque and undocumented.
Despite this, GPUHammer overcomes these barriers and launches successful attacks on GDDR6.
Step 1: Reverse Engineering GPU DRAM Mappings
#
To craft effective Rowhammer attacks, we first need to identify memory addresses that map to the same DRAM bank on an NVIDIA GPU. Unlike CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs do not expose the physical addresses to user-level CUDA code, making it challenging to identify and hammer DRAM rows in the same bank. However, observing that the NVIDIA GPU driver consistently maps virtual memory to the same physical memory, we reverse engineer the virtual memory offsets to DRAM bank mappings. Inspired by the
DRAMA
technique, we use timing differences between memory accesses to the same bank vs. different banks.
One key obstacle, as shown in
Fig. 1
, is the
Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA)
effect in memory access latencies for addresses accessed in pairs, which makes it hard to pinpoint same-bank addresses. Based on the insight that addresses in the same DRAM bank must have similar latency when accessed  in isolation, we filter out such addresses contributing to the NUMA effects and clearly identify addresses mapping to the same DRAM bank (see
Fig. 2
). This accurately identifies same-bank address pairs needed for crafting Rowhammer patterns.
Fig. 1:
Naively accessing pairs of addresses: different-bank latencies (320-370ns) overlap with same-bank latencies (370-380ns) due to NUMA effects.
Fig 2:
After filtering addresses with different latencies when accessed in isolation, same and different bank address pairs are distinguishable.
Step-2: Maximizing Hammering Intensity
#
GPU memory accesses are up to
4× slower
slower than CPUs, making it hard to reach the activation rate needed for Rowhammer attacks using naive,
single-threaded
hammering like in CPUs (
Fig. 3
, green line). To overcome this, we exploit the GPU’s
SIMT parallelism
, launching multiple threads and warps in parallel. This
multi-threaded, multi-warp approach
(
Fig. 3
, orange line) eliminates idle time in the memory controller and reaches the maximum possible hammering rate.
Fig. 4
shows how these strategies maximize memory controller utilization.
Fig. 3:
Number of activations in a single refresh period (tREFW) for single-thread, multi-thread, and multi-warp hammering.
Fig. 4:
Memory controller utilization with (a) single-thread,
(b) multi-thread, and (c) multi-warp hammering. Multi-warp
hammering minimizes idle time, maximizing activation rates.
Step-3: Synchronizing to Refreshes, Defeating Mitigations
#
Prior works like
SMASH
and
BlackSmith
show that synchronizing hammering to refreshes (REF) is key to bypassing in-DRAM defenses.
However, CUDA’s synchronization primitives (like
__syncthreads()
) used to synchronize threads can reorder warp execution. Instead, we use implicit per-warp delays, aligned such that REF commands overlap with our inserted delays, to align our hammering with refreshes and defeat in-DRAM mitigations like TRR while preserving warp execution order.
Fig. 5:
Per-warp delays inserted using
adds
for synchronizing
to REF. When the delays overlap, the REF
is inserted in alignment with the hammering pattern.
💥 What Did We Break?

NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB GDDR6)
across four DRAM banks and observed

data.title: Hand: open-source Robot Hand
data.author: vineethy
data.article_summary: AmazingHand项目旨在开发一种低成本（<200€）、开源、具有8个自由度的仿人机械手，适用于Reachy2机器人，但也可适应其他机器人。该手具有4根手指，每个手指由2个小Feetech SCS0009伺服电机驱动，通过平行机制控制其弯曲/伸展和外展/内收。机械手所有 actuators 都内置于手内，无需外接电缆，重量约400克，且可通过3D打印制造。控制方式有两种：使用Waveshare串行总线驱动器和Python脚本，或使用Arduino和Feetech TTL Linker。项目提供了详细的物料清单（BOM）、CAD文件、组装指南和基本演示软件。注意，实际角度可能与理论值有差异，需进一步开发智能软件以实现复杂抓取任务。

Amazing Hand project
Robotic hands are often very expensive and not so expressive. More dexterous often needs cables and deported actuators in forearm i.e..
Aim of this project is to be able to explore humanoid hand possibilities on a real robot (and Reachy2 is the perfect candidate for that !) with moderate cost.
=> Wrist interface is designed for Reachy2's wrist (Orbita 3D), but it can be easily adapted to other robot's wrist...
Amazing Hand is :
8 dofs humanoid hand with 4 fingers
2 phalanxes per finger articulated together
flexible shells allmost everywhere
All actuators inside the hand, without any cables
3D printable
400g weight
low-cost (<200€)
open-source
AmazingHand_Overview
Each finger is driven by parallel mechanism.
That means 2x small Feetech SCS0009 servos are used to move each finger in flexion / extension & Abduction / Adduction
2 ways of control are available :
Use a Serial bus driver (waveshare i.e.) + Python script
Use an Arduino + feetech TTL Linker
Detailed explaination are available for both ways and Basic demo software is available also.
Up to you !

Assembly guide for the Amazing Hand in combination with standards components in the BOM is here :

With Python & Waveshare serial bus driver :
here
With Arduino & TTLinker :
here
Note that this assembly guide is for a standalone Right hand.
If you need to build a standalone Left hand, you can keep the sames IDs for servos location, and select if it's a right or left hand in the software.
BUT, if you need to build both right and left hands to plug them on a robot, you will have to attribute differents IDs for right and left hands. You can't have same ID for different servos on the same serial bus...
Run basic Demo
Basic Demo which is available with both Python & Arduino.

Disclaimer
I noticed some variations between theorical angles for Flexion / Extension, Abduction / Adduction and angles in real life prototypes. This is probably due to several sources of variation (3D printed parts are not perfect, balljoint rods are manually adjusted one by one, esrvo horn rework, flexibility of plastic parts...).
This design has not yet bene tested for long and complex prehensive tasks. Before to be able to grasp objetcs safely (that means without damaging servos or mehanical parts), kind of smart software need to be build.
SCS0009 servos have smart capaibilities as:
Torque enable / disable
Torque feedback
Current position sensor
Heat temperature feedback
...

• 有人提到具体项目和公司（如Pollen Robotics和HuggingFace）对机器人领域的贡献（[mclau157]）。
• 有人关注创意应用，如将机器人装饰成万圣节的装饰物（[ortusdux]）。

补充讨论：
• 技术细节上的讨论，例如通过肌腱减少手臂重量（[amelius]）和提升重量的能力（[mandeepj]）。
• 有人询问类似的外骨骼或支持设备项目（[agumonkey]）。
• 设计上的讨论，包括四指设计的考虑因素和成本效益（[TheAceOfHearts]），以及人类手型是否为最佳握持设计（[mft_]）。
• 对设计美学的评价，如卡通风格的手指设计（[fitsumbelay]）和整体设计的欣赏（[SequoiaHope]）。
• 有人觉得该设计似曾相识，可能与其它作品有相似之处（[schainks]）。

争议焦点：
• 四指设计是否出于成本考虑及其功能上的优劣是讨论中的一个小争议点。

data.author: seangrvs

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在企业报告和财务风险披露中的作用及影响

不同观点：
• **PDF内容模糊性**：mansoor_ 认为某份PDF内容过于模糊，几乎可以被空白页取代，暗示内容缺乏实质性。
• **风险披露的动机**：yellow_lead 指出公司财务报告中的“风险”部分更多是为了“保护自己”（CYA），而非真正担心AI的影响。
• **AI讨论的趋势性**：seydor 纠正关于“1/X公司”的表述，认为公司谈论AI并不意味着他们会采取实际行动，只是因为这是当前的潮流。
• **AI对就业的影响**：MinimalAction 提出疑问，如果AI作为“更便宜”的替代方案取代工作岗位，是否会以同样的生产力指标节省成本。netrap 补充说明，企业报告中通常不会提到工作岗位风险，因为减少工作岗位对企业来说是“好事”。
• **AI对财富积累和市场的影响**：amelius 担心如果AI在股票交易中表现优于人类，可能会导致财富集中于少数大型AI公司，使股市对其他人失去意义。
• **报告本身的质量和意义**：MarkusQ 讽刺报告本身空洞无物，认为AI对撰写此类报告的咨询公司构成存在性风险。

补充讨论：
• **LLM分析风险披露**：simonw 提到通过LLM分析最近的10-K报告，发现3/4的S&P 500公司相较于之前的10-K提到了额外的AI风险，包括AI驱动的网络攻击、深度伪造、能源需求和法规（如欧盟AI法案）等。

争议焦点：
• AI在企业风险披露中的真实作用：是真正的风险预警还是仅仅为了“保护自己”而做的表面文章。
• AI对就业和财富分配的潜在影响：一方认为AI可以提高效率、节省成本，另一方则担心其对就业和财富分配的负面影响。

data.title: My bank keeps on undermining anti-phishing education
data.author: cheesepaint
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者收到一封来自当地银行（Sparkasse）的电子邮件，推广一个名为Wero的数字支付系统和抽奖活动。邮件内容和格式与网络钓鱼邮件极为相似，包括提供高额奖金、使用无关域名、以及缺乏具体背景信息等特点。尽管邮件看似可疑，发件人地址和个性化称呼表明它确实来自银行。作者进一步访问银行官网确认了活动的真实性，但对银行使用类似钓鱼邮件的方式推广活动感到不满。网站要求用户同意分析支付数据以参与抽奖，并收集个人信息。文章最后简要介绍了Wero支付系统。此事在Hacker News上引发了讨论，有人担心银行可能因此面临法律风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：银行及金融机构在客户安全验证、反欺诈措施和域名使用等方面的实践与问题

不同观点：
• **wccrawford**：经历过银行发送看似钓鱼邮件要求提供保险证明，尽管最终是合法的，但银行无法理解其邮件为何引发钓鱼怀疑。最终通过亲自前往银行分行解决问题。

• **TheFreim**：其银行采用 fraud detection 系统，当检测到可疑活动时会打电话要求回拨验证。然而，每次提供的回拨号码都不同，且在网上难以验证，导致用户难以区分合法与欺诈电话。

• **RandomBacon**：其银行（USAA）曾使用不同域名发送看似合法的邮件，引发钓鱼担忧。与银行 fraud 部门沟通后，账户被锁定，需再次联系解锁。用户认为银行的操作可能导致客户更容易被钓鱼攻击。

• **j_seigh**：提到某些信用卡商户可能通过跟踪更新卡信息进行欺诈，即使用户更换新卡，坏人仍能获取新卡信息。解决办法是关闭并重新开设银行账户。

• **pyuser583**：在购房等场景中，多种实体使用不同域名，增加了对可信域名的判断难度。建议银行公开“合作伙伴域名”列表，并通过可信的.gov网站查询联系方式验证银行真实性。

• **TimTheTinker**：指出决策者往往低估安全风险，直到有人被骗。约2012年前，这种现象在美国企业中较为普遍，后来由于黑客攻击频发，问题才得到缓解。

• **clarkdale**：认为银行的营销部门与核心IT部门不协调，导致不同部门使用不同域名和网站，增加了客户的困惑。

• **dsabanin**：多次收到诈骗电话，最终因忽略看似诈骗的贷款电话而导致信用记录问题（未支付的新HVAC系统贷款）。

• **0x5FC3**：批评印度银行的用户界面不友好，包括限制密码长度、禁止复制粘贴、客户端密码哈希等问题，认为其技术实践落后。

• **meindnoch**：曾有银行在推销电话中要求提供生日和母亲名字，用户质疑银行应先证明其真实身份。

• **Rygian**：主张银行应因发送类似钓鱼邮件对客户承担法律责任，特别是因重大过失导致客户混淆。

• **massung**：其银行（USAA）的电话验证流程较为安全，先通过应用程序验证用户身份，再进行多因素认证，确保通话安全性。

• **phendrenad2**：讨论公司内部IT部门与其它部门在域名使用上的矛盾，部分公司因高风险拒绝使用子域名，导致其它部门注册独立域名，增加了钓鱼风险。

• **rwmj**：其银行将电话认证改为语音识别，但用户认为这种方法并非绝对安全，可能存在被伪造的风险。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于银行和金融机构在安全验证和反欺诈措施上的不完善，用户经常感到不安，尤其是在面对看似欺诈的邮件和电话时。
• 不同用户对银行的域名使用、电话验证及安全协议有不同的体验和建议，反映出行业内实践的多样性和潜在的安全隐患。
• 用户普遍认为银行应采取更透明和安全的措施，如公开可信域名、改进电话验证流程以及增强客户教育。

44592377.article_content:
TLDR: my bank sent out emails with websites which looked a lot like phishing mails, so much so that this similarity could potentially be used against them legally by potential phishing victims
– Discussion at hackernews (soon)
Chapter 1: You’ve got mail
#
As I was writing my first post some weeks ago, I got an email from my bank in my inbox:
Here the English translation of the email:
Dear …,
The big Wero Win Weeks are starting! Take part now and secure your chance every week to win 7 prizes of €1,000 each.
With Wero, you can send money from account to account in under 10 seconds. It’s easy, fast, and secure. And the best part: If you register once for the prize draw now, you will automatically participate in the draw until September 2nd. With a chance to win every week!
Join now! Win €1,000 seven times every week!
Here’s how it works:
Some background information for my non-German readers:
What is a Sparkasse?
The bank in question is my local Sparkasse. Sparkassen are regional savings banks that exclusively serve people in their region. They are generally owned and sponsored by their serving municipalities. Each Sparkasse is an independent institution, but they are all connected through an umbrella organisation, which coordinates their activities, ensures interoperability and gives it an overarching corporate design. Their areas are focused on SMEs and private customers, and in general, they have a strong local economic impact and are serving a lot of people. All institutes combined, the Sparkassen financial group is the largest financial service provider in Europe.
A link to the Wikipedia article.
What is Wero?
The email in question was promoting Wero. And I do not mean the Māori challenge, which is part of the welcoming ceremony. Wero is a new European digital payment system launched by the European Payment Initiative (EPI). It was created to replace several local payment systems, which were only used in the respective countries. Imagine it more or less like a rival to PayPal, just decentralised among all banks. Initially it focused on P2P payments (which is promoted in this mail), but sometime they plan to support online and in-store payments. They are still in an early adaptation phase.
A link to the Wikipedia article.
This email address wasn’t on a spam list yet, so I was quite confused. I mean, the indicators are clear:
You can win quite a large sum of money
The prize draw without context (more on that later)
Contains a link to a domain unrelated to my bank (“gewinnen-mit-wero.de”)
The text in the subject and the body are very generic and tonally like phishing emails.
As there is nothing like free lunch, this must be spam. But on the other side:
The sender address is a domain from my local Sparkasse institute
The email is personalised with my name
I went to my bank’s website and checked whether the prize draw really exists and if they use the same domain. And they do. So I started to get angry: How can a trusted institution like a bank send such a spam-looking mail? Then I went to the website, and it just got worse…
Chapter 2: It gets worse…
#
Here the English translation of the website:
Send money. Win money. With the Wero-Win Weeks
#
Fill out the one-time participation form.
Send money with Wero in the Sparkasse app.
Automatically be entered into the prize draw with every amount you send.*
Promotion period: 18.03. to 02.09.2025
Participate now
Send money, win, celebrate
#
Anyone who sends money with Wero has the chance to win one of seven weekly cash prizes worth €1,000 – every week brings a new chance!
Wero-Win Weeks. Join now!
#
Register: Sign up once.
Send money: Send money at least once a week with Wero to friends or family. By the way, in order to participate in the prize draw, you must agree to the “analysis of data from payment transactions.”
By agreeing to the analysis of payment data, you participate in the prize draw.
Increase your chances: Every successful payment earns you a spot in that week’s prize draw.
Didn’t win? Your entries remain valid.
Important:
A maximum of seven payments per week will be counted. You only have a chance to win in the weeks when you send money with Wero.
Each week, seven €1,000 cash prizes are awarded.
Haven’t activated Wero in the Sparkasse app yet? You can catch up easily.
How to activate Wero in the Sparkasse app.
Participation Form:
First name
Last name
Date of birth
IBAN
Email address
☑ I accept the terms and conditions and privacy policy. I am aware that Sparkasse employees are excluded from participating.
☑ I would like to receive email updates and news about the prize draw. I can revoke this consent at any time.
Submit
What is Wero?
#
Wero is the new payment solution for sending money
within seconds
– directly from phone to phone.
Secure and fast
Send and receive money in under 10 seconds.
Transparent
Keep track of incoming and outgoing transactions on your account in real time.
Simple and always available
From account to account, directly in the Sparkas

data.title: BB(6) Is Hard (Antihydra) (2024)
data.author: Fibra
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一个与Collatz类似的函数，定义为：

$$
\begin{array}{l}
f(2n)   & = & 3n   \\
f(2n+1) & = & 3n+1 \\
\end{array}
$$

或者等价于：

$$
f(n) = n + \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor
$$

从数字8开始应用该函数，会生成一个无穷序列。文章探讨了在序列生成过程中，是否会出现奇数规则应用次数超过偶数规则应用次数的两倍的情况。

该问题与解决6状态2符号的Busy Beaver问题相关，并引入了"Antihydra"概念，它与之前的"Hydra"规则类似，但起始值和终止条件不同。文章详细描述了Antihydra的规则和迭代过程，并通过模拟展示了迭代步数和状态变化。

文章还讨论了Busy Beaver问题的未来，提到BB(6)的发现让问题变得更加复杂，并提出了寻找新的Busy Beaver值和解释新"Cryptids"作为新的研究目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过6状态图灵机编码Collatz式迭代，以及BB(6)的上限问题

不同观点：

Note: All Discord links are for the
https://bbchallenge.org/
Discord server.
Consider the Collatz-like function:
\[\begin{array}{l}
f(2n)   & = & 3n   \\
f(2n+1) & = & 3n+1 \\
\end{array}\]
or equivalently defined as
\[f(n) = n + \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor\]
Starting from 8 and repeatedly applying \(f\) we get the infinite sequence:
\[8 \xrightarrow{E} 12 \xrightarrow{E} 18 \xrightarrow{E} 27 \xrightarrow{O} 40 \xrightarrow{E} 60 \xrightarrow{E} 90 \xrightarrow{E} 135 \xrightarrow{O} 202 \cdots\]
where the
O
s and
E
s above each arrow represent whether we chose the Odd or Even rule to apply (i.e. whether or not the previous value was odd or even).
Starting from 8, will you ever reach a point where the cumulative number of
O
s applied is greater than twice the number of
E
s applied?
Solving the 6-state, 2-symbol Busy Beaver problem requires solving this Collatz-like problem! Yes, that’s right, we have our first BB(6)
Cryptid
, the “
Antihydra
”.
For returning visitors who may be feeling a sense of Deja-Vu: Yes, this is almost identical to the
Hydra
rules! In fact, the only difference is that Antihydra starts at 8 instead of 3 and that the halting condition is “reversed” (\(2O > E\) instead of \(2E > O\)).
Antihydra

This TM was discovered and shared by @mxdys on 28 June 2024
on Discord
with the message: “This TM looks like a random [walk] like hydra”. Shortly afterwards, Racheline (@rae) discovered and shared the precise rules described below.
Analysis
Let
\[E(a, b) = 0^\infty \; 1^b \; 0 \; 1^a \; \text{E>} \; 0^\infty\]
Then the following rules apply:
\[\begin{array}{l}
\text{Start} & & \xrightarrow{11} & E(4, 0) \\
E(2n,   & b)   & \to & E(3n+2, b+2)       & \text{ if } n \ge 1 \\
E(2n+1, & 0)   & \to & \text{Halt}(3n+3)  & \text{ if } n \ge 1 \\
E(2n+1, & b+1) & \to & E(3n+3, b)         & \text{ if } n \ge 1 \\
\end{array}\]
Where “Start” is the TM in state
A
on a blank tape and “Halt(x)” means the TM halts with \(x\) non-zero symbols on the tape.
Alternative Collatz map
Like with Hydra, we can shift this map to produce a more familiar mapping.
Let
\[A(a, b) = E(a-4, b)\]
then for all \(n \ge 3\) and \(b \ge 0\) we have:
\[\begin{array}{l}
\text{Start} & & \xrightarrow{11} & A(8, 0) \\
A(2n,   & b)   & \to & A(3n, b+2) \\
A(2n+1, & 0)   & \to & \text{Halt}(3n-3) \\
A(2n+1, & b+1) & \to & A(3n+1, b) \\
\end{array}\]
which is (as previously stated) the same as the Hydra map, but starting from 8 and with the reverse halting condition.
Note that the \(n \ge 3\) conditions does not cause any trouble since this iteration starts at \(a = 8\) and \(a\) strictly increases after each iteration (for all \(a \ge 2\)).
Trajectory
@mxdys has simulated this iteration out to \(2^{31} = 2\,147\,483\,648\) steps at which point \(b = 1\,073\,720\,884\) (only 20940 below the expected value if this were a random walk) (
Discord link
). As with Hydra and Bigfoot, if we treat this iteration as a random walk, it has a miniscule chance of ever returning to \(b = 0\) and thus of ever halting.
The Future of Busy Beaver
On Tuesday, we at bbchallenge.org
announced a Coq proof of the BB(5) problem
(and Ben Brubaker at Quanta wrote a
lovely article
describing the 60 year journey!). And within a week before that, we have also found this first BB(6) Cryptid. This combination of events leaves me with some sadness alongside my joy. One of the things I’ve long talked about loving when it comes to the Busy Beaver problem, is the idea that we will never be done with it. Nobody can ever find all Busy Beaver values, so there will always be one more puzzle to solve, one more mystery to explore.
But with this discovery of Cryptids in BB(6), we now know (in an especially concrete way) how the next puzzle will be quite hard. Scott Aaronson is quoted in Ben’s article saying “It’s conceivable that this is the last busy beaver number that we will ever know.” Is this the end of the Busy Beaver problem? Instead of an end I think it is a sharp turn on the racecourse. Up until now, our goal has been to find new Busy Beaver champions and prove that all other TMs run forever. Now, it feels, that our goal has changed slightly: in addition to finding new champions, we are also looking for new Cryptids and trying to explain them in as simple a way as possible.
Solving BB(6) feels out of reach in my lifetime, but solving BB(6) modulo a handful of Cryptids feels possible. As Busy Beaver hunters in a changing world, we must adapt to the new conditions and consider new prey. Let us also hunt Cryptids!

Celtuce（茎用莴苣），也称为芹菜莴苣或中国莴苣，是莴苣的一个变种，主要以其厚实的茎和叶子作为蔬菜食用。起源于地中海地区，后在唐代传入中国。它在中国的家庭中被称为"莴苣"（wōjù），在台湾和中国都很受欢迎，茎被称为"莴笋"（wōsǔn）或"青笋"（qīngsǔn）。  
  
**营养价值**：每100克生茎用莴苣提供75千焦能量，富含维生素A、C和多种B族维生素，以及钙、钾、镁等矿物质。  
  
**种植**：种子在4月至5月播种，植株间距30厘米，嫩叶在种植后4-5周可采收，茎长到约30厘米时收获，通常在7月至9月间采收。易受蚜虫侵害。  
  
**用途**：叶子与茎可生吃（如沙拉）或烹饪（如腌制、炒、烤）。茎常切片炒，并搭配味道更浓的食材。在美国，它也被用作无麸质意面替代品。

主要讨论点：钻石行业的道德、经济和功能性争议，特别是天然钻石与实验室培育钻石的对比。

不同观点：
• **wpm**：认为钻石从未是奢侈品，只是因奴隶劳工的开采和De Beers的市场营销才赋予了其虚假的稀缺性和威望。强调De Beers应该面临道德和伦理上的清算，而非经济上的困境。语气激进，认为De Beers的财富来源不正，并对其未来持幸灾乐祸的态度。

• **Cerium**：支持实验室培育钻石，认为购买钻石应基于功能性，如珠宝的切割、清晰度或用于磨料工具的硬度，而非为了显示财富或地位。

• **barbazoo**：惊讶于人们仍然在乎钻石，认为这是一种过时的、带有负面意义的追求，尤其在许多人经济状况不佳的情况下。对人们愿意为钻石花钱表示不解，因为钻石在离店后迅速贬值。

• **wantlotsofcurry**：讽刺De Beers的困境，表达对De Beers面临挑战的幸灾乐祸。

- **道德与伦理问题**：多位评论者提到钻石行业的道德问题，特别是奴隶劳工和地缘政治冲突相关的问题，对De Beers的过去持批评态度。
- **实验室培育钻石的优势**：多位评论者认为实验室培育钻石在质量、价格和道德方面具有优势，建议消费者考虑这种选择。
- **市场变化与行业未来**：评论者普遍认为传统钻石行业面临挑战，实验室培育钻石等替代品正在改变市场格局。
- **讽刺与情绪**：部分评论带有明显的讽刺和幸灾乐祸情绪，尤其是针对De Beers的财务困境。

data.title: Ukrainian hackers destroyed the IT infrastructure of Russian drone manufacturer
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IT基础设施恢复、网络战争与攻击、系统安全性与备份、技术与战争

不同观点：
• [BrandoElFollito] 认为从零重建个人实验室相对容易，但大规模基础设施的恢复则非常困难。他分享了自己在帮助医院和公司应对勒索软件攻击后恢复系统的经验，强调了多人员管理的基础设施恢复的复杂性，即使有文档和测试，现实情况依然严峻。

• [lnsru] 描述了一家德国公司在ERP系统迁移失败后，依赖于印刷的Excel表格进行生产规划的状况。指出生产管理层试图隐瞒问题，且不与工程部门沟通，预计这种状况会持续多年，且顾问借此收取高额费用。

• [Kapura] 关注乌克兰战争中的网络战与无人机攻击，指出无人机在侦察、破坏和拦截方面的革命性作用，并提到乌克兰在不对称战争中的成功，战争的未来难以预料。

• [rclkrtrzckr] 在一家中型瑞士公司工作，他们的ERP系统基于复杂的代码堆栈，称为“混乱安全”，即使攻击者破坏大部分代码，系统仍能运行，因为大部分代码已过时。

• [praptak] 指出很少有公司为所有数据存储单元被清除后从零重新部署做准备，强调了未从零引导系统可能导致的部署依赖循环问题。

• [hosh] 关注文章中对网络活动者与网络犯罪者的定义模糊问题，并将其与私掠者历史类比，讨论了平民与军事角色模糊的现代战争规则。

• [grishka] 提到访问某网站时遇到的网络封锁和技术障碍，如TLS错误和Cloudflare阻挡页面，最终通过VPN访问到俄语文章。

• [frou_dh] 关注无人机固件被篡改的可能性及其在敌方无人机上的价值。

• [v5v3] 提到乌克兰网络活动者与军事情报合作，质疑这是否属于直接的网络战争。

• [ShadowBanThis03] 主张文明国家应联合摧毁俄罗斯的IT基础设施。

• [ropable] 认为最棘手的问题是恢复和替换奇怪的IT-OT接口部分，如仅能运行在Windows 98上的CNC设备，这些部分通常无人备份和记录。

• [garfieldnate] 对图片日期接近Unix纪元开始日表示有趣。

• [nicholast] 认为比无人机更经济有效的技术是数字干预。

• [madebywelch] 好奇是否进行过灾难恢复演练。

• 讨论涉及IT基础设施恢复的复杂性，尤其是多人员管理和历史遗留系统。
• 网络战争和无人机技术在现代战争中的应用及其潜在威胁。
• 系统安全性和备份的重要性，尤其是过时和未记录系统的处理。
• 对网络活动者和网络犯罪者定义的模糊性及其在现代战争中的角色。

data.title: Doge Put Free Tax Filing Tool on Chopping Block After One Meeting with Lobbyists
data.author: josefresco
data.article_summary: 本文报道了美国国税局（IRS）的免费报税工具Direct File面临被取消的情况。该工具本应不受削减，但在所谓政府效率部门（DOGE）介入后，其命运发生变化。DOGE领导层最初对Direct File表示支持，但在与报税软件游说团体会面后，态度发生转变。DOGE成员之一、由Andreessen Horowitz支持的健康创业公司CEO Sam Corcos建议取消该工具，并与Free File Inc.（包括Intuit和TurboTax等公司）会面。尽管Direct File将在2025年报税季前保持在线，但可能明年被取消。DOGE团队包括多名与Intuit有财务关联的成员，他们参与了多个IRS项目，包括评估使用Palantir软件。这一变化引发对政府与私营企业利益冲突的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：税务申报工具及其与政府和第三方公司的关系

不同观点：
• dlcarrier认为，税务申报不应依赖类似TurboTax的独立工具，而应直接集成到IRS网站中。用户可以登录查看收入信息、补充扣除或额外收入、申诉不准确的信息，并直接申请退款或支付税款。补贴小公司与大公司竞争无法解决问题，只会加深行业壁垒和游说活动。
• Donald提到联邦承包商在DOGE方面的经验，指出资金重新分配的问题，并暗示国会听证会将揭示更多细节，可能成为公众关注的焦点。
• potato3732842指出，第三方解释税法并将责任转移给政府和纳税人，这种模式对政府有利，因此维持现状。第三方承担责任，政府避免直接与纳税人的纠纷。
• bediger4000认为，免费税务申报应成为常态，第三方营利性税务软件对公民和政府都不利。DOGE的存在并没有消除浪费，反而可能成为一个巨大的问题，最终可能被以不民主的方式处理。
• chmaynard强烈反对游说者，认为他们是只关心利益的雇佣兵，对政策没有真正的关心。
• kotaKat对IRS免费文件项目被取消感到不满，担心未来报税会更加复杂，并质疑是否需要为私人公司的高管买单。同时关心州级税务申报的延续性问题。
• chopete3建议IRS展示强制性收入列表和税务义务，以减少猜谜和误算，并认为这可以防止不正当的公司操作。
• bko认为，税务软件的复杂性和高成本源于税法的复杂性，而不是工具本身。如果政府重新编写免费税务软件，成本会转移到纳税人或IRS上。质疑政府是否能比私人公司更有效地开发税务软件，并认为简化税法是解决问题的根本途径。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应由政府直接提供免费税务申报工具，还是依赖第三方软件公司。
• 讨论中多次提到简化税法以减少税务申报复杂性的必要性。
• 对游说者和DOGE等机构的批评，反映了对政策执行和资金使用的广泛不满。
• 州级税务申报的延续性问题也被提及，表明纳税人对地方和联邦税务整合的关注。

44593180.article_content:
Save Story
Save this story
Save Story
Save this story
When the
so-called Department of Government Efficiency
(DOGE) arrived at
the Internal Revenue Service
earlier this year, leaders of the group reassured workers that the agency’s free tax filing tool, Direct File, would be spared from cuts. But only a few days after meeting with tax software lobbyists, the beloved tool was placed on the chopping block, multiple sources familiar tell WIRED.
The plans to potentially kill Direct File, the free tax filing tool developed by the IRS which services 25 states, was initiated by Sam Corcos, CEO of an Andreessen Horowitz–backed health startup that has ties to SpaceX. Corcos’ suggestion to cut the popular service was presented to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in the beginning of March, multiple sources familiar say.
The weekend before Corcos suggested ending Direct File, he spoke of it positively to IRS engineers. By Friday, he had changed his tune. As sources WIRED spoke to understand it, Direct File would remain online through the 2025 tax filing season but would likely be dead by next year.
“Throughout the week, the tone had shifted,” says one source. The decision to end Direct File “came out of nowhere.”
Days after the weekend meeting, Corcos told multiple sources that he had met with Free File Inc. (previously the Free File Alliance), a group of tax preparation software companies that partner with the IRS to offer free online tax filing services. The group was organized by Intuit, which produces TurboTax, more than 20 years ago as a means of offering free filing services to lower-income taxpayers. In return, the IRS promised not to create its own government-run online filing system.
Before Inauguration Day in January and well into the following month, DOGE leadership, including Steve Davis, CEO and president of Elon Musk’s Boring Company, and Amy Gleason, acting administrator for the US DOGE Service, said they were impressed with the Direct File project and reassured the engineering team working on it that it was safe, multiple sources tell WIRED. (Though Davis stepped away from government last month, he continued to lead meetings and
deliver orders
to DOGE representatives. This included Corcos, who reportedly refused to cooperate, and Davis
attempted
to oust him.)
The IRS did not immediately respond to a request for comment from WIRED. Corcos now serves as the Treasury’s chief information officer.
“We think [the IRS] ought to wind it down, and they ought to focus their attention on other key priorities like modernization,” David Ransom, a tax lobbyist representing the American Coalition for Taxpayer Rights,
told NOTUS in April
. At least two tax preparation companies represented by the American Coalition for Taxpayer Rights, TaxSlayer and TaxHawk, also belong to the Free File Alliance. (By 2021, Intuit and H&R Block left the Free File Alliance.)
Prior to Intuit’s departure, ProPublica reported that code had been introduced into the company’s
version of the Free File website
that essentially hid the service from search engines like Google, making it nearly impossible to find without directly navigating to it.
Corcos has been one of DOGE’s primary decisionmakers at the IRS, multiple sources at the agency tell WIRED. In April, he led
a three-day workshop
with a number of representatives from Palantir to build a new “mega API” for accessing all internal IRS records. At the time, sources said the IRS was testing whether to use Palantir’s Foundry software as a central reading center for all IRS systems.
Around the time Corcos arrived as a senior adviser at the Treasury Department in late February, other DOGE members were being onboarded to the agency. Todd Newnam, who previously was a CEO of a tech company, joined as a Schedule C employee. As Corcos’ supervisor, Newnam was the DOGE team lead at the Treasury for all IRS-related matters, according to a court filing. Corcos reported to Newnam through early May, when he was named the Treasury CIO, and as stated in a separate court filing, the group worked on a variety of projects, including “reviewing of the [IRS’s] vendor contracts.” In his financial disclosure form, Newnam listed owning shares of Intuit, as
first reported
by Politico. Newnam wasn’t the only DOGE member to own Intuit shares—Linda Whitridge and Tom Krause, both at the Bureau of Fiscal Service, own shares of Intuit.

• Donald提到联邦承包商在DOGE方面的经验，指出资金重新分配的问题，并暗示国会听证会将揭示更多细节，可能成为公众关注的焦点。
• potato3732842指出，第三方解释税法并将责任转移给政府和纳税人，这种模式对政府有利，因此维持现状。第三方承担责任，政府避免直接与纳税人的纠纷。
• bediger4000认为，免费税务申报应成为常态，第三方营利性税务软件对公民和政府都不利。DOGE的存在并没有消除浪费，反而可能成为一个巨大的问题，最终可能被以不民主的方式处理。
• chmaynard强烈反对游说者，认为他们是只关心利益的雇佣兵，对政策没有真正的关心。
• kotaKat对IRS免费文件项目被取消感到不满，担心未来报税会更加复杂，并质疑是否需要为私人公司的高管买单。同时关心州级税务申报的延续性问题。
• chopete3建议IRS展示强制性收入列表和税务义务，以减少猜谜和误算，并认为这可以防止不正当的公司操作。
• bko认为，税务软件的复杂性和高成本源于税法的复杂性，而不是工具本身。如果政府重新编写免费税务软件，成本会转移到纳税人或IRS上。质疑政府是否能比私人公司更有效地开发税务软件，并认为简化税法是解决问题的根本途径。

• 争议焦点在于是否应由政府直接提供免费税务申报工具，还是依赖第三方软件公司。

44579717.article_content:
I started to code more in
Python
around 6 months ago.
Why?
Because of AI, obviously.
It’s clear (to me) that big
money
opportunities are all over AI these days.
And guess what’s the
de facto
programming language for AI?
Yep, that sneaky one.
I had used Python before, but only for small scripts.
For example,
this script
scrapes metadata from all videos on
my YouTube channel
.
The metadata is dumped as
a JSON file
that I use to nicely display statistics of the videos
on this static page
.
As you can
see here
, this little script runs in solo mode every Monday via GitHub Actions.
Doing this kind of thing in Python is just way more convenient than, say, using Batch.
Not only because the syntax is more human-friendly, but also because the Python interpreter is natively integrated in all Unix distros.
Isn’t that cool?
So yeah, Python is powerful, and it couples very well with the now ubiquitous
VSCode
editor.
But I didn’t treat it seriously until recently,
1
it was just after I wanted to build AI applications (RAG, Agents, GenAI tools, etc.) for the “real world” that I realized that whether you like it or not, Python is the language of choice for those matters.
So I decided to give it a serious try, and to my great surprise, I’ve found that Python, and everything around it, has really improved a lot over the last decades.
Here’re just three examples:
Python has created a very complete ecosystem of libraries and tools for processing and analyzing data.
2
Python has gotten faster with optimized static compilers like
Cython
.
Python has done a good job of hiding its legacy ugliness (such as
__init__
,
__new__
, and similar aberrations), sweetening its syntax to accommodate developers
with good taste
.
Thanks to this and many other things, I’m now feeling a particular joy for the language.
However, during this time, I’ve found that there’s still a big gap between using Python for “production-ready”
3
apps vs. the usual Jupyter notebook or script-based workflow.
So in this post, I share the tools, libraries, configs, and other integrations that bring me joy, and that I now use for building my Python applications.
⚠️ This post is highly biased toward the tools I personally use today, and if you think I’m missing some gem, please let me/us know (preferably in the comment section below).
NOTE:
Somehow this article got
600+ comments
on Hacker News (just another proof that you never really know).
Project Structure
I prefer to use a
monorepo
structure (backend and frontend) for my Python projects.
4
Why?
Because of my bad memory: I don’t like code parts scattered across multiple repositories (it’s definitely not search-friendly).
Because having multiple repos is mostly unnecessary: I’m just one guy, and I believe that if a project grows to the point that it needs to be split into multiple repositories, then it’s a sign of over-engineering.
Because I’m lazy: I like to keep things as simple as possible, compile, test, containerize, and deploy from a single location.
5
I would like to have a tool that generates the project structure for me, but I haven’t found one that fits me yet.
In the past, I used
CCDS
, a project initialization tool mostly for Data Science projects.
It’s very good, but it’s not targeting full-stack developers as its core users.
Here’s the typical structure of a project with a frontend-backend architecture (I’ll go through each subpart later in this post):
project/
│
├── .github/
# GitHub Actions workflows for CI/CD pipelines
│   ├── workflows/
# Directory containing YAML files for automated workflows
│   └── dependabot.yml
# Configuration for Dependabot to manage dependencies
│
├── .vscode/
# VSCode configuration for the project
│   ├── launch.json
# Debugging configurations for VSCode
│   └── settings.json
# Project-specific settings for VSCode
│
├── docs/
# Website and docs (a static SPA with MkDocs)
│
├── project-api/
# Backend API for handling business logic and heavy processing
│   ├── data/
# Directory for storing datasets or other static files
│   ├── notebooks/
# Jupyter notebooks for quick (and dirty) experimentation and prototyping
│   ├── tools/
# Utility scripts and tools for development or deployment
│   ├── src/
# Source code for the backend application
│   │   ├── app/
# Main application code
│   │   └── tests/
# Unit tests for the backend
│   │
│   ├── .dockerignore
# Specifies files to exclude from Docker builds
│   ├── .python-version
# Python version specification for pyenv
│   ├── Dockerfile
# Docker configuration for containerizing the backend
│   ├── Makefile
# Automation tasks for building, testing, and deploying
│   ├── pyproject.toml
# Python project configuration file
│   ├── README.md
# Documentation for the backend API
│   └── uv.lock
# Lock file for dependencies managed by UV
│
├── project-ui/
# Frontend UI for the project (Next.js, React, etc.)
│
├── .gitignore
# Global Git ignore file for the repository
├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
# Configuration for pre-commit hooks
├── CON

data.title: LLM Inevitabilism
data.author: SwoopsFromAbove
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了与擅长辩论的人争论时的挫败感，强调了掌控对话框架的重要性。作者通过朋友的例子和阅读《监控资本主义时代》一书，引出了“必然主义”（Inevitabilism）概念。必然主义者声称某些未来不可避免，从而将讨论限定在如何适应这一未来，而非质疑或选择未来。科技界名人如马克·扎克伯格等常使用这种策略，将人工智能的发展描述为不可避免的趋势，隐含威胁意味。作者呼吁不要被必然主义框住，要主动思考和争取我们想要的未来，而不是被动接受所谓不可避免的未来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）技术的现状、未来发展及其社会影响

不同观点：
• lsy认为，LLMs作为一项新技术，虽然难以逆转其发展趋势，但目前尚未找到与其巨大投入相匹配的商业模式，且其能力正趋于平庸化，未来可能会在特定用例中找到较为平凡的位置。
• keiferski将AI inevitabilism（人工智能不可避免论）与历史上的宗教和哲学思想（如预定论）进行类比，认为这是一种心理模式的重复，即将自由和责任转移给一个强大的外部力量。
• delichon反驳lsy的观点，认为LLMs的广泛应用是不可避免的，就像智能手机的普及一样，无法通过主观愿望来回避。
• Animats预测可能会出现“LLM Winter”（LLM寒冬），即人们对LLMs失去信任，公司会试图将LLM错误的责任转嫁给消费者。
• dasil003指出，LLMs具有以前计算技术无法实现的功能，但同时也有很多人在炒作其潜力以获取利益。他主张应客观评估LLMs的能力，而不是被科技公司的高调宣传左右。
• mg通过个人经历说明LLMs的实用价值，认为其普及是不可避免的，就像互联网的发展一样。
• sircastor批评那些推动LLMs不可避免论的人往往是投入巨资开发和推广这项技术的人，认为他们的立场有利益驱动。
• tines表达了对未来社会的忧虑，担心技术权力集中在少数人手中，公众失去自主权和判断力。
• Workaccount2认为，人们喜欢用自然语言与计算机交互，LLMs是计算技术从“早期阶段”向更自然交互方式转变的第一步，因此其发展是不可避免的。
• trash_cat将LLMs的不可避免论与Timothy Snyder提出的“政治不可避免论”联系起来，认为这是一种剥夺公众代理权的语言策略。
• cdrini提出如何区分辩论技巧与真实思想，以及如何区分好的辩论与好的想法，认为即使出于不良意图的辩论也可能包含好的论点。
• ccortes批评当前许多初创公司都在做LLM相关项目，感觉缺乏创新灵感，认为这些项目非常泛泛。
• JimmaDaRustla强烈支持LLMs的不可避免性，认为那些否认AI和LLMs影响力的人是在“否认现实”，并提供链接以证明其观点。
• bloppe认为，LLMs的不可避免性假设是其能力将超越人类，如果这个假设不成立，那么LLMs的未来可能只是AI热潮中的另一个梦想。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是LLMs是否真的具有不可避免的发展趋势，部分评论者如delichon和mg认为其发展不可阻挡，而lsy和Animats则认为其未来可能有限。
• 另一个重要讨论点是LLMs的商业化问题，dasil003和sircastor指出当前商业模式不清晰，且有炒作和利益驱动现象。
• 还有评论如tines和trash_cat关注LLMs对社会和政治的潜在影响，担心技术权力集中和公众失去代理权。
• 技术不可避免论的心理和社会背景也被讨论，keiferski和cdrini将其与历史和哲学思想联系起来，探讨其背后的深层次心理模式。

44567857.article_content:
Have you ever argued with someone who is seriously good at debating? I have. It sucks.
You’re constantly thrown off-balance, responding to a point you didn’t expect to. You find yourself defending the weak edges of your argument, while the main thrust gets left behind in the back-and-forth, and you end up losing momentum, confidence, and ultimately, the argument.
One of my close friends won international debate competitions for fun while we were at university (he’s now a successful criminal barrister), and he told me that the only trick in the book, once you boil it all down, is to make sure the conversation is framed in your terms. Once that happens, it’s all over bar the shouting.
Earlier this year I read Professor Shoshana Zuboff’s fantastic book
The Age of Surveillance Capitalism
. I learned a lot from it (and I’m sure I’ll rave about it in more detail in other posts), including many new terms for phenomina that have long frustreated me.
Being able to put a name to something abstract allows you to more easily build an argument about it, explain the concept to strangers, and unify opposition to it. It’s a key success of Professor Zuboff’s book that it has introduced so many new terms to the lexicon.
The word that is relevant to this post is “Inevitabilism”.
People advancing an inevitabilist world view state that the future they perceive will inevitably come to pass. It follows, relatively straightforwardly, that the only sensible way to respond to this is to prepare as best you can for that future.
This is a
fantastic
framing method. Anyone who sees the future differently to you can be brushed aside as “ignoring reality”, and the only conversations worth engaging are those that
already accept your premise
.
“We are entering a world where we will learn to coexist with AI, not as its masters, but as its collaborators.” – Mark Zuckerberg
“AI is the new electricity.” – Andrew Ng
“AI will not replace humans, but those who use AI will replace those who don’t.” – Ginni Rometty
These are some big names in the tech world, all framing the conversation in a very specific way. Rather than
“is this the future you want?”
, the question is instead
“how will you adapt to this
inevitable
future?”
. Note also the threatening tone present, a healthy psychological undercurrent encouraging you to go with the flow, because you’d otherwise be messing with scary powers way beyond your understanding.
I’m not convinced that LLMs are the future. I’m certainly not convinced that they’re the future I want. But what I’m most certain of is that we have choices about what our future should look like, and how we choose to use machines to build it.
Don’t let inevitabilism frame the argument and take away your choice. Think about the future
you
want, and fight for it.

• keiferski将AI inevitabilism（人工智能不可避免论）与历史上的宗教和哲学思想（如预定论）进行类比，认为这是一种心理模式的重复，即将自由和责任转移给一个强大的外部力量。
• delichon反驳lsy的观点，认为LLMs的广泛应用是不可避免的，就像智能手机的普及一样，无法通过主观愿望来回避。
• Animats预测可能会出现“LLM Winter”（LLM寒冬），即人们对LLMs失去信任，公司会试图将LLM错误的责任转嫁给消费者。
• dasil003指出，LLMs具有以前计算技术无法实现的功能，但同时也有很多人在炒作其潜力以获取利益。他主张应客观评估LLMs的能力，而不是被科技公司的高调宣传左右。
• mg通过个人经历说明LLMs的实用价值，认为其普及是不可避免的，就像互联网的发展一样。
• sircastor批评那些推动LLMs不可避免论的人往往是投入巨资开发和推广这项技术的人，认为他们的立场有利益驱动。
• tines表达了对未来社会的忧虑，担心技术权力集中在少数人手中，公众失去自主权和判断力。
• Workaccount2认为，人们喜欢用自然语言与计算机交互，LLMs是计算技术从“早期阶段”向更自然交互方式转变的第一步，因此其发展是不可避免的。
• trash_cat将LLMs的不可避免论与Timothy Snyder提出的“政治不可避免论”联系起来，认为这是一种剥夺公众代理权的语言策略。
• cdrini提出如何区分辩论技巧与真实思想，以及如何区分好的辩论与好的想法，认为即使出于不良意图的辩论也可能包含好的论点。
• ccortes批评当前许多初创公司都在做LLM相关项目，感觉缺乏创新灵感，认为这些项目非常泛泛。
• JimmaDaRustla强烈支持LLMs的不可避免性，认为那些否认AI和LLMs影响力的人是在“否认现实”，并提供链接以证明其观点。
• bloppe认为，LLMs的不可避免性假设是其能力将超越人类，如果这个假设不成立，那么LLMs的未来可能只是AI热潮中的另一个梦想。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是LLMs是否真的具有不可避免的发展趋势，部分评论者如delichon和mg认为其发展不可阻挡，而lsy和Animats则认为其未来可能有限。
• 另一个重要讨论点是LLMs的商业化问题，dasil003和sircastor指出当前商业模式不清晰，且有炒作和利益驱动现象。
• 还有评论如tines和trash_cat关注LLMs对社会和政治的潜在影响，担心技术权力集中和公众失去代理权。
• 技术不可避免论的心理和社会背景也被讨论，keiferski和cdrini将其与历史和哲学思想联系起来，探讨其背后的深层次心理模式。

IntelliJ IDEA Moves to the Unified Distribution
Aleksey Stukalov
Read this post in other languages:
한국어
We are excited to announce the next step for IntelliJ IDEA: we are moving to a single, unified distribution. And yes, before you ask, our commitment to open source remains as strong as ever.
There will be just one IntelliJ IDEA installer, replacing the separate downloads for Community Edition and Ultimate Edition. In this new setup, all Ultimate features will still require a subscription to unlock. But even without a subscription, the IDE will remain fully functional, free to use for both commercial and non-commercial projects, and will include more features than the current Community Edition ever had.
In this article, we will walk you through the actual transition plan, what it means for your day-to-day development (spoiler: we expect it will only improve your experience), why we are making this change, how we are continuing to support open source, and other questions you might have about the new unified distribution.
The Plan for Transition
The move to a unified distribution will happen in several steps to ensure a smooth and transparent experience for all users. Here is how the transition will unfold and what it means for you. It will include three steps illustrated in the picture below.
Enabling CI/CD Pipelines and Open Source Builds on GitHub
We are making it easier than ever to build IntelliJ IDEA from source. To support open-source workflows and improve transparency, we will begin publishing open-source builds directly to
GitHub Releases
. These builds will include only the open-source components, as outlined in the
More Details About Open Source
section below.
We are also introducing ready-to-use CI/CD pipelines powered by GitHub Actions. With just a few steps, anyone can fork the project and produce a working build from the source.
This step is entirely non-intrusive and won’t affect your day-to-day workflow.
Introducing a Graceful License Expiration Experience
Starting with IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2, we are updating the licensing experience for Ultimate users. If your subscription expires, you won’t be locked out of the IDE. Instead, you will continue to have access to the full IDE, but with the feature set matching what is available for free (previously known as Community Edition).
This means your work will not be interrupted, even if your subscription lapses while you are on vacation or between renewals. You will still be able to open your projects, write code, and stay productive.
This step affects only users of IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and ensures a better experience in case of license expiration.
Migrating to the Unified Distribution
With the 2025.3 release, IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition will no longer be distributed as a separate product. Instead, all users will download a single IntelliJ IDEA distribution: one installer and one update stream.
If you are currently using Community Edition, your IDE will automatically update to the unified distribution via the usual patch update process. You will get access to additional features at no cost and a more seamless experience. You will also be able to try Ultimate features with just one click.
The change is minimal for Ultimate users: the IDE will simply be called IntelliJ IDEA without the “Ultimate” suffix.
The Way to Single Distribution
When we introduced IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition in 2009, it was an important milestone — not only for the IDE, but also for JetBrains as a company. For the first time,
we opened the source code of our IDE and provided a full-featured Java development environment for free
. It was a bold step, and looking back, one of our best. We remain proud of it!
The Community Edition became the foundation of our open-source efforts. It enabled millions of developers to start using IntelliJ IDEA and helped build a strong ecosystem of contributors, plugin creators, educators, and learners. For many, it was their first introduction to Java or Kotlin programming and IntelliJ IDEA.
Over time, though, the boundary between open-source and proprietary components blurred. Today, even the Community Edition includes some functionality that is not open source.
This was never the original intention
. These additions have been made gradually, one by one, to support real user needs. After years, they reached a critical mass that introduced inconsistency in what the “Community Edition” name was originally given to.
One of our longstanding goals has always been to provide a
smooth “out-of-the-box” experience
. That is what we continue to build. With the move to a single distribution, we want to honestly reflect the reality of what IntelliJ IDEA has become: a single, complete IDE that delivers the best experience for professional development with Java a

data.title: How the brain wakes up from sleep – and produces that morning feeling
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 一项研究揭示了大脑从睡眠中醒来的过程，特别是与随后困倦程度相关的脑电活动。研究记录了1,000多次苏醒过程，发现大脑前部的执行功能和决策区域首先被激活，随后觉醒波向后扩散，最后到达与视觉相关的区域。这表明醒来是一个从前到后的有序激活过程，而非简单的逆向睡眠。该研究由荷兰神经科学研究所的Francesca Siclari及其同事进行，使用了256个传感器记录参与者的大脑活动。研究结果有助于理解和管理睡眠惰性，即许多人按掉闹钟后感到的困倦感。文章发表在《Current Biology》上。

Electrical activity in the brain during awakening is linked with subsequent levels of grogginess.
Credit: Getty
How does your brain wake up from sleep? A study of more than 1,000 arousals from slumber has revealed precisely how the brain bestirs itself during the transition to alertness
1
— a finding that might help to manage sleep inertia, the grogginess that many people feel when hitting the snooze button.
Recordings of people as they woke from the
dream-laden phase of sleep
showed that the first brain regions to rouse are those associated with executive function and decision-making, located at the front of the head. A wave of wakefulness then spreads to the back, ending with
an area associated with vision
.
The findings could change how we think of waking up, says Rachel Rowe, a neuroscientist at the University of Colorado Boulder, who was not involved with the work. The results emphasize that “falling asleep and waking up aren’t simply reverse processes, but really waking up is this ordered wave of activation that moves from the front to the back of the brain”, whereas falling asleep seems to be less linear and more gradual.
The study was published today in
Current Biology
.
Sleeping-brain signature
The wide-awake brain shows a characteristic pattern of electrical activity, recorded by sensors on the scalp — it looks like a jagged line made up of small, tightly packed peaks and valleys. Although the pattern looks similar during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, when vivid dreams occur, this stage features a lack of skeletal-muscle movement. The peaks are taller during most stages of non-REM sleep, which ranges from light to very deep slumber.
Deep asleep? You can still follow simple commands, study finds
Scientists already knew that the ‘awakened’ signature occurs at different times in different brain regions, but common imaging techniques did not allow these patterns to be explored on a precise timescale.
To refine the understanding of awakening, Francesca Siclari, a neuroscientist at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam, and her colleagues studied 20 people as they woke from sleep. Each participant’s brain activity was recorded using 256 sensors on their scalps. Some awakenings were spontaneous; in other cases, participants were jolted awake by an alarm.

data.title: Tilck: A tiny Linux-compatible kernel
data.author: chubot
data.article_summary:
Tilck是一个教育性质的单体kernel，旨在与Linux在二进制级别上兼容，目前支持i686和RISCV64架构。其小规模、简单设计使其成为内核开发的理想实验平台，同时能够运行与Linux kernel相同的用户模式程序，如BusyBox。Tilck并非旨在重写或取代Linux kernel，而是利用Linux的程序和工具链来验证其正确性。与Linux不同，Tilck不针对多用户服务器或桌面系统，也不支持X服务器。

未来计划包括支持嵌入式系统、实时操作系统特性、ARM架构移植，以及对MMU-less CPU的支持。此外，还将增加基本网络和存储支持，目标是能够在如Raspberry Pi等SoC上运行。Tilck设计上极为轻量，可在仅3MB内存的QEMU虚拟机中运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tilck操作系统的特性、适用场景及其潜在价值

不同观点：
• brucehoult认为Tilck是一个介于xv6和完整Linux内核之间的有趣中间点，并指出它能够在LicheeRV Nano等廉价RISC-V板上运行，但也提到目前缺乏网络和多核支持。
• weinzierl强调Tilck是一个真正的操作系统，能够在真实硬件上运行，不同于那些只能在虚拟机中运行的操作系统，填补了一个长期存在的空缺。
• CaseFlatline对Tilck的快速启动和运行Doom游戏的能力表示赞赏，并提到开发者对CS学生的指导。
• marto1询问Tilck是否适合小型嵌入式设备，假设更换bootloader等组件。
• jlundberg对Tilck的README文件表示赞赏，认为它对操作系统开发者来说值得一读。
• netfortius从教育角度出发，询问Tilck对Minix用户的实用性。
