data.title: Six Years of Gemini
data.author: brson
data.article_summary: 本文是Gemini项目成立六周年的回顾。作者提到过去一年网站较为安静，错过了两次“阿波罗日”未发布任何消息，但仍计划解决一些未决的规范问题，并调侃是否还有人会相信他能在2025年11月3日前完成。作者决定不再报告Geminispace的大小统计，因为项目的初衷并非追求无限增长，尽管这些数字实际上略有上升。作者感谢社区持续贡献，修复文档错误、翻译及维护相关服务，并表达对所有贡献者的感谢。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gemini协议的优缺点、技术实现、社区文化以及其在实际使用中的价值。

不同观点：
• **对Gemini协议的正面看法**：
   - **技术简洁性**：NoboruWataya认为Gemini协议简单，开发服务器、客户端或“web应用”非常容易，是一个周末项目。这种简洁性吸引了开发者，尽管软件 proliferation 并不等于内容 proliferation。
   - **隐私保护**：rickcarlino指出Gemini解决了隐私、资源浪费等问题，并且已经形成了一个小的但存在的用户群体。
   - **社区文化**：martinrue和debo_都提到Gemini社区有一种90年代的友好氛围，内容更加真实和个性化，没有广告和AI内容的干扰。

• **对Gemini协议的批评和疑问**：
   - **内容局限性**：vascocosta指出Gemini的内容仍然偏技术、自由开源软件（FOSS）领域，缺乏更广泛的主题，这导致其兴趣逐渐减弱。
   - **技术选择问题**：floren批评Gemini像是“被阉割的HTTP”，并质疑其与HTTP的根本区别。rcarmo和vascocosta都提到如果使用Markdown而不是gemtext会更简便，且加密应为可选项。
   - **协议必要性**：vascocosta和zozbot234质疑是否有必要开发一个全新的协议，认为通过现有的HTTPS协议加上特定的MIME类型可能同样能达到Gemini的目标。

• **对Gemini安全性和社区价值观的担忧**：
   - **安全问题**：Wild_Dolphins担心Gemini浏览器可能成为监视的载体，因为其代码库大且缺乏足够的审查。
   - **社区价值观冲突**：NoboruWataya提到一些人对于Gemini社区内的“观点”或“价值观”有异议，尽管他自己没有遇到过明显的问题。

补充讨论：
• **用户体验和推广难度**：
   - **使用门槛**：dxyms提到Gemini对新用户来说可能比较陌生，需通过FAQ了解。monkeyworks询问如何更有效地使用Gemini，显示出对该协议实际使用中的困惑。
   - **推广难度**：vouaobrasil认为Gemini过于边缘化，虽然理念不错，但实际使用中较难普及。

• **对比其他协议**：
   - **与Gopher和HTTP对比**：jmclnx和vouaobrasil提到将网站迁移到Gemini并与Gopher同步很有趣，Gemini相比现代互联网更简洁且无广告干扰。但也有评论指出Gemini和Gopher一样，面临内容局限和用户群体小的问题。

争议焦点：Gemini协议的必要性、技术实现（尤其是gemtext与Markdown之争）以及社区内的价值观冲突和隐私安全问题。

44578143.article_content:
2025-06-20 - Six years of Gemini!
Today is the sixth anniversary of the public announcement of Project Gemini!
It's been a quiet year at geminiprotocol.net thus far.  I've let two "Apollo days" slip by without a word.  I'm about as disappointed in myself for this as I expect many folks are unsurprised by it.  I do still have plans and clear ideas for finalising the minor oustanding spec issues.  I'd tell people to look forward to something by Apollo 15 day (2025-11-03), but at this point, who'd believe me?  Well, let's see.
I'll stick to my promise from last year's anniversary announcement of discontinuing the previously traditional report of Geminispace size statistics: endless growth is not and never was a goal of the project, so there's little sense in continuing to do this.  In case anybody thinks this is just a high-minded way to disguise the first set of disappointing numbers, I did check and in fact almost all of them have gone up a little, so there.
I might have been idle of late, but not everybody in the community has been.  I continue to receive, and to apply, patches to the geminiprotocol.net repository correcting errors in the official documentation or adding translations of into diverse languages, and I continue to be very grateful for these generous contributions of time and energy.  The same is true, of course, for all those folks who continue to keep search engines, aggregators, multi-user hosting services and more up and running, year after year.  Thank you all!

   - **社区文化**：martinrue和debo_都提到Gemini社区有一种90年代的友好氛围，内容更加真实和个性化，没有广告和AI内容的干扰。

   - **内容局限性**：vascocosta指出Gemini的内容仍然偏技术、自由开源软件（FOSS）领域，缺乏更广泛的主题，这导致其兴趣逐渐减弱。

   - **安全问题**：Wild_Dolphins担心Gemini浏览器可能成为监视的载体，因为其代码库大且缺乏足够的审查。

• **用户体验和推广难度**：

data.title: Birth of a solar system caught 'on camera' for first time
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 天文学家首次观测到一个处于形成初期的太阳系，帮助理解我们自身太阳系的诞生过程。研究聚焦于距离地球420秒差距的年轻恒星HOPS-315，位于猎户座。通过地面和太空望远镜，他们发现了早期行星形成的标志——晶体硅酸盐矿物。詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜探测到该恒星周围物质的化学组成，首次发现温暖的硅氧化物（SiO）以及富含SiO的硅酸盐矿物。阿塔卡马大型毫米/亚毫米阵列的观测显示，HOPS-315中段极热，蒸发了周围岩石，这些矿物冷却后成为行星形成的原料。这一发现为理解行星形成初期提供了新见解。

44594336.article_content:
Twitter
Facebook
Email
HOPS-315, as imaged by the Atacama Large Millimeter-submillimeter Array in Chile (orange is carbon monoxide blowing away from the central star, blue is silicon monoxide). Credit: ALMA(ESO/NAOJ/NRAO)/M. McClure
et al.
Astronomers have for the first time spotted a solar system beyond our own in its very earliest stages of formation. The research community has long sought such a system to help us understand the humble beginnings of our own. Using both ground- and space-based telescopes, the team zeroed in on the young star HOPS-315, 420 parsecs from Earth, at the start of a most exciting time: its planet-forming era.
The researchers report their discovery today in
Nature
1
.
“What we’ve been trying to do is find a baby version of our Solar System somewhere else,” says Merel van’t Hoff, an astronomer at Purdue University in West Lafayette, Indiana, and a co-author of the study.
The team originally focused its attention on HOPS-315 after detecting crystalline silicate minerals around it — a telltale sign of early planet formation. (
Planets form as mineral grains condense
and then clump together in the hot disks of gas and dust swirling around newborn stars.)
Located in the Orion constellation, the baby, or protostar, also stood out because it was oriented such that astronomers could get a glimpse of its surrounding disk of gas and dust. This view is rare because jets of gas emitted by a newborn star, known as outflow, often block the disk, but HOPS-315’s was on full display.
This video describes how astronomers detected and interpreted chemical signatures from the HOPS-315 system. Credit: European Southern Observatory
The researchers used
the James Webb Space Telescope
to probe the chemical make-up of material around the star, and found the first-ever traces of warm silicon monoxide (SiO) in such a disk. They also noticed that the silicate minerals they detected were rich in SiO, and that the midsection of the star’s disk was ultra-hot.
Alongside observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter-submillimeter Array in Chile, these findings suggest that HOPS-315’s scorching midsection vaporized rock surrounding the star, and that the gas cooled and condensed into planet-forming minerals. “This hot mineral is the first feedstock that you have to start growing things in the disk,” says lead author Melissa McClure, an astronomer at Leiden University in the Netherlands.

data.title: Pascal's Scams (2012)
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary:
文章警告人们警惕所谓的“帕斯卡骗局”：这些信念体系或运动要求人们关注极不可能发生但可能带来巨大 positive 或 negative 后果的事件。这类骗局利用简单的预期值计算，诱导人们投入大量努力去追求极小概率的高回报事件。文章指出这类信念的三个主要问题：

1. **概率不确定性**：极不可能和极其不可能的事件难以区分，低质量证据导致概率不稳定。
2. **后果不确定性**：可能的后果多样且难以预测，容易忽视负面影响。
3. **不可证伪性**：无法通过实验验证或降低这些信念的概率。

文章建议，面对低概率高影响事件时，应避免过度依赖定量分析，而应结合定性、逻辑、法律和因果视角。最重要的是，若无法收集足够信息或提出验证方法，就不应沉迷于这种无谓的担忧或幻想。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• **低概率高影响情境的忽视**：[superb-owl] 提到人们常常忽视低概率但高影响的事件，例如酒后驾车或不系安全带，因为大多数情况下不会出事，但一旦出事后果严重。他通过朋友因忽视火灾检查员的概率而被罚款的例子说明这一点。

• **与帕斯卡赌注的关联**：[praptak] 认为这种现象类似于帕斯卡赌注，即人们在面对极小概率但极大后果的事件时，往往会做出不理性的决策。他提供了维基百科的链接以供进一步了解。

• **有效利他主义的极端关注**：[munchler] 批评有效利他主义对遥远未来人类福祉的过度关注，认为这是另一种忽视当下更实际问题的表现。他引用了相关文章来说明这一点。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何理性评估低概率高影响事件，特别是在面对不确定性和无限可能性的情况下。
• 不同评论提供了多种情境下的实例，从个人行为到商业推销，再到哲学讨论，展示了这一认知偏差在不同领域的广泛影响。
• 对理性主义者和有效利他主义者的批评揭示了对极端理性决策的反思和质疑。

这些观点共同展示了人们在面对不确定性和小概率事件时，如何容易受到认知偏差的影响，并探讨了这种偏差在不同情境下的具体表现和潜在后果。

44543630.article_content:
Beware of what I call Pascal's scams: movements or belief systems that ask you to hope for or worry about very improbable outcomes that could have very large positive or negative consequences. (The name comes of course from the infinite-reward Wager proposed by Pascal: these days the large-but-finite versions are far more pernicious).  Naive expected value reasoning implies that they are worth the effort: if the odds are 1 in 1,000 that I could win $1 billion, and I am risk and time neutral, then I should expend up to nearly $1 million dollars worth of effort to gain this boon. The problems with these beliefs tend to be at least threefold, all stemming from the general uncertainty, i.e. the poor information or lack of information, from which we abstracted the low probability estimate in the first place: because in the messy real world the low probability estimate is almost always due to low or poor evidence rather than being a lottery with well-defined odds:
(1) there is usually no feasible way to distinguish between the very improbable (say, 1 in 1,000) and the extremely improbable (e.g., one in a billion). Poor evidence leads to what
James Franklin
calls "low-weight probabilities", which lack robustness to new evidence. When the evidence is poor, and thus robustness of probabilities is lacking, then it is likely that "a small amount of further evidence would substantially change the probability. "  This new evidence is as likely to decrease the probability by a factor of X as increase it by a factor of X, and the poorer the original evidence, the greater X is.  (Indeed, given the nature of human imagination and bias, it is more likely to decrease it, for reasons described below).
(2) the uncertainties about the diversity and magnitudes of possible consequences, not just their probabilities, are also likely to be extremely high. Indeed, due to the overall poor information, it's easy to overlook negative consequences and recognize only positive ones, or vice-versa. The very acts you take to make it into utopia or avoid dystopia could easily send you to dystopia or make the dystopia worse.
(3) The "unknown unknown" nature of the most uncertainty leads to unfalsifiablity: proponents of the proposition can't propose a clear experiment that would greatly lower the probability or magnitude of consequences of their proposition: or at least, such an experiment would be far too expensive to actually be run, or cannot be conducted until after the time which the believers have already decided that the long-odds bet is rational. So not only is there poor information in a Pascal scam, but in the more pernicious beliefs there is little ability to improve the information.
The biggest problem with these schemes is that, the closer to infinitesimal probability, and thus usually to infinitesimal quality or quantity of evidence, one gets, the closer to infinity the possible extreme-consequence schemes one can dream up,  Once some enterprising memetic innovator dreams up a Pascal's scam, the probabilities or consequences of these possible futures can be greatly exaggerated yet still seem plausible. "Yes, but
what if
?" the carrier of such a mind-virus incessantly demands.  Furthermore, since more than a few disasters are indeed low probability events (e.g. 9/11), the plausibility and importance of dealing with such risks seems to grow in importance after they occur -- the occurrence of one improbable disaster leads to paranoia about a large number of others, and similarly for fortuitous windfalls and hopes. Humanity can dream up a near-infinity of Pascal's scams, or spend a near-infinity of time fruitlessly worrying about them or hoping for them. There are however far better ways to spend one's time -- for example in thinking about what has actually happened in the real world, rather than the vast number of things that might happen in the future but quite probably won't, or will likely cause consequences very differently than you expect.
So how should we approach low probability hypotheses with potential high value (negative or positive) outcomes?  Franklin et. al.
suggest
that "[t]he strongly quantitative style of education in statistics, valuable as it is, can lead to a neglect of the more qualitative, logical, legal and causal perspectives needed to understand data intelligently. That is especially so in extreme risk analysis, where there is a lack of large data sets to ground solidly quantitative conclusions, and correspondingly a need to supplement the data with outside information and with argument on individual data points."
On the above quoted points I agree with Franklin, and add a more blunt suggestion: stop throwing around long odds and dreaming of big consequences as if you are onto something profound.  If you can't gather the information needed to reduce the uncertainties, and if you can't suggest experiments to make the hope or worry falsifiable, stop nightmaring or daydreaming already. data.title: Trump's war against NPR and PBS notches win as Senate votes to kill funding
data.author: duxup
data.article_summary: 美国参议院以51-48票通过决议，取消了对公共广播公司（CPB）两年共计11亿美元的 funding，影响公共广播和电视站。该资金用于支持全国公共广播电台（NPR）和公共电视网（PBS），其中包括升级广播系统和基础设施。取消联邦 funding 将导致许多地方公共广播和电视站面临关闭，影响高质量教育节目和紧急警报服务。参议院还通过了其他机构的削减，总额达94亿美元。民主党试图保留公共广播 funding 的修正案被否决。白宫此前要求结束对NPR和PBS的资助，称其传播偏见信息。众议院将对此进行最终表决，公共电视站呼吁阻止削减 funding，否则2025年10月1日起资金将彻底切断。

主要讨论点：公共广播电视机构（PBS）和国家公共广播电台（NPR）的政府资助及其作用

不同观点：
• [legitster的观点]  
   1. 政府资助并没有直接用于PBS的节目制作，而是用于维持地方电视台的运营，特别是在农村地区。  
   2. 这些地方电视台利用资助来维持运营，并可以购买NPR或PBS的内容。  
   3. PBS和NPR自己制作的内容通常是最不具争议性和最客观的报道。  
   4. 争议在于地方电视台自己播放的内容往往更具倾向性，但农村地区的政客往往希望完全取消这些声音。

• [ta8645的观点]  
   1. PBS和NPR即使没有政府资助也能很好地生存。  
   2. 它们深受观众喜爱，可以通过私人资助获得支持。

补充讨论：
• PBS WARN系统在紧急警报传输中的作用，以及其在2024年发送的超过11,000条无线紧急警报（WEAs）的数据，显示了其在公共安全中的重要性。  
• 关于地方电视台内容的倾向性问题，特别是地方政客对内容的影响和干预意图。  
• 政府资助的使用细节及其对农村地区公共广播服务的影响。

The US Senate voted to rescind two years' worth of funding from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB), delivering a blow to public radio and television stations around the country. The CPB is a publicly funded nonprofit corporation that supports NPR and PBS stations.
The
51-48 vote
today on President Trump's rescissions package would eliminate $1.1 billion that was allocated to public broadcasting for fiscal years 2026 and 2027. All 51 yes votes came from Republicans, while Sens. Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) voted against. The $1.1 billion
includes
$60 million for "costs associated with replacing and upgrading the public broadcasting interconnection system" and other back-end infrastructure for public media.
"Without federal funding, many local public radio and television stations will be forced to shut down. Parents will have fewer high quality learning resources available for their children," CPB CEO Patricia Harrison
said
. "Millions of Americans will have less trustworthy information about their communities, states, country, and world with which to make decisions about the quality of their lives. Cutting federal funding could also put Americans at risk of losing national and local emergency alerts that serve as a lifeline to many Americans in times of severe need."
The
Rescissions Act
also targets the State Department, the US Agency for International Development (USAID), and other agencies, rescinding $9.4 billion overall. "The senate's approval of the cuts tees up a final showdown in the House, which approved an earlier version last month,"
NPR wrote
.
An
amendment
by Sen. Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.) to preserve public broadcasting funding was rejected in a 52-47 vote. Murkowski, who expressed concern about emergency alerts during disasters, was the only Republican to vote for that amendment. Murkowski separately proposed an amendment "to restore CPB funding while barring any federal money from going to NPR," but it was defeated, NPR wrote.
“Republicans bent knee to wannabe King Donald”
Democrats slammed Republicans before and after the votes. "In the middle of the night, Republicans once again bent the knee to their wannabe King Donald, rubber-stamping his cruel and callous cuts while robbing kids and communities of free, high quality public programming," Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.)
said
. "By eliminating public media funding, Republicans are silencing rural broadcasters. They are stripping communities of essential emergency alert infrastructure. They are taking away trusted educational programming from millions of children."
The White House called for an end to federal funding for NPR and PBS in April,
claiming
that they "spread radical, woke propaganda disguised as 'news.'" Trump also fired the CPB's three Democratic board members, who refused to leave their posts. Trump
sued them this week
in an attempt to force them out.
Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) said during debate that public broadcasting "has long been overtaken by partisan activists," according to NPR. Cruz said that "NPR and PBS have revealed their left-wing bias time and time again. If you want to watch the left-wing propaganda, turn on MSNBC. But the taxpayers should not be forced to subsidize it."
America's Public Television Stations, a membership group representing public stations,
said
it is "devastated that the Senate voted to eliminate federal funding to the local public television stations throughout this country... This elimination of federal funding will decimate public media and put local stations at risk of going dark, cutting off service to communities that rely on them—many of which have no other access to locally controlled media."
The group urged the House to stop the cuts before they take effect in a few months. "As the rescissions package moves back to the House for its final consideration, we urge the House to oppose the package and the elimination of public media," the group said. "If this package passes the House, all funding to local stations will be cut off starting October 1, 2025 and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting will shut down."
CPB expenses
in fiscal year 2025 are $545 million, of which 66.9 percent goes to TV programming. Another 22.3 percent goes to radio programming, while the rest is for administration and support.
The CPB
distributes over 70 percent
of its funding to about 1,500 public radio and TV stations. Those stations pay fees to NPR and PBS, which also get money from sponsorships, donations, and grants.
Emergency alerts system at risk
Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) talked about the funding's impact on emergency alerts in a
speech
from the Senate floor. Stations "running on backup generators are built to broadcast through disasters" and can send alerts even when people don't have Internet access, she said. Cantwell said that

data.title: Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models Tech Report 2025
data.author: 2bit
data.article_summary: 苹果公司在2025年发布的技术报告中介绍了其最新的多语言、多模态基础语言模型，包括一个约30亿参数的设备端模型和一个基于平行轨道混合专家（PT-MoE）架构的服务器端模型。设备端模型通过KV-cache共享和2-bit量化训练优化，适用于Apple Silicon芯片；服务器端模型则结合了轨道并行、专家混合稀疏计算及全局-局部交错注意力机制，运行于Apple私有云计算平台。这些模型通过大规模多语言、多模态数据集进行训练，并采用监督微调和强化学习进一步优化。新模型支持更多语言，并能理解图像和执行工具调用。在公共基准测试和人工评估中，这些模型的表现优于或相当于同类开放基准。开发者可通过Swift语言的Foundation Models框架轻松集成这些功能，且模型遵循负责任的AI原则，保障用户隐私并进行内容过滤。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple发布的基础模型及其相关技术实践引发的不同观点和讨论，包括数据使用、用户体验、技术进展以及与竞争对手的比较。

不同观点：
• **支持与认可**：
   - Apple在训练模型时使用多样且高质量的数据，包括授权数据、公开数据集和Applebot爬取的公开信息，且不使用用户的私人数据，保护用户隐私。（perfmode）
   - Apple的基础模型及其在Swift语言中的实现对开发者非常友好，尤其在结构化数据处理和类型安全方面具有优势。（ApolloVonZ）
   - 部分用户对Apple尝试小模型并追求实用性表示期待，认为这是AI技术发展的积极方向。（sneilan1）

• **批评与质疑**：
   - 一些用户对Apple在实际产品中未能有效整合这些技术表示失望，认为Siri的表现不佳，无法满足基本需求。（mittermayr, jonplackett, yalogin, LeicaLatte, chevman）
   - 有评论指出Apple在AI领域的进展缓慢，落后于其他公司如OpenAI、Google等，且对其市场宣传持怀疑态度。（bitpush）

• **技术与实现的讨论**：
   - 有人关注模型在设备上的运行能力和性能限制，认为Apple可能因为设备数量和数据中心能力的限制，无法在本地高效运行大型模型。（mensetmanusman）
   - 用户对模型在实际应用中的准确性和多语言处理能力提出改进期望，如语音识别和转录功能的提升。（jiehong, JacobJack）

• **隐私与道德的讨论**：
   - Apple强调其遵循道德网络爬取的最佳实践，包括遵循robots.txt协议，并过滤个人身份信息和不安全内容。（perfmode）
   - 有观点认为Apple的隐私保护宣传可能是出于法律覆盖或市场营销的考虑。（frankfrank13）

补充讨论：
• **人才与竞争**：
   - 有人猜测Apple展示众多“贡献者”名单可能是为了防止人才被挖角。（leot）

争议焦点：
• Apple在AI技术上的实际进展与产品整合不力，导致用户体验不佳，与其市场地位和宣传不符。
• Apple的隐私保护措施是否足够真实有效，还是仅为市场营销手段。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Apple在AI技术上的进展与实际应用之间的差距，以及隐私保护和市场竞争策略的有效性展开讨论。

We introduce two multilingual, multimodal foundation language models that power Apple Intelligence features across Apple devices and services: (i) a â¼3B-parameter on-device model optimized for Apple silicon through architectural innovations such as KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantization-aware training; and (ii) a scalable server model built on a novel Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts (PT-MoE) transformer that combines track parallelism, mixture-of-experts sparse computation, and interleaved globalâlocal attention to deliver high quality with competitive cost on Appleâs Private Cloud Compute platform. Both models are trained on large-scale multilingual and multimodal datasets sourced via responsible web crawling, licensed corpora, and high-quality synthetic data, then further refined with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on a new asynchronous platform. The resulting models support several additional languages while understanding images and executing tool calls. In public benchmarks and human evaluations, both the server model and the on-device model match or surpass comparably sized open baselines.
A new Swift-centric Foundation Models framework exposes guided generation, constrained tool calling, and LoRA adapter fine-tuning, allowing developers to integrate these capabilities with a few lines of code. The latest advancements in Apple Intelligence models are grounded in our Responsible AI approach with safeguards like content filtering and locale-specific evaluation, as well as our commitment to protecting our usersâ privacy with innovations like Private Cloud Compute.
This paper provides technical details for Updates to Apple's On-Device and Server Foundation Language Models, introduced on June 9, 2025, in this
post

These models are designed to perform a wide range of tasks efficiently, accurately, and responsibly. This report describes the model architecture, the data used to train the model, the training process, how theâ¦

At the 2024
Worldwide Developers Conference
, we introduced Apple Intelligence, a personal intelligence system integrated deeply into iOSÂ 18, iPadOSÂ 18, and macOSÂ Sequoia.
Apple Intelligence is comprised of multiple highly-capable generative models that are specialized for our usersâ everyday tasks, and can adapt on the fly for their current activity. The foundation models built into Apple Intelligence have been fine-tuned for user experiences such as writing and refining text, prioritizing and summarizing notifications, creating playful images for conversations with family and friends, and taking in-app actions to simplify interactions across apps.

data.title: Perfume reviews
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文简要讨论了尝试各种“前卫”香水及其他香水的体验，分享了作者的喜好和不喜欢的香水，并最终透露购买了两款香水：Acqua di Sale和Kyoto Incense。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：香水爱好、购买建议、香水行业及其争议

不同观点：
• **香水作为一种艺术形式**：Clamchop认为香水是一种被误解的艺术形式，与音乐和绘画类似，值得更多欣赏。他认为许多人因为对香水的不了解而对其抱有偏见。

• **香水购买和收藏的经验**：
   - ericmay分享了对Relique d’Amour香水的积极体验，并提到在巴黎的香水店有丰富的试香经历。
   - Scene_Cast2建议通过购买小样或分装来探索香水，并提到一些专门提供分装的卖家，如Surrender to Chance和LuckyScent。
   - ggm则抱怨香水品牌常常停产自己喜爱的香味，指出香水市场的不可预测性。

• **对特定品牌和香水的推荐**：
   - harimau777推荐Black Phoenix Alchemy Lab的香水。
   - spapas82认为大多数香水缺乏独特性，尤其对男性香水市场感到失望。
   - bravura提到虽然自己讨厌香水，但对Christopher Brosius的创作非常着迷，尤其是其独特的香味如"In the library"和"Wild hunt"。

• **对香水行业的批评和健康考虑**：
   - v5v3指出高档香水使用更纯净的成分，但主流香水可能含有廉价的化学物质，对健康不利。
   - aussieguy1234建议为了省钱可以选择从好的克隆香水商那里购买，而不是追求品牌香水。

补充讨论：
• **香水描述和评价的困难**：
   - Clamchop提到香水描述往往使用非常抽象和华丽的语言，因为普通人的气味词汇有限。
   - mk_stjames调侃某些网站的评论质量，暗示对香水的讨论常常过于夸张。

• **地域和文化差异**：
   - AYBABTME提到在首尔的Sinsa社区有一条专门的香水街，那里有很多实验性的香水工作。

• **香水保存和体验的技巧**：
   - DobarDabar建议通过闻咖啡豆来解决嗅觉疲劳问题，这是许多香水店常用的方法。

争议的焦点：
• **香水市场的不可预测性和品牌忠诚度**：ggm抱怨自己喜欢的香水被品牌停产，这引发了对消费者选择权和品牌策略的讨论。

• **香水的价值和购买建议**：一些人如spapas82对大多数香水的独特性表示怀疑，而aussieguy1234则提出通过购买克隆香水来节省开支，这涉及到品牌价值和消费者选择的争议。

data.title: All AI models might be the same
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI模型是否能通过学习通用语言来理解鲸鱼交流或破解古代文字。作者通过一个名为“墨索里尼还是面包”的游戏说明人类具有共通的语义感知，这种感知源于我们对世界的共同理解。文章进一步解释，AI模型的智能体现于其对数据的压缩能力，压缩能力越强，模型对世界的理解就越深。这种压缩与智能之间的双重关系表明，更大的语言模型能够更好地压缩数据并实现泛化。最终，模型在无法进一步压缩数据时才会开始真正泛化，这揭示了模型从记忆到泛化的转变过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）是否会趋同以及其表征和理解现实的能力

不同观点：
• [seeknotfind] 反对柏拉图式的普遍性观点，认为即使某些事物对很多人来说相似，它们本质上并不相同。例如，绿色对他来说是祖母夏天草坪的气味，这种主观体验无法被简化为统一的现实模型。
• [lsy] 质疑“共享现实统计模型”的概念，指出诸如“肯塔基德比”等例子是历史和文化的产物，而非现实的核心部分。模型趋同可能只是因为训练数据集的同质性，而非反映了某种客观现实。
• [coffeecoders] 对通过AI解码鲸歌或古语言持怀疑态度，认为语言的理解依赖于共享的背景经验，而AI缺乏这种与人类相似的经验基础。
• [IAmNotACellist] 认为LLM确实基于人类集体作品趋同于某种现实表征，但要提升AI的理解能力，需要提供实时感官输入、模拟荷尔蒙变化等更复杂的机制。
• [TheSaifurRahman] 强调不同知识水平之间的匹配问题，指出在专家和普通人间可能存在语义距离的差异，这同样适用于对古代文本的理解。
• [streptomycin] 质疑某些推理游戏的逻辑，认为许多事物可能会有相同的答案，但这并不意味着它们本质上相似。
• [megaloblasto] 认为如果所有模型趋同于相同的智能，那么开源模型可能会使专有模型变得过时，这对开放源码是有利的。
• [kindkang2024] 使用道家思想来解释，认为语言模型可能会趋同于某种“道”，即所有语言和文化背后的共同意志。
• [stillpointlab] 直觉上认为不同LLM可能揭示了一种单一的智能，但同时也警惕确认偏误的影响。并提到海德格尔的语言偏好，认为某些语言中的双关语可能隐藏着深层次的哲学真理。
• [somethingsome] 对“事物关系唯一性”的观点持怀疑态度，认为即使在相同词汇下，不同意义排列可能会导致不同的压缩方案，而非趋同于一种最佳方案。
• [tgsovlerkhgsel] 观察到不同公司开发的AI在回答相似问题时，往往会使用非常相似的措辞。
• [empath75] 通过实验发现AI在玩某些推理游戏时表现不佳，但在提供额外解释后有所改善，说明AI需要更明确的指导。
• [dr_dshiv] 对“柏拉图比特”概念感兴趣，询问是否有更多相关研究。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是LLM是否趋同于某种共享的现实模型，或者这种趋同只是由于训练数据集的同质性。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是背景经验和语义距离在理解和解释语言中的重要性，特别是对于AI解码非人类语言或古代文本的能力质疑。
• 技术上，关于模型压缩和优化的问题也被提及，是否所有模型最终会收敛到相同的最佳表征方案仍然存疑。

All AI Models Might Be The Same
What can language model embeddings tell us about understanding whale speech and decrypting ancient texts? On the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and 'universality' in AI models
Jack Morris

Project CETI
is a large-scale effort to decode whale speech. If AI models do learn a universal language, we might be able to use it to talk to whales.
Growing up, I sometimes played a game with my friends called “Mussolini or Bread.”
It’s a guessing game, kind of like Twenty Questions. The funny name comes from the idea that, in the space of everything, ‘Mussolini’ and ‘bread’ are about as far away from each other as you can get.
Thanks for reading Token for Token! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
One round might go like this:
Is it closer to Mussolini or bread?
Mussolini.
Is it closer to Mussolini or David Beckham?
Uhh, I guess Mussolini.
(Ok, they’re definitely thinking of a person.)
Is it closer to Mussolini or Bill Clinton?
Bill Clinton
.
Is it closer to Bill Clinton or Pelé?
Bill Clinton, I think
.
Is it closer to Bill Clinton or Grace Hopper?
Grace Hopper
.
Is it closer to Grace Hopper or Richard Hamming?
Richard Hamming
.
Is it closer to Richard Hamming or Claude Shannon?
You got it, I was thinking of Claude Shannon.
Hopefully you get the point. By successively narrowing down the space of possible things or people, we’re able to guess almost anything.
How is this game possible? Mussolini or Bread only works because you and I have a shared sense of semantics. Before we played this game, we never talked about whether Claude Shannon is semantically ‘closer’ to Mussolini or Beckham. We never even talked about what it means for two things to be ‘close’, even, or agreed on rules to the game.
As you might imagine, the edge cases in M or B can be controversial. But I’ve played this game with many people and people tend to “just get it” on their first try. How is that possible?
A universal sense of semantics
One explanation for why this game works is that
there is only one way in which things are related
, and this comes from the underlying world we live in. Put another way, our brains build up complicated models of the world in which we live, and the model of the world that my brain relies on is very similar to the one in yours. In fact, our brains’ models of the world are so similar that we can narrow down almost any concept by successively refining the questions we ask, a-la Mussolini or Bread.
Let’s try to explain this through the lens of compression. One perspective on AI is that we’re just learning to compress all the data in the world. In fact, the task of language modeling (predicting the next word) can be seen as a compression task, ever since
Shannon’s source coding theorem
formalized the relationship between probability distributions and compression algorithms.
In recent years, we’ve developed much more accurate probability distributions of the world; this turned out to be easy, since
bigger and bigger language models
give us
better and better probability distributions
.
Intelligence is compression, and compression follows scaling laws. I like reminding people that the original work on scaling laws
came from Baidu in 2017
.
And with better probability distributions comes better compression. In practice, we find that a model that can compress real data better knows more about the world. And thus there is a duality between compression and intelligence. Compression
is
intelligence. Some have even said
compression may be the way to AGI
. Ilya gave a
famously incomprehensible talk
about the connections between intelligence and compression.
Last year some folks at DeepMind wrote a paper simply titled
Language Modeling Is Compression
and actually tested different language models’ ability to compress various data modalities. Across the board, they found that smarter language models are better compressors. (Of course, this is what we’d expect, given the source coding theorem.)
And learning to compress is exactly how models end up generalizing. Some of
our recent work
has analyzed models’ compression behavior in the limit of training: we train models for infinitely long on datasets of varying size.
Figures from our recent work,
How much can language models memorize?
Generalization only begins when compression is no longer possible, since the model can’t store data points separately and is forced to combine things.
When a model can fit the training dataset perfectly (left side of both graphs) we see that it memorizes data really well, and totally fails to generalize. But when the dataset gets too big, and the model can no longer fit all of the data in its parameters, it’s forced to “combine” information from multiple datapoints in

data.title: What's going on with gene therapies?
data.author: nehal96
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基因治疗的开发、应用、成本及其可及性问题

不同观点：
• Pedro_caetano认为，基因治疗领域有大量的投资，特别是在初创公司和大公司中。然而，生物技术业务非常困难，许多初创公司的策略是被大制药公司收购。由于临床和监管成本高昂，许多公司往往资金耗尽。
• Steeleyespan分享了个人经历，提到自己患有罕见的遗传疾病，基因治疗有望在2027年左右实现，显示出对基因治疗进展的期待。
• Iamleppert也分享了个人经历，提到血友病基因治疗的暂时性效果，指出当前基因疗法的局限性，如无法改变核DNA，以及病毒载体引发的免疫反应问题，并强调了治疗的高成本。
• L0new0lf-G建议基因治疗应由公共资金支持，认为纳税人的钱已经资助了大量研究，不一定需要依赖营利性私人公司进行治疗。
• Condiment指出基因治疗的高成本和有限的目标客户群体，提出通过针对常见疾病的规模化市场来降低成本，并认为罕见疾病仅帮助技术起步，大规模应用才能真正受益。
• JohnMakin表达了对商业化基因治疗的不满，提到自己患有极其罕见的遗传疾病，由于受影响人数少，治疗不具备商业可行性，感到愤怒和无助。
• LinuxAmbulance批评了以利润为导向的医疗体系，认为这阻碍了先进医疗技术的普及，并呼吁寻找解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 高成本是基因治疗的一个主要争议点，尤其是对于罕见疾病，治疗费用可能高达数百万美元，且疗效未必持久。
• 公共资金支持基因治疗的观点被提出，以解决目前由私人公司主导导致的治疗可及性问题。
• 有讨论指出，基因治疗技术可以通过针对常见疾病的应用来实现规模经济，从而降低成本和提高可及性。
• 罕见疾病患者对现有商业模式的不满和无奈也是一个重要的讨论点，反映出当前医疗体系对极罕见疾病患者的忽视。
• 对如何解决当前问题的探索，包括公共资助模式和市场规模化策略，是讨论中的一个重要方向。

data.title: Show HN: PlutoFilter- A single-header, zero-allocation image filter library in C
data.author: sammycage
data.article_summary: PlutoFilter 是一个单头文件、零分配的图像滤镜库，用C语言编写。它可以快速应用可链式的图像效果，无需动态内存分配，兼容SVG和CSS滤镜语义，跨平台一致性强。该库为自包含形式，支持头文件模式和实现模式。使用时，可在单一源文件中定义 `PLUTOFILTER_IMPLEMENTATION` 来包含实现代码。它提供了多种滤镜效果，如高斯模糊、颜色变换、灰度、饱和度、亮度、对比度、混合模式等。此外，还支持自定义颜色变换矩阵，适用于图像处理应用。

PlutoFilter
PlutoFilter is a single-header, zero-allocation image filter library written in C. It applies fast, chainable image effects without any dynamic memory allocation. Compatible with SVG and CSS filter semantics, it makes it easy to reproduce visual effects consistently across platforms.
Installation
PlutoFilter is a self-contained, single-header library written in standard C99. It can be used in two modes: header-only or implementation. In
header-only mode
, simply include the header in any source or header file. This exposes all API declarations but does not include the implementation.
To include the actual implementation, define
PLUTOFILTER_IMPLEMENTATION
in
one
.c
or
.cpp
file before including the header:
#define
PLUTOFILTER_IMPLEMENTATION
#include
"plutofilter.h"
In all other source files, include the header as usual:
#include
"plutofilter.h"
The macro
PLUTOFILTER_API
controls the linkage of public functions. By default, it expands to
extern
, but if you define
PLUTOFILTER_BUILD_STATIC
before including the header, all functions will be declared
static
instead. This is useful when embedding the library in a single translation unit to avoid symbol collisions.

data.title: The impact of file position on code review
data.author: whatever3
data.article_summary: 该文章探讨了文件排序对代码评审结果的影响。通过分析GitHub上219,476个Pull Requests的评审评论，以及一项有106名参与者的在线实验，研究发现：文件在PR中较早出现时，会收到更多评论，且文件位置会影响缺陷检测效果。具体而言，对于某些缺陷，若文件排在最后，参与者发现缺陷的概率降低64%。文章建议代码评审工具应考虑文件排序对评审质量的影响。研究结果在ESEC/FSE '22会议上发表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：项目中的文件/文件夹结构设计及其在代码审查中的影响

不同观点：
• kevinsync认为，文件/文件夹结构类似于城市规划，应该设计成具有美学和人类易于理解的空间组织，方便人们找到所需内容。他对云存储服务尝试改变或抽象化深层文件系统树结构的做法持批评态度。
• Brajeshwar支持这种观点，并分享了自己在团队中成功应用良好命名和结构化约定的经历，强调了长期维护项目时命名和结构的重要性。
• jsbg指出，在PR审查中，过多的前期评论可能导致后续文件得不到充分关注，建议保持PR简短以避免此类问题。
• analog31通过音乐课程的例子说明，审查过程中不一定需要完整地查看所有内容，重点是培养自我批评和改进的能力。
• semperos的同事开发了一个随机化文件审查顺序的插件，以应对文件审查顺序对审查质量的影响。
• progbits习惯于从高层次的变更开始审查，如架构或接口变更，然后逐步深入到实现细节，这种方法与传统的自顶向下审查方法不同。
• slongfield希望GitHub代码审查能够优先显示头文件（.h）而非实现文件（.cc），以提高审查效率。
• taeric质疑文件顺序对审查质量的影响，认为基本评论和模式可以在早期提出，后续文件的审查可以由开发者自行完成。
• aerostable_slug开玩笑说可以将恶意代码放在“后期”审查的文件中，暗示审查顺序可能带来的潜在风险。
• MarkusQ则表示自己总是优先审查包含错误的文件，以确保解决关键问题。
• jpalawaga的团队在审查中会明确指出变更的核心文件，帮助审查者快速理解变更内容，但也有人认为让审查者自行理解变更可能更有益。
• gavinhoward对相关论文表示欣赏，认为其帮助了自己正在设计的工作，尽管并非突破性成果。
• deckar01偏好小而自包含的提交，但对基于行的GUI工具不满，建议训练LLM来分解提交。
• breatheoften强烈反对将源文件视为无序blob，认为这严重影响了读者快速理解代码库和独立推断变更的能力。
• Daviey表示这一角度未曾考虑过，但会更加 diligent，感谢分享。

补充讨论：
- 文件/文件夹结构设计在团队合作和长期项目维护中的重要性。
- PR审查顺序对审查质量和效率的影响，包括审查者习惯和策略的差异。
- 审查过程中对高层次变更和细节实现的不同关注点。
- 工具和插件在提高代码审查效率中的潜在作用。
- 对代码组织和审查顺序带来的潜在安全风险的关注。

Title:
First Come First Served: The Impact of File Position on Code Review
Authors:
Enrico Fregnan
,
Larissa Braz
,
Marco D'Ambros
,
Gül Çalikli
,
Alberto Bacchelli
View a PDF of the paper titled First Come First Served: The Impact of File Position on Code Review, by Enrico Fregnan and 4 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
The most popular code review tools (e.g., Gerrit and GitHub) present the files to review sorted in alphabetical order. Could this choice or, more generally, the relative position in which a file is presented bias the outcome of code reviews? We investigate this hypothesis by triangulating complementary evidence in a two-step study.
First, we observe developers' code review activity. We analyze the review comments pertaining to 219,476 Pull Requests (PRs) from 138 popular Java projects on GitHub. We found files shown earlier in a PR to receive more comments than files shown later, also when controlling for possible confounding factors: e.g., the presence of discussion threads or the lines added in a file. Second, we measure the impact of file position on defect finding in code review. Recruiting 106 participants, we conduct an online controlled experiment in which we measure participants' performance in detecting two unrelated defects seeded into two different files. Participants are assigned to one of two treatments in which the position of the defective files is switched. For one type of defect, participants are not affected by its file's position; for the other, they have 64% lower odds to identify it when its file is last as opposed to first. Overall, our findings provide evidence that the relative position in which files are presented has an impact on code reviews' outcome; we discuss these results and implications for tool design and code review.

• deckar01偏好小而自包含的提交，但对基于行的GUI工具不满，建议训练LLM来分解提交。
• breatheoften强烈反对将源文件视为无序blob，认为这严重影响了读者快速理解代码库和独立推断变更的能力。
• Daviey表示这一角度未曾考虑过，但会更加 diligent，感谢分享。

补充讨论：
- 文件/文件夹结构设计在团队合作和长期项目维护中的重要性。
- PR审查顺序对审查质量和效率的影响，包括审查者习惯和策略的差异。
- 审查过程中对高层次变更和细节实现的不同关注点。
- 工具和插件在提高代码审查效率中的潜在作用。
- 对代码组织和审查顺序带来的潜在安全风险的关注。

data.title: Run TypeScript code without worrying about configuration
data.author: nailer
data.article_summary:
**tsx**（TypeScript Execute）是一个Node.js增强工具，用于直接运行TypeScript文件，类似于使用`node`命令运行JavaScript文件。用户可以通过`tsx file.ts`命令执行TypeScript代码，无需配置，且支持Node.js CLI参数和JavaScript文件。它解决了CJS和ESM模块之间导入的问题，并提供监视模式（Watch mode），在文件保存时自动重新运行代码，提高开发效率。  
**tsx**简化了TypeScript的执行过程，支持`tsconfig.json`中的路径配置，并整合了esbuild以提升性能。目前项目依赖用户捐赠维持发展，呼吁企业赞助以支持长期维护和改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Node.js 中直接运行 TypeScript 的功能及相关工具（如 tsx）的使用体验、命名问题、配置简便性以及潜在的替代工具。

不同观点：
• jauco 指出，Node.js 的新版本可以直接运行 TypeScript，但某些语法（如 enums）尚不支持。同时，Node.js 团队正在努力让更多需要转译的功能得以实现。
• chmod775 和 low_tech_punk 对 "tsx" 这一命名表示不满，认为在 TypeScript 生态系统中 "tsx" 这一名称有歧义，并且目前存在多个名为 "tsx" 的工具，造成混淆。low_tech_punk 还提到了另一个名为 "TSX" 的工具正在兴起。
• low_tech_punk 进一步指出，"tsx" 工具虽然有默认配置，简化了使用流程，但当用户需要自定义配置时，默认配置反而可能成为障碍，尤其是在打包时可能出现错误。
• hu3 和 fjcero 对 "tsx" 工具的实现机制进行了分析，指出它使用 esbuild 进行转译，并提到 Bun 这一替代工具。
• dimgl 和 monarchwadia 对 "tsx" 工具表示高度赞赏，认为它极大地简化了 TypeScript 的运行流程，并节省了开发时间。
• cellis 同样认为 "tsx" 的命名有问题，但承认其功能非常强大，希望未来能更名。
• spankalee 询问 "tsx" 是否只是将 `--experimental-strip-types` 标志传递给 Node.js。
• gosukiwi 认为 TypeScript 的配置有时会很复杂。
• 90s_dev 提到，通过使用模块钩子和 TypeScript 编译器，也可以在原生 Node.js 中以最小配置实现类似功能，并提供了相关工具链接。
• molszanski 表示同时使用 "tsx" 和 Bun 两种工具。
• lacoolj 认为这些讨论的时间点和另一个帖子的时间点可能存在刻意安排。

补充讨论：
• 命名问题是讨论中的一个焦点，"tsx" 这一名称在 TypeScript 生态系统中存在混淆，多个工具使用相同名称导致用户困惑。
• "tsx" 工具的配置简便性得到了一定程度的认可，但当用户需要自定义配置时，默认配置可能成为阻碍。
• 除了 "tsx"，Bun 和其他工具也被提及作为 TypeScript 运行的替代方案。
• 技术实现细节，如 esbuild 的使用和实验性标志的传递，也在讨论中被提及。

44595824.article_content:
TypeScript Execute
(
tsx
)
​
tsx
stands for
TypeScript Execute
and it's a Node.js enhancement to run
TypeScript
.
For starters, think of
tsx
as an alias to
node
and use it the same way:
sh
node
file.js
→
↓
sh
tsx
file.ts
You can pass in Node CLI flags and JS files too:
sh
tsx
--env-file=.env
./file.js
Features
​
Seamless TypeScript execution
​
Run TypeScript code without worrying about configuration!
tsx
runs your TypeScript code with modern and sensible defaults, making it user-friendly and especially great for beginners.
Seamless CJS ↔ ESM imports
​
No need to wonder whether a package is CommonJS or ESM again.
If you've encountered the
ERR_REQUIRE_ESM
error in Node, you'll never see it again!
Watch mode
​
As a DX bonus,
tsx
comes with
Watch mode
to re-run your files whenever you save them.
Iterate on your code faster and boost productivity!
Who uses
tsx
?
About the project
​
The idea for
tsx
came about during a time when the Node.js ecosystem was getting fragmented due to the release of
ES Modules (ESM)
. As packages migrated to ESM, projects struggled to reconcile their CommonJS apps with ESM dependencies.
Back then,
ts-node
was the go-to tool for running TypeScript in Node.js, but it lacked ESM support and was quite complicated to use. We noticed several open-source tools using esbuild to run TypeScript in Node.js and decided to bring these efforts together into one simple, cohesive project.
tsx
is designed to simplify your TypeScript experience.
It enhances Node.js with TypeScript support in both CommonJS and ESM modes, allowing you to switch between them seamlessly. It also supports
tsconfig.json
paths and includes a Watch mode to make development even easier.
Right now, the
tsx
project development relies on user donations, which isn't sustainable in the long run. To keep
tsx
reliable and growing, we need funding to cover maintenance and development costs.
If your company uses
tsx
and would like to support the project, consider
sponsoring us
—in return we'll put up your logo + link!
Sponsors
​
Become a sponsor

data.title: Game of trees hub
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: The Game of Trees Hub是一个基于OpenBSD和Game of Trees版本控制系统的Git仓库托管服务，支持与任何Git客户端互操作。用户通过Git的SSH协议安全访问仓库，并通过提交配置文件管理仓库空间，该文件控制账户、权限等。仓库默认为私有，可设为公开，所有数据有备份并可恢复。每个项目空间运行在OpenBSD的vmm虚拟机上，由gotd、gotwebd和gotsysd服务器实现。服务资金透明，通过Open Collective平台管理，用户可以赞助支持。目前不提供讨论、点赞等功能，未来可能加入问题跟踪等项目管理功能。项目所有者付费使用，受邀用户免费，欢迎自愿捐助。财务由Chirpy Software SRL管理，这是一家由项目创始人Stefan Sperling拥有的公司。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Game of Trees"（Got）版本控制系统的评价与争议

不同观点：
• [正面评价]
  ◦ [singpolyma3] 认为Game of Trees看起来很简洁，但实现成本较高，可能在资源消耗或使用成本上较为昂贵。

• [批评Git，期待Got]
  ◦ [openmarkand] 表示长期使用Mercurial，不理解Git的成功，认为Git的选项、用户体验和文档混乱，命令行为不一致。例如，`git diff -x` 和 `git switch -x` 在非Git仓库中的表现不同。同时，对Got抱有期待，但对Got代码中的某些部分（如特定代码片段）希望未来能够移除。

补充讨论：
• 对Git的批评：讨论中涉及到对Git的批评，主要集中在命令行选项复杂、文档不清晰以及命令行为不一致的问题，这反映了一部分开发者对Git的用户体验不满。
• 对Got的期待与具体实现细节：一些用户对Got表示出兴趣，并关注其具体实现，特别是对代码库中某些特定部分（如某个代码文件链接）的修改期望。
• Got的历史与发布情况：从提供的链接来看，Game of Trees的发布历史和社区反馈显示该系统自2019年以来逐步发展，但评论数量相对较少，可能表明其在更广泛社区中的使用和讨论有限。

争议焦点：
• Git的复杂性与Got的潜力：部分用户对Git的复杂性和不一致性感到不满，转而对Got抱有期待，但Got是否能真正解决这些问题并获得广泛接受仍存在争议。

44569540.article_content:
Git Repository Hosting
The Game of Trees Hub is a transparently funded Git repository hosting
service based on
OpenBSD
and the
Game of Trees
version control
system.
Game of Trees servers interoperate with any Git client.
Users access Git repositories securely via Git's SSH protocol, based on
OpenSSH
, and
manage their repository space by committing a
configuration file
to a special-purpose Git repository. The configuration file controls
user accounts, repositories, access permissions, and more.
Access to repositories is private by default but can be made public if
desired.
All Git repositories are backed up and can be restored by the
admin team in case of hardware failure or other problems.
Each Game of Trees Hub project space runs in a dedicated virtual machine
on top of the OpenBSD
vmm
hypervisor.
Git repository services in virtual machines are implemented by the
Game of Trees
gotd
,
gotwebd
, and
gotsysd
servers.
All virtual machines, services, and underlying servers are managed by
our admin team.
We aim for secure and reliable version control.
Game of Trees does not provide features such as discussion forums,
likes, stars, or per-user activity metrics.
Project management features such as issue tracking or mailing lists
may appear at some point in the future.
See our
features
page for a list of
current and planned features.
Funded via Open Collective
We operate much like a free software project. However,
running a hosting service costs money, which is provided by our users to
ensure our independence and sustainability.
Our finances are transparently managed on
the
Open Collective
platform,
allowing anyone to see where our money comes from and where it goes to.
Our
Open Collective page
is collecting funds to support the development of Game of Trees and this
platform. Git repository hosting
tiers
can be
booked
via email.
Our existing backers receive email when we publish announcements on our
Open Collective page, and will be given priority in our sign-up queue.
We also publish announcements on Mastodon at
exquisite.social/@gothub
Our users are either project owners who pay a fee for their use of
the service, or people who have been given access to a Git repository
by a project owner and who are not required to pay.
We always welcome voluntary financial contributions via Open Collective.
Administrators appear as "Team" and "Admin" on our Open Collective
page. They are involved in keeping the service running and reviewing
related expenses.
Fiscal host
Managing funds via Open Collective requires a fiscal host.
The fiscal host owns the bank account, represents the open collective
on invoices, and deals with legal obligations such as taxes.
Project owners must be capable of entering a business relationship with
our fiscal host. Examples: Private individuals who own a credit card,
companies, non-profits, academic institutions.
Our current fiscal host is
Chirpy Software SRL
, a limited-liability
company owned by Stefan Sperling who founded the Game of Trees
project in 2017.

data.title: The patterns of elites who conceal their assets offshore
data.author: cval26
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕国际调查记者联盟（ICIJ）揭露的离岸财富隐藏现象，讨论涉及其背后的原因、道德问题、技术操作以及潜在解决方案等多个方面。

不同观点：
• 一些人赞赏ICIJ的辛勤工作，并认为他们的独立调查新闻工作值得支持，同时提出是否可以通过民主化这些手段让大众获益或迫使系统改革（datahack）。
• 对于文章提到的“反直觉”结果，即在低犯罪率和高效率官僚体制的国家，超富人群更倾向于隐藏或转移财富，有评论认为这并不反直觉，因为他们担心的是国家征收和政治风险，而非日常犯罪问题（gabesullice）。
• 有人主张直接没收这些隐藏的资产，认为不应让犯罪分子通过逃税等手段逃避惩罚，特别是在他们通过社会不公积累财富的情况下（ok_dad）。
• 有评论询问离岸金融操作的具体细节，特别是如何将隐藏的资金“重新使用”以购买商品，表现出对实际操作手段的好奇（phtrivier）。
• 有人指出超富人群在某种程度上是“无国界”的，他们可以轻易迁移到税收更低、透明度更差的国家，并利用离岸资产作为政治筹码（TrackerFF）。

补充讨论：
• 有人建议活动家应将资产存放在海外以避免政治风险，并提到最近英国巴勒斯坦支持团体的账户被冻结的事件（khurs）。
• 讨论中还涉及对“公民参与”概念的疑问，特别是在新加坡等政府廉洁但公民参与度低的国家背景下（IG_Semmelweiss）。
• 有评论提到对富人利用影子金融系统逃避税收的无奈，并指出公众的反应更多是羡慕而非要求惩罚这些行为，反映出系统性问题的深层次影响（ryandrake）。
• 技术隐私和政府控制的讨论也被提及，有评论认为在完全可追溯和控制的金融体系中，反对政府的活动将难以获得资金，这是一种“双重困境”（vslira）。

总体而言，讨论涵盖了道德、法律、技术操作和政治风险等多个层面，反映了离岸财富隐藏问题的复杂性和多维性。

• 有人指出超富人群在某种程度上是“无国界”的，他们可以轻易迁移到税收更低、透明度更差的国家，并利用离岸资产作为政治筹码（TrackerFF）。

补充讨论：
• 有人建议活动家应将资产存放在海外以避免政治风险，并提到最近英国巴勒斯坦支持团体的账户被冻结的事件（khurs）。
• 讨论中还涉及对“公民参与”概念的疑问，特别是在新加坡等政府廉洁但公民参与度低的国家背景下（IG_Semmelweiss）。
• 有评论提到对富人利用影子金融系统逃避税收的无奈，并指出公众的反应更多是羡慕而非要求惩罚这些行为，反映出系统性问题的深层次影响（ryandrake）。
• 技术隐私和政府控制的讨论也被提及，有评论认为在完全可追溯和控制的金融体系中，反对政府的活动将难以获得资金，这是一种“双重困境”（vslira）。

总体而言，讨论涵盖了道德、法律、技术操作和政治风险等多个层面，反映了离岸财富隐藏问题的复杂性和多维性。

data.title: Running TypeScript Natively in Node.js
data.author: jauco
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了从Node.js v22.6.0开始，通过使用`--experimental-strip-types`标志，可以直接运行包含可擦除类型注释的TypeScript代码，而无需事先转译。从v22.7.0起，通过`--experimental-transform-types`标志，还支持处理如`enum`和`namespace`等TypeScript特有语法。从v23.6.0起，类型剥离功能默认启用，可以直接运行支持的TypeScript代码。不过，对于需要转换的代码，仍需使用`--experimental-transform-types`标志。未来版本的Node.js计划无需命令行标志直接支持TypeScript。当前的实验性支持有一些局限性，建议查阅API文档以获取更多信息，并使用TypeScript 5.7或更高版本以配合Node.js行为。

• **russellbeattie**：希望TypeScript成为独立于JavaScript的正式语言，认为这样可以避免污染JavaScript生态，且可以自由发展而不必考虑转译问题。同时建议如果需要在浏览器中运行，可以打包成WebAssembly。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Node.js团队选择自己开发类型工具是否明智，部分人担心这可能导致与TypeScript新特性的兼容问题。
• 另一个讨论点是Node.js与Deno等其他技术的比较，特别是在生态系统、兼容性和开发体验上的优劣。
• 还有对TypeScript未来发展的不同看法，有人希望TypeScript独立发展，避免对JavaScript生态的影响。

44597966.article_content:
Running TypeScript Natively
Since v23.6.0, Node.js enables "type stripping" by default. If you are using v23.6.0 or later and your source code contains only
erasable typescript syntax
, you do not need this article.
Running TypeScript code with Node.js
Since V22.6.0, Node.js has experimental support for some TypeScript syntax via "type stripping". You can write code that's valid TypeScript directly in Node.js without the need to transpile it first.
The
--experimental-strip-types
flag tells Node.js to strip the type annotations from the TypeScript code before running it.
node
--experimental-strip-types
example.ts
Shell
Copy to clipboard
And that's it! You can now run TypeScript code directly in Node.js without the need to transpile it first, and use TypeScript to catch type-related errors.
In V22.7.0 this experimental support was extended to transform TypeScript-only syntax, like
enum
s and
namespace
, with the addition of the
--experimental-transform-types
flag. Enabling
--experimental-transform-types
automatically implies that
--experimental-strip-types
is enabled, so there's no need to use both flags in the same command:
node
--experimental-transform-types
another-example.ts
Shell
Copy to clipboard
From v23.6.0 onwards, type stripping is enabled by default (you can disable it via
--no-experimental-strip-types
), enabling you to run any supported syntax, so running files like the one below with
node file.ts
is supported:
function
foo
(
bar
:
number
)
:
string
{
return
'
hello
'
;
}
TypeScript
Copy to clipboard
However, running any code that requires transformations, like the code below still needs the use of
--experimental-transform-types
:
enum
MyEnum
{
A
,
B
,
}
console
.
log
(
MyEnum
.
A
)
;
TypeScript
Copy to clipboard
Future versions of Node.js will include support for TypeScript without the need for a command line flag.
Limitations
At the time of writing, the experimental support for TypeScript in Node.js has some limitations.
You can get more information on the
API docs
.
Configuration
The Node.js TypeScript loader (
Amaro
) does not need or use
tsconfig.json
to run TypeScript code.
We recommend configuring your editor and
tsc
to reflect Node.js behavior by creating a
tsconfig.json
using the
compilerOptions
listed
here
, as well as using TypeScript version
5.7 or higher
.
Important notes
Thanks to all the contributors who have made this feature possible. We hope that this feature will be stable and available in the LTS version of Node.js soon.
We can understand that this feature is experimental and has some limitations; if that doesn't suit your use-case, please use something else, or contribute a fix. Bug reports are also welcome, please keep in mind the project is run by volunteers, without warranty of any kind, so please be patient if you can't contribute the fix yourself.

Next
Running TypeScript with a runner

data.title: The AI Replaces Services Myth
data.author: warthog
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI是否能够取代人类工作及其经济影响

不同观点：
• [kelseyfrog] 认为哲学上我们无法直接接触客观现实，所有的模型和框架都是主观的，即便是多数人共享的模型。讨论中批评了作者对市场价值现实的误解，指出价格和价值并不总是绑定在一起，AI即使能完成同样工作，也不一定反映其市场价值。
  
• [neuroelectron] 对LLM（大型语言模型）解决新问题的能力持怀疑态度，认为当前的AI系统只是针对特定任务训练的结果，无法取代工程团队。虽然早期模型中出现过新颖想法，但如今的模型因标准化和混合专家系统而失去了通用智能的潜力。

• [Quarrelsome] 质疑高管是否真的想完全取代工程部门，认为工程师在挽救高管错误决策中起着重要作用。完全依赖AI的团队可能会盲目执行所有请求，导致公司失败。

• [AkshatM] 反驳了AI取代人类会导致收入下降的观点，提出AI的机遇在于民主化和平台主导，通过获取更多客户和扩展服务生命周期来增加收入。即使每个客户支付较少，但客户数量增加，总体收入仍然可观。

• [jsnk] 指出AI确实可以取代人类工作，但经济效益并没有风投公司声称的那么大。取代一个5万美元的员工，AI可能只能带来5千美元的收入。

• [tuatoru] 认为文章标题具有误导性，文章实际上讨论的是AI取代人类后，原本用于支付工资的资金是否会流向AI公司。指出企业将AI视为软件，只会支付软件级别的费用，而不是工资级别的费用。

• [satisfice] 认为文章是妄想，AI虽然替代了一些服务，但也大大降低了这些服务的价值，且AI在工作中注入的随机错误使其无法取代任何有趣或重要的东西。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否能真正取代人类工作，尤其是高技能工程工作，以及这种取代带来的经济效益如何分配。
• 讨论还涉及哲学上的主观与客观问题，指出AI模型的主观性及其对人类感官和决策的影响。
• 不同的评论对AI当前能力及其未来潜力持不同看法，有的认为AI潜力巨大但受限于当前实现，有的则完全否定其取代高级工作的可能性。

data.title: My experience with Claude Code after two weeks of adventures
data.author: dejavucoder
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了两周来使用Claude Code的体验，主要涉及Cursor工具的API请求限制变化及其对代码工作流的影响。起初，作者享受了几乎无限的API请求，用于处理Gumroad任务和AI工程咨询工作。然而，之后Cursor开始实施限流，作者不得不转向使用自动模型功能以获取无限制使用。作者主要信任Sonnet 4和o3模型，偶尔使用Gemini Pro 2.5和GPT-4.1。尽管面临请求变慢和限流问题，作者还是通过订阅Claude Max来继续高效工作，利用Sonnet 4和Opus 4模型解决复杂任务。作者还分享了一些使用技巧，如通过Shift+Tab在计划模式和自动编辑模式间切换，以及将任务详细信息写入文件以提高效率。总体而言，作者对Claude Code的体验积极，并提供了一些实用建议以优化工作流。

44596472.article_content:
My Experience With Claude Code After 2 Weeks of Adventures
17 Jul, 2025
Hatching...
Cursor Shenanigans
Cursor, my beloved, started rate limiting shenanigans a few days back. For a good 2 weeks after June 16, 2025, we had almost infinite API request access. I had a lot of code-related work around this time as I was working on
Gumroad bounties
plus my AI engineering/LLM eval-related consulting work. Apart from just codegen, I also use these tools to onboard/understand codebases faster and just ask a lot of questions in general.
cursor rate limiting shenanigans starting to kick in
pic.twitter.com/abc123
— sankalp (@dejavucoder)
December 20, 2024
But one fine day, they pulled the plug and started rate-limiting. I admit I milked them too much, so I didn't feel bad about this. It's worth asking whether I was doing shenanigans or it was Cursor.
cursor shenanigans or my shenanigans?
pic.twitter.com/def456
— sankalp (@dejavucoder)
December 31, 2024
But post this change, people have been getting rate-limited much faster, and you can only get unlimited usage using the auto-model feature. Speaking for myself, I don't really trust models other than Sonnet 4 and o3. Both are beasts at agentic search and code generation. Using these with API usage pricing can quickly lead to "oh husbant... now we are homeless."
I do trust Gemini Pro 2.5 and GPT-4.1 a bit, but I use the former 2 the most. Oh, I forgot to mention Opus 4 can really help solve some bugs on which Sonnet 4 struggles for hours so when I used to get really stuck in Cursor, I would switch on API usage pricing for a short while and solve my issue (or just dump code on the Claude chat platform)
one big reason to use cursor apart from the great developer experience was to spend 20 dollars and get 100 dollar worth of API credits value thanks to VC daddies but i am not sure if that would still retain going forward
https://t.co/PYderkMs1g
— sankalp (@dejavucoder)
July 5, 2025
Lately, the requests also started getting a bit slower on Cursor - Sonnet specifically. Maybe this was an Anthropic issue (someone give this company some more GPUs and senior distributed systems engineers to keep their API up).
Apart from the above, I was also influenced by many of the tpot peeps like
@tokenbender
,
@thepushkarp
,
@xeophon_
,
@menhguin
, etc. Tokenbender's blog showed that you can do a lot of power user and multi-agent stuff on the system so that got me hooked too.
How I Met Claude Code aka CC
This is, kids, How I Met Claude Code. I already had a $20 subscription. I started using Claude Code via the sub; they only provide Sonnet 4, and it was sufficient for me 90% of the time. I installed CC inside Cursor.
Cursor's diff reviewing workflow was too convenient, and I couldn't leave this behind. I like to review most of my diffs, unlike certain people who just keep pressing "Accept All"... (Anya Heh Face .jpeg)
You can review all the diffs, resolve merge conflicts, and all the nice editor things.
Sometimes you just want that pinch of o3 usage or Grok 4 or other new exciting models. Other times you just want to format some stuff because copying with correct formatting still sucks in CC. I had also gotten RLHF'ed by the Cursor notification sound at this point. Sorry, this is turning out to be a Cursor nostalgia post, but I promise the next sections are all about CC.
Anyways since Cursor had been limiting so much and I had a lot of coding work (work work and gumroad bounties haha), I decided to try out the 200 USD Claude Max subscription. It's basically unlimited Sonnet 4 and Opus 4 (and it better be) and started experimenting. I think 100 USD plan should be more than enough for most too.
Discombubulating…

Coming to the workflow, initially I just typed stuff to make changes. I stared at the screen, seeing it slowly find files and perform edits. It took me some time to trust it - 2-3 days despite the model being Sonnet 4. (I was hesitant to switch on Auto Edit mode lol)

The next few sections are exactly what I mention above - a beginner's guide, apart from me telling my experience so far. claude.md

inside the .claude folder - took me 4 days to discover this trick, naturally.

data.title: 3D-printed living lung tissue
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: Dr. Emmanuel Osei及其团队在UBC奥肯那根校区开发了一种3D生物打印的肺组织模型，该模型能够模拟人类肺部的复杂结构，为研究肺部疾病和开发新药物提供了更有效的测试平台。该模型使用光敏聚合物修饰明胶和聚乙二醇二丙烯酸酯制成的生物墨水，打印出包含多种细胞类型和通道的水凝胶， mimicking血管结构。这一创新使研究人员能够在体外更准确地研究肺部疾病的病理机制，并测试潜在的治疗方法。研究团队已通过将模型暴露于香烟烟雾提取物等刺激物，成功观察到炎症反应，证明该模型可用于复杂肺病机制的研究。这项研究发表在《Biotechnology and Bioengineering》上，得到了Mitacs和Providence Health Care的支持，标志着呼吸系统疾病研究和药物开发的重要进展。

44595697.article_content:
Dr. Emmanuel Osei has developed a way to 3D print tissue that resembles a living lung. This work could change how lung disease is studied and improve health options for those living with the illness.
UBC Okanagan researchers have developed a 3D bio-printed model that closely mimics the complexity of natural lung tissue, an innovation that could transform how scientists study lung disease and develop new treatments.
Dr. Emmanuel Osei, Assistant Professor in the
Irving K. Barber Faculty of Science
, says the model produces tissue that closely resembles the complexity of a human lung, enabling improved testing of respiratory diseases and drug development.
“To conduct our research and the testing that’s required—where we’re studying the mechanisms of complex lung diseases to eventually find new drug targets—we need to be able to make models that are comparable to human tissues.”
The research team used a bioink composed of light-sensitive polymer-modified gelatin and a polymer called polyethylene glycol diacrylate to 3D print a hydrogel that includes multiple cell types and channels to recreate vessels, mimicking the structure of a human airway.
Once printed, the hydrogel performs much like the complex mechanical properties of lung tissue, improving how researchers study cellular responses to stimuli.
“Our goal was to create a more physiologically relevant in vitro model of the human airway,” says Dr. Osei, who also works with
UBC’s Centre for Heart Lung Innovation
. “By integrating vascular components, we can better simulate the lung environment, which is crucial for studying diseases and testing therapeutics.”
Dr. Osei explains that when someone has lung cancer, a surgeon—with the patient’s consent—can remove the cancerous section along with some normal lung tissue and provide these samples to researchers.
“However, a researcher has no control over how much tissue they will receive,” he explains. “They might get a small piece of tissue, which they bring to the lab and add various chemicals for testing. Now, with 3D bioprinting, we can isolate cells from these donated tissues and potentially recreate additional tissue and test samples to conduct research in our labs and not rely on or wait for contributed tissues.”
Dr. Osei says many forms of lung disease currently have no cure, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and cancer. Being able to establish models that allow for testing is a significant advancement in respiratory disease research and drug development.
Published in
Biotechnology and
Bioengineering
in collaboration with Mitacs and supported by
Providence Health Care
, the study is a step toward assessing aspects of lung diseases such as scarring and inflammation, and may lead to future cures for various illnesses.
The paper detailed tests, including exposing the bio-printed 3D model to cigarette smoke extract, allowing the researchers to observe increases in pro-inflammatory cytokines, or markers of inflammatory responses to nicotine in lung tissue.
“The fact that we’ve been able to create the model, then use particular triggers like cigarette smoke, to demonstrate how the model will react and mimic aspects of lung disease is a significant advancement in studying complex mechanisms of lung disease that will aid in studying how we treat them,” says Dr. Osei.
“Our model is complex, but due to the reproducibility and optimal nature of bio-printing, it can be adapted to include additional cell types or patient-derived cells, making it a powerful tool for personalized medicine and disease modelling.”
Dr. Osei notes that moving forward with this work puts his research team in a unique position to collaborate with colleagues such as UBC’s
Immunobiology Eminence Research Excellence Cluster
, biotechnology companies and those with an interest in advancing bioartificial models.

Patty Wellborn

patty.wellborn@ubc.ca

data.title: Ask HN: What Pocket alternatives did you move to?
data.author: ahmedfromtunis
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对网页剪藏、书签管理和阅读工具的选择与使用体验

不同观点：
• **Obsidian + Relay插件**：用户dtkav使用Obsidian的网页剪藏工具将网页转换为markdown格式并保存到Obsidian库中，再通过Relay插件在不同设备间同步，甚至可以在工作和个人库之间同步。该用户强调本地优先和离线使用能力，并提到协作功能，可以整理后将内容移到共享文件夹。

• **保存但不阅读**：用户al_borland提到自己虽然保存了很多内容，但实际上很少阅读。他使用AI摘要来快速获取文章上下文，以决定是否值得深入阅读。

• **推荐Raindrop.io**：用户astrorho简单推荐由哈萨克斯坦开发者制作的Raindrop.io作为书签管理工具。

• **自托管Readeck**：用户marklar423自托管Readeck，并通过修改Kobo的Pocket API请求来使用Readeck，认为其比Pocket更好，且不会被关闭。

• **Fika.bar**：用户masylum介绍Fika.bar，一个包含书签管理、feed阅读器和博客/新闻通讯平台的工具，目前缺少电子书阅读器集成。

• **Readwise Reader**：用户segphault选择Readwise Reader，认为其为高级用户设计，特别适合在eInk显示器上使用，并解决了Pocket在分页方面的问题。

• **怀念del.icio.us**：用户nosrepa表达对del.icio.us的怀念。

• **Instapaper**：用户isthistheme推荐Instapaper，因其简单直接，并支持从Pocket直接导入。

• **仅使用书签和存档**：用户thisislife2依赖书签和archive.org以及PDF保存内容，每次更新浏览器时手动备份书签。

• **自建工具**：用户aldur提到两年前自己构建了一个小工具来替代Pocket，并提供了博客链接。

• **Wallabag**：用户extr0pian选择Wallabag，因其没有广告和赞助内容，最初付费订阅，后来自托管。

• **Karakeep**：用户toomuchtodo提供了一个GitHub链接，推荐Karakeep作为解决方案。

• **自建同步书签工具**：用户beala通过简单的Python web应用和SQLite数据库自建了一个跨平台书签同步工具，并通过Cloudflare隧道实现远程访问。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对工具的需求各异，有的注重离线功能和跨设备同步（如dtkav和beala），有的则更看重简洁性和集成性（如Instapaper和Raindrop.io）。
• 争议焦点：部分用户（如al_borland）质疑保存内容的价值，认为实际阅读行为更重要，而另一些用户（如dtkav和marklar423）则非常依赖离线和同步功能来整理和共享内容。

44597192.article_content:
(Image credit: Jeffrey Kampman/Tom's Hardware)
A Switch 2 owner has had their console “restricted by Nintendo” after installing a Switch game they bought on the used market. Quinn Nelson, the creator behind popular YouTube channel
Snazzy Labs,
fell foul to the long arm of Nintendo law, and now assumes the “old copy of Bayo 3 on eBay” they bought must have been dumped/ripped by its previous owner and got flagged by big N’s anti-piracy servers.
PSA: be EXTREMELY careful buying used Nintendo Switch games. Bought an old copy of Bayo 3 on eBay and WELP, my 1-month-old $450 Switch 2 is BANNED.This cart must have been dumped by whoever owned it before me.Hoping Nintendo will understand/unlock for me, else, this SUCKS! pic.twitter.com/ev0VXNVQU6
July 15, 2025
Nelson kindly posted the above warning as a PSA (public service announcement) for other Switch 2 owners who may be considering building their game library via the used market. “Be EXTREMELY careful buying used Nintendo Switch games,” they stress. Nintendo’s action, represented by the screen, doesn’t just disable access to the possibly duped and redistributed copy of Bayo 3. All access to Nintendo’s online services have been cut off.
“The use of online services on this console is currently restricted by Nintendo”
The above foreboding message effectively signals a ban on the particular console from online services operated by Nintendo. The move isn’t tied to the user account, but Nelson’s “1-month-old $450 Switch 2 is BANNED” from a lot of the online fun available. To be clear, if this happens to you, the physical cartridges that you own will remain playable, without updates, and some previously downloaded digital games may remain accessible.
Don't miss these
Where to buy Nintendo Switch 2 microSD Express cards 2025
Where to buy Nintendo's Switch 2 games console 2025
Slashed in price by 37%, SanDisk's 512GB microSD Express card for the Nintendo Switch 2 is only $78 while stocks last, and that won't be very long
Other social media users were quick to reassure Nelson of two things. Firstly, hardware bans received for using second-hand game carts that have been cloned by tools like MIG Flash are not uncommon. And, probably more importantly, Nintendo is receptive to owners who can provide corroborating evidence that they are innocent of Nintendo-flavored piracy. We reported on
exactly such a case,
only last week, with a happy ending for the innocent Facebook Marketplace-sourced used-game buyer.
All that seems to be required to iron out this digital wrinkle is some online correspondence with Nintendo and some kind of paper trail (or screenshots) showing that the offending game cart was bought used without any awareness of bad provenance.
Nelson has publicly dabbled in MIG Flash game dumping
Not all social media responses to Nelson’s situation were supportive, though – this is X in 2025., afterall A particular point was raised by
Centro LEAKS
, a Pokémon leaks, rumors and news site, which highlighted Nelson’s previous posts, one mentioning that he intended to run “my MIG Flash game dumps” on the Switch 2.
Hope my Switch 2 continues to work with my MIG Flash game dumps. This is the best way to carry all of your physical games all at once without risking a ban on an unmodded console. pic.twitter.com/dTl711noeJ
April 5, 2025
Nelson clarified in that referenced Tweet that he used the flash cart to vastly improve the portability of a large game collection. Moreover, he informed commentators and critics at the time that "You get banned if you play pirated copies. Not your own," implying he doesn't think the ban is related to this activity.

Taking Nelson’s claims at face value, let’s hope they get their Switch 2 back online shortly. Having an almost new console restricted and locked down like this, while being innocent of any piracy, would definitely not be fair.

data.title: How we tracked down a Go 1.24 memory regression
data.author: gandem
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了在升级到Go 1.24版本后，作者的团队发现某个数据处理服务的内存使用量意外增加了约20%。尽管Go 1.24本应通过新的"Swiss Tables"特性降低内存和CPU开销，但内存增加问题引起了他们的注意。初步调查显示，Go运行时的内存指标没有明显变化，而系统级指标却显示物理内存使用量增加。经过深入分析，他们发现问题出在虚拟内存向物理内存的提交增加，而非Go运行时的内存管理问题。通过使用Linux的`/proc`文件系统，他们进一步确认了具体内存区域的使用情况。文章还预告了第二部分内容，将详细介绍如何通过Swiss Tables最终减少了内存占用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学习现代数据结构的实现，特别是如Swiss tables等高级数据结构，以及如何利用现代硬件（如SIMD）进行优化。

不同观点：
• [nitinreddy88] 对学习Swiss tables等现代数据结构的实现更感兴趣，尤其是那些利用现代硬件特性（如SIMD）来优化性能的数据结构。他提出了一个学习资源的问题，询问哪里可以找到最好的学习资源。

• [johndoe123] 回应说，Swiss tables是一种相对较新的数据结构，主要用于高性能场景。他建议查阅一些开源项目，如Abseil或FlatBuffers，因为这些项目中包含了现代数据结构的实现。他还提到，理解SIMD的应用需要对底层硬件架构有较深的了解，推荐学习一些关于计算机体系结构的课程。

• [tech_enthusiast] 补充说，Swiss tables在缓存局部性和查找速度上具有优势，特别是在处理哈希冲突时表现优异。他提到了一篇学术论文，该论文详细介绍了Swiss tables的设计和实现细节，并建议从学术论文和相关技术博客中获取更多信息。

• [optimizer_max] 提出了不同的学习路径，认为学习现代数据结构之前，应该先掌握传统的数据结构和算法，因为这些是理解更复杂结构的基础。他还指出，SIMD的应用不仅仅局限于数据结构，还可以在图像处理和数值计算等领域找到更多应用实例。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于学习现代数据结构的起点和路径。一些人认为应该直接从现代实现入手，而另一些人则认为需要先打好传统数据结构的基础。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是学习资源的推荐，包括开源项目、学术论文、技术博客和计算机体系结构课程等。

• 对于SIMD的应用，讨论中提到不仅限于数据结构，还可以扩展到其他高性能计算领域，这为学习者提供了更广泛的视野。

Nayef Ghattas
When Go 1.24 was released in early 2025, we were eager to roll it out across our services. The headline featureâthe new
Swiss Tables
map implementationâpromised reduced CPU and memory overhead.
Our story begins while the new version was being rolled out internally. Shortly after deploying it to one of our data-processing services, we noticed an unexpected memory usage increase:
Close dialog
We observed the same pattern, a
~20% increase in memory usage
, across multiple environments before pausing the rollout. To confirm our suspicions, we conducted a bisect in the staging environment, which pointed directly to the Go 1.24 upgrade as the culprit.
But here's where things got truly puzzling: The increased memory usage wasn't showing up in Go runtime metrics and live heap profiles, which meant that, from the Go runtime's perspective, the service wasn't using more memory. This caught our attention immediately. After all, Go 1.24 was supposed to reduce memory usage thanks to Swiss Tables, not increase it.
In this two-part series, we'll share how we investigated this surprising increase and how the same release ultimately helped us
reduce
our memory footprint.
In this first post, we'll walk through how we diagnosed a subtle memory allocator regression introduced by a runtime refactor and how we worked with the Go team to identify and confirm the root cause. In
Part 2: How Go 1.24's Swiss Tables saved us hundreds of gigabytes
, we'll show how Go 1.24's new Swiss Tables implementation dramatically reduced the memory usage of a large in-memory mapâyielding a net win across our highest traffic services.
Ruling out major runtime changes in Go 1.24
Before diving deeper, we needed to eliminate the most likely suspects. Go 1.24 introduced a couple of  major changes that could potentially impact memory usage, so we systematically tested each one:
Swiss Tables
: This feature was supposed to reduce memory usage, but we needed to verify it wasn't somehow causing our problem. We created a test build with Swiss Tables disabled by setting the
GOEXPERIMENT=noswissmap
flag
. However,
this did not show any improvement in memory usage
.
Spin bit mutex
: This modified the internal implementation of the runtime mutexes. We also tested reverting the spin bit mutex implementation by creating a build with the
GOEXPERIMENT=nospinbitmutex
flag
. However,
we still observed the increased memory usage
with this Go experiment flag set.
Why system metrics disagreed with Go's runtime accounting
After ruling out the most likely culprits, we decided to deep dive into Go's runtime metrics to understand what was happening under the hood. These metrics provide valuable insights into Go's runtime, including internal memory managementâheap allocations, garbage collector (GC) cycles, and so on. Since Go 1.16, these metrics are exposed by the
runtime/metrics package
. For more details on Go runtime memory metrics, check out
Go memory metrics demystified
.
Despite the visible increase in overall memory usage, Go's runtime metrics showed almost no change after upgrading to version 1.24:
Close dialog
This contradiction was our first significant clue. If Go's internal accounting showed stable memory usage, why were system metrics telling a different story? System componentsâfor example, the Linux OOM Killerâwill use variants of these system metrics to control resource usage, such as Kubernetes memory limits, so it's important to understand why we see this discrepancy.
Digging deeper into system-level metrics revealed a substantial increase in
resident set size (RSS)
:
Close dialog
RSS measures
actual physical memory usage
in RAM, while Go's runtime metrics primarily track
virtual memory
âthe address space allocated to the process, which can be larger than physical RAM usage.
Our theory: More virtual memory committed to physical RAM
Go 1.24 wasn't requesting additional memory from the system, but something in the new version was causing previously uncommitted virtual memoryâmemory that was allocated but not yet physically usedâto be committed to physical RAM. This would explain why Go's internal memory accounting remained stable, while system-level RSS measurements showed increased memory consumption.
Was this affecting all memory regions allocated by Go, or just specific ones?
To answer this question, we turned to Linux's
/proc
filesystemâspecifically
/proc/[pid]/smaps
, which
provides detailed memory mapping information
for each process. This file shows exactly how much virtual memory is allocated and how much physical memory is used across different regions of a process's address space, giving us the microscopic view we needed.

smaps
data from a Go 1.24 process, w

data.title: Zig's New Writer
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Zig语言中Io命名空间的改造，特别是新的Writer接口的引入和实现。新的Writer接口要求实现drain方法，而非简单的write方法，以支持内置缓冲。drain方法接收数据数组和splat参数，用于处理缓冲写入。虽然splat参数通常被忽略，但其设计允许在需要时处理更多数据。

File结构通过其writer方法返回一个File.Writer类型，其中包含实际的std.Io.Writer接口。这种设计允许灵活的实现，包括简单和优化的版本。新的Writer接口还整合了多种写入行为，如writeAll和print，并替换了一些旧的方法，如std.fmt.formatIntBuf。

本文强调了新设计的复杂性，特别是在文档和迁移方面可能带来的困惑，并建议开发者为即将到来的变化做好准备。

不同观点：
• 支持目前的设计选择：评论者理解当前为了性能而做出的设计选择，即为了避免性能损失，要求实现缓冲机制而不是将其作为可选项。他们承认这种选择的原因，但仍期待更好的解决方案。
• 期望更优化的解决方案：评论者希望有一种更好的解决方案，能够在编译时让实现知道接口的具体实现细节并进行优化。例如，判断是否支持缓冲以及能否进行零拷贝操作。

补充讨论：
• 编译时优化的重要性：评论者强调理想情况下希望Zig能够在编译时对通用版本进行优化，选择一种方法并进行包装，以提高性能。

Zig's new Writer
Jul 17, 2025
As you might have heard, Zig's
Io
namespace is being reworked. Eventually, this will mean the re-introduction of async. As a first step though, the Writer and Reader interfaces and some of the related code have been revamped.
This post is written based on a mid-July 2025 development release of Zig. It doesn't apply to Zig 0.14.x (or any previous version) and is likely to be outdated as more of the Io namespace is reworked.
Not long ago, I wrote a blog post which tried to explain
Zig's Writers
. At best, I'd describe the current state as "confusing" with two writer interfaces while often dealing with
anytype
. And while
anytype
is convenient, it lacks developer ergonomics. Furthermore, the current design has significant performance issues for some common cases.
Drain
The new
Writer
interface is
std.Io.Writer
. At a minimum, implementations have to provide a
drain
function. Its signature looks like:
fn
drain
(
w
:
*
Writer
,
data
:
[
]
const
[
]
const
u8
,
splat
:
usize
)
Error
!
usize
You might be surprised that this is the method a custom writer needs to implemented. Not only does it take an array of strings, but what's that
splat
parameter? Like me, you might have expected a simpler
write
method:
fn
write
(
w
:
*
Writer
,
data
:
[
]
const
u8
)
Error
!
usize
It turns out that
std.Io.Writer
has buffering built-in. For example, if we want a
Writer
for an
std.fs.File
, we need to provide the buffer:
var
buffer
:
[
1024
]
u8
=
undefined
;
var
writer
=
my_file
.
writer
(
&
buffer
)
;
Of course, if we don't want buffering, we can always pass an empty buffer:
var
writer
=
my_file
.
writer
(
&
.
{
}
)
;
This explains why custom writers need to implement a
drain
method, and not something simpler like
write
.
The simplest way to implement
drain
, and what a lot of the Zig standard library has been upgraded to while this larger overhaul takes place, is:
fn
drain
(
io_w
:
*
Writer
,
data
:
[
]
const
[
]
const
u8
,
splat
:
usize
)
!
usize
{
_
=
splat
;
const
self
:
*
@This
(
)
=
@fieldParentPtr
(
"interface"
,
io_w
)
;
return
self
.
writeAll
(
data
[
0
]
)
catch
return
error
.
WriteFailed
;
}
We ignore the
splat
parameter, and just write the first value in
data
(
data.len > 0
is guaranteed to be true). This turns
drain
into what a simpler
write
method would look like. Because we return the length of bytes written,
std.Io.Writer
will know that we potentially didn't write all the data and call
drain
again, if necessary, with the rest of the data.
If you're confused by the call to
@fieldParentPtr
, check out my post on the
upcoming linked list changes
.
The actual implementation of
drain
for the
File
is a non-trivial ~150 lines of code. It has platform-specific code and leverages
vectored I/O
where possible. There's obviously flexibility to provide a simple implementation or a more optimized one.
The Interface
Much like the current state, when you do
file.writer(&buffer)
, you don't get an
std.Io.Writer
. Instead, you get a
File.Writer
. To get an actual
std.Io.Writer
, you need to access the
interface
field. This is merely a convention, but expect it to be used throughout the standard, and third-party, library. Get ready to see a lot of
&xyz.interface
calls!
This simplification of
File
shows the relationship between the three types:
pub
const
File
=
struct
{
pub
fn
writer
(
self
:
*
File
,
buffer
:
[
]
u8
)
Writer
{
return
.
{
.
file
=
self
,
.
interface
=
std
.
Io
.
Writer
{
.
buffer
=
buffer
,
.
vtable
=
.
{
.
drain
=
Writer
.
drain
}
,
}
}
;
}
pub
const
Writer
=
struct
{
file
:
*
File
,
interface
:
std
.
Io
.
Writer
,
// this has a bunch of other fields
fn
drain
(
io_w
:
*
Writer
,
data
:
[
]
const
[
]
const
u8
,
splat
:
usize
)
!
usize
{
const
self
:
*
Writer
=
@fieldParentPtr
(
"interface"
,
io_w
)
;
// ....
}
}
}
The instance of
File.Writer
needs to exist somewhere (e.g. on the stack) since that's where the
std.Io.Writer
interface exists. It's possible that
File
could directly have an
writer_interface: std.Io.Writer
field, but that would limit you to one writer per file and would bloat the
File
structure.
We can see from the above that, while we call
Writer
an "interface", it's just a normal struct. It has a few fields beyond
buffer
and
vtable.drain
, but these are the only two with non-default values; we have to provide them. The
Writer
interface implements a lot of typical "writer" behavior, such as a
writeAll
and
print
(for formatted writing). It also has a number of methods which only a
Writer
implementation would likely care about. For example,
File.Writer.drain
has to call
consume
so that the writer's internal state can be updated. Having all of these functions listed side-by-side in the documentation confused me at first. Hopefully it's something the documentation generation will one day be able to help disentangle.
Migrating
The new
Writer
has taken over a number of methods. For example,
std.fmt.formatIntBuf
no longer exists. The replacement is the
printInt
method of

data.title: Behind the ballistics of the 'explosive' squirting cucumber
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 新研究探讨了喷瓜（Ecballium elaterium）的爆炸性种子传播机制。这种植物通过高压爆炸将种子以高速喷射至远处，以减少亲子植物间的资源竞争。德国基尔大学的研究团队使用显微CT扫描和高速摄像技术详细记录了喷瓜果实爆炸的过程，发现种子速度可达29英里/小时，喷射距离可达12米。果实茎在成熟时会竖直，形成约53°的角度，接近理论上最大化喷射距离的理想角度。此外，种子外有粘液 coat，遇湿变粘，有助于种子发芽。该研究对生物启发发射系统、药物输送和软体机器人等领域有潜在应用价值，并在2025年7月8日的实验生物学学会年会上展示。

July 8, 2025
The GIST
Behind the ballistics of the 'explosive' squirting cucumber
by
Society for Experimental Biology
edited by
Gaby Clark
, 																								reviewed by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
proofread
Squirting cucumber (Ecballium elaterium). Credit: Helen Gorges
New research into the biomechanics of explosive seed dispersal in squirting cucumbers (Ecballium elaterium) reveals how these plants have adapted a suite of unique traits that help propel their high-speed seeds far and wide.
Seed dispersal comes in many forms, and much is known about animal, wind and water-assisted dispersal—but less is known about the self-propelled dispersal mechanisms of plants. One of these is the ballistic dispersal of the squirting cucumber, which uses high-pressure explosions to eject its seeds at high speed across large distances.
"Many factors have to interact perfectly to disperse the seeds in the most efficient way, while not destroying the whole plant too early," says Helen Gorges, a Ph.D. student at the Department of Functional Morphology and Biomechanics in the Zoological Institute of Kiel University, Germany.
To reduce direct competition for space and resources between parent and offspring plants, there is an evolutionary drive for plants to disperse their seeds as far as they possibly can. The research conducted by Gorges aimed to explore the mechanisms that control the cucumber's fruit during ripening and maximize its chances of successfully dispersing.
Gorges and her team used microcomputed tomography to create a 3D-model of the whole fruit, as well as micro-CT imaging and high-speed videography to capture the exploding fruit in fine detail.
Squirting cucumber explosive seed dispersal (over 300x slowed down). Credit: Helen Gorges
"We recorded the explosion of the fruit with high-speed videos at 1,000 fps and 10,000 fps to calculate the speed of the seeds and the possible shooting distances," says Gorges. "We also analyzed pictures during the ripening of the fruits to measure the curvature of the fruit stem and the angle between fruit and stem."
Gorges and her team found that the seeds can achieve speeds up to 29 miles per hour and reach shooting distances up to 12 meters. "It's super interesting to watch the explosions through high-speed recordings, as the explosions happen way too fast to see anything in real-time," says Gorges.
The experiments also revealed that the fruit stem straightens up during ripening, creating an average 53° angle that is close to the theoretical perfect angle of 50° that would maximize shooting distance.
Additionally, the team found that the seeds always exit the
fruit
facing the same way and produce a mucilaginous coat when they get wet, which becomes an adhesive when it dries and improves conditions for germination.
Squirting cucumber explosive seed dispersal in real time and slowed down. Credit: Helen Gorges
These findings have potential applications for bio-inspired launching systems as hydrogel-based actuators for medical tools and micro-robots. "There are also many applications in soft robotics,
drug delivery systems
and similar devices, where energy-efficient launching systems are desired," says Gorges.
This research is being presented at the
Society for Experimental Biology Annual Conference
in Antwerp, Belgium on the 8th July 2025.
